a_rows_sample.anchor: ActionDisposition ├── ACT ├── REFRAIN ├── DEFER ├── ESCALATE ├── INVESTIGATE └── REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION ... Decision -> ActionDisposition. ActionDisposition=ACT ⇒ Authorization ⇒ Action. ActionDisposition=REFRAIN ⇒ NoAction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes replacing the direct Decision->Action edge with Decision->ActionDisposition in {ACT,REFRAIN,DEFER,ESCALATE,INVESTIGATE,REQUEST_AUTHORIZATION}: ActionDisposition=ACT proceeds through Authorization to Action; ActionDisposition=REFRAIN yields NoAction. Argues a responsible agent must be able to output DO NOT ACT when evidence is insufficient, authorization is absent, the requirement is ambiguous, conflicting claims exist, or the action is outside scope -- framed as often the correct outcome, not agent failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionDeferred. The meaning is: No operational decision has yet been authorized. This is not failure. ... DecisionEscalated. ... Escalation ≠ Failure. ... DecisionDispositionSetToRefrain. This represents a deliberate decision not to act. ... Input → Determine → DoNothing. The 'do nothing' outcome must be intentional and auditable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Elaborates the ActionDisposition branch events at the domain-event level: DecisionDeferred means no operational decision has yet been authorized (not failure); DecisionEscalated means authority was insufficient or the case needs higher governance (Escalation != Failure); DecisionDispositionSetToRefrain represents a deliberate, intentional and auditable decision not to act (KnowledgeOS should support Input -> Determine -> DoNothing as a valid outcome, unlike conventional workflows that implicitly assume Input -> Action).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ActionExecution \neq AgencyAttribution
b_rows_sample.statement: Verse 27's doer/agency discussion (explicitly not encoded as a universal engineering fact) reveals ActionExecution ≠ AgencyAttribution, requiring separation of Action, Actor, Execution, Cause, Responsibility, AgencyAttribution. Action is reformalized from (Actor,Operation,Result) to Action=(Actor,Operation,Purpose,Authority,Context,Execution,Outcome,Attribution), distinguishing who performed vs authorized vs caused vs is responsible for an action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservableAction \neq SemanticAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 3's contrast of attachment-to-results vs action-without-attachment shows the same observable action can carry different semantic status depending on orientation: ObservableAction ≠ SemanticAction, ActionMeaning=f(Operation,Actor,Intention,Purpose,Norm,Context). Adds Intention ≠ Purpose (example: Purpose=fulfil duty vs Intention=obtain personal gain, same Action=perform operation X), giving Action=(Operation,Actor,Intention,Purpose,Context). Also adds ExemplaryBehavior/NormPropagation (Actor_A --Example--> Actor_B, verse 21) as a 'Governance/Normative Influence' bounded context, and OptimalGuidance ≠ MaximumInformation (verse 26: do not disturb the learner), giving Guidance=f(CurrentUnderstanding,Capability,Readiness,Purpose,Risk) and introducing LearningReady(K,U,Actor) / Readiness(Actor,Knowledge,Context) distinct from DecisionReady.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge does not determine Action by itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two new constitutional invariants: 'Knowledge does not determine Action by itself' formalized as Action=f(Knowledge,Understanding,Norms,Role,Purpose,Intention,Authority,Context,Decision); and 'Action does not prove Understanding' — someone may execute an instruction without understanding it, and Understanding ⇏ Action because authority/role/constraints/decision criteria may intervene, giving the non-implication chain Knowledge ⇏ Understanding ⇏ Decision ⇏ Action, each transition requiring its own semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Goal \neq Duty \neq Intention
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the generic 'Purpose' field as too coarse: Goal (what is ultimately sought) ≠ Duty (what is prescribed) ≠ Intention (why the actor acts) ≠ Result ≠ Orientation, all distinct. Revises the Action tuple to A=(Actor,Role,Operation,Duty,Intention,Orientation,Context,Outcome), noting not every field must always be populated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same external action \not\Rightarrow same semantic action
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the strongest mathematical insight of the chapter (verses 25-26): the learned and ignorant may perform outwardly similar actions with different orientation, giving ObservedAction ≠ MeaningfulAction ≠ ActionIntent, and ActionIdentity ≠ ActionObservation, illustrated by two engineers both running deploy() with identical observable events but different authorization/intent (authorized correct change vs unauthorized personal shortcut) — 'the operational event may look identical, the semantic event is not'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ApplicableNorms + ActorRole + Context + Understanding \rightarrow CandidateActions
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Chapter 3 supplies something more interesting than 'decision readiness': Arjuna's question is 'given my situation, what course of action should I follow?', requiring ApplicableNorms+ActorRole+Context+Understanding -> CandidateActions -> Decision, judged a better formulation than simply introducing 'DecisionGap' (which is later demoted, see below).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Instruction \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Test Case 9 (a constitutional rule 'all production software must have an approved ADR') shows the pipeline must produce a NormativeProposition distinct in semantic type from a FactualProposition, exposing that a single undifferentiated Proposition model cannot serve both. Test Case 10 (a human instruction 'upgrade Nexus to 3.70') shows an instruction must NOT become Assertion:Nexus.version=3.70 directly — it produces Instruction:Upgrade(Nexus,3.70), which may later produce an Action, which may produce a new Observation, which may then produce an Assertion. This establishes two fundamentally different flows: Epistemic acquisition (Input->Observation->Interpretation->Assertion) and Action/effect (Instruction->Action->Observation->Knowledge) — flagged as important for later defining Sārathi.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['action', 'model'])

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now change mode. The first 100 steps established the architectural theory and closure. Step 101 begins the empirical phase: Intended Architecture -> Implemented Architecture -> Running Architecture. The central question is no longer 'is this architecture conceptually sound' but 'does our actual K
a_rows_sample.statement: Announces Step 101's mode shift from architectural theory (Steps 1-100) to the empirical conformance question: does the actual system implement the defined architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.1 — Three architectures ... A. Intended architecture A_I. B. Implemented architecture A_C. C. Runtime architecture A_R(t). A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the three-architectures distinction: A_I (intended, per docs/ADRs/principles/governance), A_C (implemented, per actual repositories/config/code), A_R(t) (runtime, actually deployed/behaving), and the conformance question A_I =? A_C =? A_R(t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.2 — Why this matters ... a common architecture failure looks like A_I≠A_C while everybody assumes A_I=A_C. An even more dangerous situation: A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R. The documentation is correct. The code is correct. The deployment is not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns of two failure patterns: assuming A_I=A_C when A_I≠A_C, and the more dangerous A_I=A_C but A_C≠A_R (correct docs, correct code, incorrect deployment).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.3 — Experiment 1: documented component missing ... Architecture declares EvidenceService. Repository contains no implementation. Expected classification: SpecifiedButMissing. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a declared-but-unimplemented EvidenceService is classified SpecifiedButMissing; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.4 — Experiment 2: undocumented component exists ... Repository contains LegacyKnowledgeImporter. Architecture does not mention it. Expected: ImplementedButUndocumented. This is architecture drift. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an undocumented existing component (LegacyKnowledgeImporter) is ImplementedButUndocumented — architecture drift; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.5 — Experiment 3: wrong implementation ... Architecture requires PolicyEngine to enforce AuthorizationInvariant. Code contains a policy engine, but authorization is bypassable. Expected: ImplementedIncorrectly. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a policy engine that exists but leaves authorization bypassable is ImplementedIncorrectly; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.6 — Experiment 4: partially implemented concept ... Architecture defines Evidence with provenance, source, timestamp, confidence, classification. Implementation contains only source. Expected: PartiallyImplemented. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: an Evidence implementation retaining only 'source' of five required fields is PartiallyImplemented; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.7 — Five-state conformance vocabulary ... Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified. Much more useful than simply saying 'the architecture is implemented.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the five-state conformance vocabulary (Implemented, PartiallyImplemented, SpecifiedButMissing, ImplementedIncorrectly, NotYetVerified), far more useful than a bare 'implemented' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.8 — But we need evidence ... Every classification should have Evidence. ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConformanceFinding=(Requirement,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Status), requiring every conformance classification to carry supporting evidence.

type_signature.domain: Requirement x Expected x Observed x Evidence

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.9 — Experiment 5 ... Reviewer says 'the evidence model is implemented.' No repository location, code reference, schema or test is provided. Expected: NotYetVerified. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: an unsupported reviewer claim (no repo location/code reference/schema/test) must be classified NotYetVerified; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.10 — Architecture claims become evidence-backed claims ... 'Evidence service exists' becomes Claim: EvidenceCapabilityImplemented supported by RepositoryEvidence+SchemaEvidence+TestEvidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes architecture claims as evidence-backed claims (RepositoryEvidence+SchemaEvidence+TestEvidence) rather than bare assertions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.11 — Architecture requirement traceability ... Requirement→ArchitectureRule→Component→Code→Test→RuntimeEvidence. This becomes our central conformance chain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the central conformance chain Requirement→ArchitectureRule→Component→Code→Test→RuntimeEvidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.12 — Experiment 6 ... Requirement exists. Architecture rule exists. Implementation exists. No test exists. Expected: ImplementedButUnverified. Not Assured. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an implemented but untested capability is ImplementedButUnverified, not Assured; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.13 — Conformance is multidimensional ... A component can be Implemented=True but Verified=False. Similarly Implemented=True but GovernanceCompliant=False. Therefore a single status is insufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a single conformance status is insufficient: Implemented=True can coexist with Verified=False or GovernanceCompliant=False.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.14 — Conformance vector ... C(x)=(Implementation,Semantic,Security,Privacy,Governance,Verification,Runtime). Each dimension may have its own status.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-dimension conformance vector C(x)=(Implementation,Semantic,Security,Privacy,Governance,Verification,Runtime), each with independent status.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.15 — Experiment 7 ... Component AgentRegistry. Implementation=PASS, Semantic=PASS, Security=PASS, Privacy=UNKNOWN, Runtime=UNKNOWN. Expected: overall result cannot simply be 100% Correct. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: mixed per-dimension statuses (some PASS, some UNKNOWN) for AgentRegistry mean the overall result cannot simply be 100% Correct; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.16 — This changes how we evaluate KnowledgeOS ... We should not produce one simplistic score such as Architecture=87%. Instead, we need a conformance matrix.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects single-score architecture evaluation (e.g. Architecture=87%) in favor of a conformance matrix.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.17 — Architecture Conformance Matrix ... Knowledge registry, Evidence model, Provenance, Governance, Agent control, Policy enforcement, AI context boundary, Runtime assurance, Evolution control -- each with Specification/Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Status columns, many marked TBD/?. The
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a sample Architecture Conformance Matrix (nine capabilities x Specification/Implementation/Verification/Runtime/Status), with unresolved '?' cells explicitly framed as an acceptable engineering state ('we don't know yet').

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.18 — Architecture archaeology ... examine Repositories, DirectoryStructure, SourceCode, Configuration, DatabaseSchemas, CI/CD, AgentHarnesses, Hooks, RuntimeArtifacts, Documentation. Then reconstruct A_C.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines 'architecture archaeology': reconstructing A_C from repositories, directory structure, source code, config, schemas, CI/CD, agent harnesses, hooks, runtime artifacts, documentation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 101.19 — The repository becomes architectural evidence ... a domain/application/infrastructure/governance/agents/evidence/verification folder structure suggests one architecture; controllers/services/utils/misc suggests something very different. But naming alone is not proof.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes directory structure suggests architectural intent but naming alone is not proof of actual conformance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the correct next phase is therefore NOT EP-01 ... EP-01 assumes that the target domain/context architecture is sufficiently informed. It isn't.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly stops the previously proposed EP-01 bounded-context-and-aggregate-validation phase, on the grounds that EKS/PKS/AIP current architecture must first be independently reconstructed and a convergence analysis run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Map A — EKS current architecture ... Map B — PKS current architecture ... Map C — KnowledgeOS proposed architecture ... Map D — Convergence matrix.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a four-map convergence method as the next investigation's required output, with a worked example convergence matrix scoring candidate kernel capabilities (Evidence, Provenance, Governance, Lifecycle, ChangeSet, Verification) across EKS/PKS/proposed-KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P2 detects shared LEXICAL terms. P2 does NOT establish semantic equivalence. That is P3. Lexical similarity is evidence for investigation, not evidence of bounded-context equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an overly strict draft rule ('NO EKS↔PKS comparison') that risked suppressing shared-vocabulary detection the study's own mandate #7 requires, replacing it with a clean split: detect shared terms now, defer semantic-equivalence judgement to Stage 4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the PKS current-state classification is not performed here — that is the P2 session's output ... no implementation search under app/, resources/, tests/, routes/, or database/ found for PKS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Anticipates from a preliminary repository search that PKS's A–G classification will be dominated by G/UNKNOWN because no implementation is found under the usual code roots, so the corpus must be expanded beyond the plan's minimum list with every admission/exclusion recorded as a finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1 — REJECTED by the Human Principal Architect: a single session combining plan-P3 (AIP) + plan-P4 (Landscape) with two commits ... an unreviewed AIP interpretation consumed by the same session's landscape would create a self-confirming architecture interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records that the Human Principal Architect explicitly rejected a v1 launch-prompt draft that would have let one session both reconstruct AIP and immediately build the EKS-PKS-AIP landscape on its own unreviewed output, on self-confirmation-risk grounds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Corpus-boundary rule (P2 precedent): §5.3 is the governed starting corpus, not necessarily exhaustive. Any additional AIP evidence admitted is admitted by role, with a recorded finding.
b_rows_sample.statement: Carries forward the P2 discipline that corpus-boundary decisions must be recorded as findings, not silent choices, into the P3 AIP launch prompt.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'architecture-conformance-engineering-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'ep01-eks-pks-aip-landscape-study' (batch B0024). Note: Step 101: pivots from architectural theory to empirical conformance measurement. Three-architectures distinction (intended/implemented/runtime), five-state conformance vocabulary with mandatory evidence, multidimensional conformance vectors (rejecting single-score evaluation), architecture archaeology and dependency-graph drift detection, a bidirectional requirement<->runtime evidence graph, the Traceability!=Correctness distinction, mismatch-diagnosis discipline (implementation-wrong vs architecture-obsolete vs both-incomplete) forbidding documentation laundering, bounded recursive self-analysis, and a queryable machine-readable self-architecture-model. Conceptual forerunner of the actual EP-01 EKS+PKS+AIP landscape study.

b_rows_sample.anchor: When several pieces of evidence support the same proposition, how should KnowledgeOS combine them? We must avoid the very tempting but incorrect rule: more sources \Rightarrow more certainty. That is only true under specific assumptions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25C.2's question, warning against the tempting-but-incorrect rule 'more sources ⇒ more certainty', true only under specific assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Start with a controlled proposition ... H="Rollback will succeed if executed." P(H)=0.5. This is an experimental prior, not a KnowledgeOS principle. ... Evidence E_1 ... P(E_1\mid H)=0.95 and P(E_1\mid\neg H)=0.10. LR_1=9.5. O(H)=1. O(H\mid E_1)=9.5. P(H\mid E_1)\approx90.5\% under this specific sta
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a fully numerical Bayesian likelihood-ratio calculation (LR1=9.5) yielding P(H|E1)≈90.5% under an explicit experimental prior, explicitly not a KnowledgeOS principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Important observation ... We have not said "KnowledgeOS now knows rollback will succeed." We have established P(H\mid E_1)\approx0.905 under the assumptions of the model. That is statistical inference, not epistemic truth. Probability\neq KnowledgeState. This confirms the layered architecture from 2
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms via the numerical example that Probability≠KnowledgeState — a computed posterior is statistical inference under model assumptions, not epistemic truth, validating the layered architecture from 25C.1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add genuinely independent evidence ... E_2 is an independently performed restore test. P(E_2\mid H)=0.90 and P(E_2\mid\neg H)=0.20. LR_2=4.5. Under the conditional-independence assumption LR_{12}=LR_1LR_2=42.75. P(H\mid E_1,E_2)\approx97.7\%. This demonstrates the legitimate case where independent e
b_rows_sample.statement: Computes the legitimate independent-evidence-combination case: LR12=LR1·LR2=42.75 yielding P(H|E1,E2)≈97.7%, demonstrating substantial legitimate confidence increase under genuine independence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now attack the independence assumption ... E_2 is simply a report generated from E_1. E_2=f(E_1). If we nevertheless calculate LR_{12}=LR_1LR_2, we manufacture certainty. This is mathematically wrong. IndependentEvidence must be established, not assumed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows that applying LR1·LR2 to a copied (E2=f(E1)) evidence pair manufactures false certainty mathematically — IndependentEvidence must be established, not assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Perfect duplicate experiment ... E_2=E_1. Then P(H\mid E_1,E_2)=P(H\mid E_1). There should be no additional information. Aggregate(E,E)=Aggregate(E) for duplicate evidence. This confirms the idempotency requirement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Numerically confirms the idempotency requirement: a perfect duplicate provides zero additional posterior shift.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A surprising consequence ... the real input to inference is not \{E_1,E_2,\ldots,E_n\}. It is closer to Evidence Graph where we know relationships such as E_1\perp E_2 or E_2=f(E_1). This is not an implementation detail. It changes the mathematics of aggregation. ... Three cases ... Case A duplicate
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the true input to inference is the Evidence Graph (relationships, not a bare set), classifying three information-gain cases (duplicate=0, dependent=less than naive, independent=>0) as the beginning of an evidence-combination theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — contradictory evidence ... E_3: Rollback test failed. P(E_3\mid H)=0.05 and P(E_3\mid\neg H)=0.80. LR_3=0.0625. 42.75\times0.0625=2.671875. P(H\mid E_1,E_2,E_3)\approx0.728. So the statistical model says approximately 72.8\%. ... But KnowledgeOS must not say merely "72.8%" ... Support=\
b_rows_sample.statement: Computes contradictory-evidence-adjusted posterior P(H|E1,E2,E3)≈72.8% while requiring the epistemic Support/Challenge structure be retained alongside the scalar — the critical result that the statistical result and qualitative epistemic state must coexist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The statistical result and epistemic state coexist ... EpistemicAssessment + StatisticalInference. Proposition: Rollback will succeed. Evidence: E1 supports, E2 supports, E3 challenges. Conflict: true. Statistical model: P(H|E) = 0.728. Inference model: Bayesian. Dependency assumptions: E1 ⟂ E2. Thi
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a worked full record combining EpistemicAssessment and StatisticalInference (evidence roles, conflict flag, model, dependency assumptions), far richer than a bare confidence percentage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — source reliability ... E_3 comes from an uncalibrated test. We should not simply discard it. Instead its statistical model should represent P(E_3\mid H) and P(E_3\mid\neg H) appropriately. Reliability belongs in the model, not as an arbitrary score.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that source reliability belongs inside the statistical likelihood model (P(E|H), P(E|¬H)) rather than as an arbitrary bolt-on score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — one very strong evidence item versus many weak ones ... E_1 is a direct successful restore test. Then ten weak human statements. Naive counting says 10>1. KnowledgeOS must not use source count. EvidenceCount\neq EvidenceStrength.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms EvidenceCount ≠ EvidenceStrength using a strong-single-test-vs-ten-weak-statements experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — common-cause dependence ... Infrastructure report, Operations report, Manager report all generated from the same monitoring dashboard. E_1,E_2,E_3 are highly correlated. There are three artifacts but approximately one underlying information source. This is exactly why lineage matters. .
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a common-cause-dependent evidence set (three reports from one dashboard, one underlying source) with a genuinely independent evidence set (three separate physical systems), showing only the latter legitimately increases support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The crucial requirement ... KnowledgeOS therefore needs to distinguish ArtifactMultiplicity from InformationMultiplicity. Three documents can represent one underlying fact. One experiment can generate several genuinely distinct observations. This is an epistemic identity problem, not merely a databa
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ArtifactMultiplicity from InformationMultiplicity as an epistemic identity problem, not merely database deduplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — evidence arriving sequentially ... After E_1: P(H)=0.905. After E_2: P(H)=0.977. After contradictory E_3: P(H)=0.728. This demonstrates Knowledge/evidence evolution can be non-monotonic. The numerical inference can increase and decrease as evidence arrives. ... But the evidence history
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces the full sequential posterior evolution (0.5→0.905→0.977→0.728), confirming non-monotonic inference alongside cumulative evidence history — InferenceState is revisable, EvidenceHistory is cumulative, matching 25A.3's earlier result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — retraction ... E_3 is later determined to be invalid. We do not erase the historical fact that at t_3, KnowledgeOS received E_3. Instead Status(E_3)=Invalid. Then recompute P(H\mid E_1,E_2,E_3^{invalid}). The inference can return toward 97.7%. But the history records why the inference c
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a retraction experiment where E3 is invalidated (not erased), triggering a recomputed posterior returning toward 97.7% while the history records why.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This produces an important invariant ... I_{t+1}=Infer(K_{t+1},M). If evidence is retracted K_{t+1}=Revision(K_t,E^{invalid}). Then I_{t+1} must be recalculated. Inference is a projection of KnowledgeState, not the KnowledgeState itself. This is an important architectural principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the invariant Inference is a projection of KnowledgeState, not the KnowledgeState itself — requiring recalculation whenever the underlying KnowledgeState is revised (e.g. via retraction).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This changes how we should model probabilities ... We should not store only P(H)=0.728. We should store InferenceResult=(H,Probability,Model,ModelVersion,InputKnowledgeSnapshot,Assumptions). Hypothesis: H, Probability: 0.728, Model: Bayesian, ModelVersion: 1.2, KnowledgeSnapshot: K17, Assumptions: E
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a full reproducible InferenceResult=(H,Probability,Model,ModelVersion,InputKnowledgeSnapshot,Assumptions) record instead of storing a bare probability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is extremely important for KnowledgeOS ... Why did KnowledgeOS say rollback had a 72.8% probability? We should be able to answer Because K_{17} + Model_{1.2} + Assumptions_{X} \Rightarrow0.728. This is much stronger than "The AI estimated 72.8%."
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the InferenceResult record enables answering 'why did KnowledgeOS say 72.8%?' with a precise reconstruction (snapshot+model+assumptions), far stronger than 'the AI estimated it'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now have a candidate inference contract ... Inference(K,H,M,C) \rightarrow R where K = knowledge snapshot; H = hypothesis; M = mathematical model; C = assumptions/context; R = inference result. This is a clean DDD/application boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the inference contract Inference(K,H,M,C)→R as a clean DDD/application boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What should happen if the model is inappropriate? ... Architecture Board approval is mandatory. Trying to calculate P(ApprovalRequired) is usually the wrong operation. The appropriate reasoning may be RuleEvaluation(K,Policy) \rightarrow Required. NotEveryPropositionRequiresStatisticalInference. Thi
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues NotEveryPropositionRequiresStatisticalInference (a normative approval requirement should use RuleEvaluation, not probability), reinforcing the rejection of a universal Bayesian kernel, and defines four reasoning modes (Deductive/Normative, Statistical, Causal, Semantic/Fuzzy).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'A1..A10'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evolution <-> KM update; Correction/Refutation <-> AGM revision. This is a genuine result and the corpus does not know it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds RevisionType::Evolution (the corpus's 'the system really changed from 3.69 to 3.70', boxed 'Evolution is not an error') is exactly Katsuno-Mendelzon's motivating case for UPDATE (the world changed, the old belief was correct then), while Correction/Refutation match AGM REVISION (new information about a static world); notes AGM is mentioned only 5 times across 564 corpus files and the KM revision/update distinction appears nowhere, so the corpus independently re-derived, from a version-number example, a distinction belief-revision literature has held since 1991 -- and split it six ways where KM splits two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The credibility set C is exactly Policy x Authority. ... C gates input acceptance; Policy+Authority gate admission; both leave the prior state unchanged on rejection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus's governed admission (Closure-03: LLM proposes, Lord evaluates, Governance authorizes; a proposal may be rejected) is exactly credibility-limited (non-prioritized) revision K⊛phi = K*phi if phi in C, else K, with the credibility set C identified structure-preservingly as Policy x Authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H monotone AND K'=Derive(H') non-monotone === JTMS
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus's boxed Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation (H'=H union {E_revision}, K'=Derive(H',Omega,EC,M)) is exactly a Doyle-style JTMS: the corpus's own Fagin extraction already states 'knowledge history is monotonic in preservation; knowledge state is not necessarily monotonic in projection', which is the JTMS invariant verbatim (justification store grows monotonically, derived belief set is non-monotone).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AGM does not apply to A as stated. Hansson's base revision does. ... importing AGM results would import theorems that are false of A.
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural incompatibility: AGM's carrier K=Cn(K) is deductively closed, but the corpus's assertion set A (measured: zero occurrences of a consequence operator Cn) is a finite set of asserted items with identity/provenance/evidence links, i.e. a Hansson belief BASE, not a belief SET; since base contraction and AGM contraction on Cn(B) are provably inequivalent, naively importing AGM theorems would import claims false of A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two of the corpus's six revision types are changes to the interpretation function, which AGM cannot express. ... This is the largest single gap found in this document, and it runs against the external theory rather than against KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive finding: AGM holds the language L and its interpretation fixed -- every operator maps L-sentences to L-sentences, with no operator for changing what sentences MEAN -- but the corpus's Reinterpretation ('the original observation was valid, but we interpreted it incorrectly', a change in Evidence(O,P,C,R)'s rule R) and ModelRevision ('reasonable under the old model, but the model itself was subsequently changed', a change in M within Derive(H,Omega,EC,M)) are both first-class corpus revision types with no AGM counterpart at all; framed as the corpus formalizing something AGM chose to hold constant, i.e. the gap runs against the external theory, not against KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma cong {0,1}^2 is a product, not an order. Supported (1,0) and Refuted (0,1) are incomparable ... Sigma cannot be an entrenchment ordering.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refutes mapping Sigma onto an AGM entrenchment ordering: AGM entrenchment <= is a total, transitive preorder satisfying dominance and minimality, but the corpus's Sigma (isomorphic to {0,1}^2, the Supported/Refuted product) is a product structure, not an order -- Supported(1,0) and Refuted(0,1) are incomparable, neither more entrenched than the other. Offers, only as a stated-not-adopted hypothesis (BR-H4), a lattice ordering (0,0)<={(1,0),(0,1)}<=(1,1) under set inclusion on the support set, explicitly noting this would order informativeness, not resistance-to-retraction, and the corpus asserts no such order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retraction — "the source withdraws its support" — is not expressible in AGM, because AGM beliefs have no sources.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes AGM models a single agent's single belief set at one time with no source identifiers, while KnowledgeOS carries provenance, multiple sources, authority and an inquiry register; consequently RevisionType::Retraction (a source withdrawing its support) cannot be expressed in AGM at all and requires base revision augmented with justifications (i.e. JTMS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: interpretation change | sources/provenance on beliefs | an authority predicate | a requirement set | a goal state | paraconsistent tolerance ... a consequence operator Cn | an entrenchment/plausibility order | a contraction operator
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists missing primitives on the belief-revision side needed to host KnowledgeOS (interpretation change for Reinterpretation/ModelRevision; sources/provenance on beliefs for Retraction; an authority predicate for governed admission; a requirement set for Zero; a goal state for Ideal State; paraconsistent tolerance for Conflict, since AGM's K*5 Consistency postulate forbids it) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host belief revision (a consequence operator Cn, currently 0 occurrences, without which 'belief set' is undefined; an entrenchment/plausibility order, since nothing currently orders assertions by retractability; a contraction operator, since Retraction is named as a RevisionType but not defined as an operator, and its membership in the operator-registry O_core is unratified).

a_rows_sample.anchor: BR-H1 ... BR-H2 ... BR-H3 ... BR-H4 ... BR-H5 ... BR-H6
a_rows_sample.statement: States six falsifiable hypotheses with named falsifiers: BR-H1 (Evolution<->KM-update and Correction/Refutation<->AGM-revision is exact in role); BR-H2 (governed admission satisfies credibility-limited-revision postulates with C=Policy x Authority, falsified by a rejected proposal that still changes A); BR-H3 (Revision=EventAddition+StateReDerivation satisfies the JTMS invariant, falsified by a RevisionType that removes an event from H); BR-H4 (Sigma admits no total entrenchment order consistent with corpus operations); BR-H5 (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision are not definable as any AGM/KM operator composition over a fixed L); BR-H6 (because Cn is absent, no AGM theorem transfers to A unmodified, falsified by exhibiting one that holds of A for a non-trivial reason).

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE CLOSEST OF THE FIVE — and the corpus is ahead of the framework on one axis ... the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: belief revision is 'the closest of the five' external theories compared in this series, with four exact correspondences (more than any other), a resolvable carrier mismatch (move from AGM to base revision), and one axis (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision) where KnowledgeOS is ahead of the external framework rather than under-formalized; endorses and sharpens the corpus's own Gardenfors-derived self-description ('epistemic states and their dynamics as the primary modelling problem', Kernel=preservation substrate) into 'the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What I would NOT implement ... AGM as KnowledgeOS revision ... Event Calculus as delta ... Description Logic as KnowledgeOS ontology ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation. Already experimentally rejected as sufficient ... Four-valued knowledge. Still insufficient ... Closed-world assumption. Explicitly rejected ... Query = Sat. Rejected ... TELL = requirement insertion. Rejected ... Model uniqueness = Determination. Not yet ... Distributed knowledge logic = KnowledgeOS social ontology. Not yet ... N_eff. Still off the critical path.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 18, an eleven-item explicit non-adoption list, each rejecting an over-strong external-theory identification even where the same Handbook material motivates the underlying distinction: AGM as the revision theory, Event Calculus as delta, Description Logic as ontology (subsumption/model-existence/instance-checking/open-world used only as research inputs), FDE as evaluation (already experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge, closed-world assumption, Query=Sat, TELL=requirement-insertion, ModelUniqueness=Determination, distributed-knowledge-logic=social-ontology, and N_eff -- all explicitly rejected or deferred as established KnowledgeOS semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 2: Knowledge Evolution and Change -- FR-5 Epistemic Change Typing [STRONG], FR-6 Non-Monotonic Evolution [STRONG], FR-8 Derivation Lineage [STRONG CANDIDATE]
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 groups FR-5, FR-6 and (unusually, ahead of the Representation part) FR-8 under Knowledge Evolution and Change: FR-5 Revision != Contraction != Update, each with a distinct signature (Revision(K_t,e), Contract(K_t,p), Update(K_t,DeltaW)); FR-6 K_t not-subseteq K_{t+1} permitted, not itself indicating failure; FR-8 Support(q)={p, p->q,...} as DerivationLineage(q), status STRONG CANDIDATE pending one validation pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 5: What Is NOT Implemented -- AGM as KnowledgeOS revision: Use distinctions only ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation: Experimentally rejected ... N_eff: Off critical path
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 5 formalizes the non-adoption list as an 11-row table (item, reason): AGM as revision (use distinctions only), Event Calculus as delta (research input only), Description Logic as ontology (research input only), FDE as evaluation (experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge (insufficient), closed-world assumption (explicitly rejected), Query=Sat (rejected), TELL=requirement-insertion (rejected), Model-uniqueness=Determination (not yet), Distributed knowledge logic (not yet), N_eff (off critical path).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two places where KnowledgeOS exceeds the external theory: Reinterpretation and ModelRevision -- AGM/KM hold the language fixed; two of the corpus's six revision types change the interpretation function. No operator exists in the framework. Determination/Decision/Action -- a three-way split where Wald has two, and the extra cut is the one governance needs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names two places where KnowledgeOS's own formalization exceeds the compared external theory rather than merely matching or falling short of it: two of the corpus's six revision types (Reinterpretation, ModelRevision) change the interpretation function itself, something AGM/KM hold fixed and have no operator to express; and the corpus's three-way Determination/Decision/Action split adds a cut beyond Wald's two-way decision-theoretic split, specifically the cut that governance needs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination ... Representation, Reasoning, Evaluation and Determination are distinct semantic functions. No result produced by one function is automatically equivalent to the result of another. Formally: Rep != Reason != Eval != Det. This should become a theory-level principle, not merely a candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central addition #1: make explicit the chain Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination as a semantic separation of distinct epistemic functions (not merely an architectural pipeline); proposes the theory-level principle Rep != Reason != Eval != Det, citing the Handbook's distinction of knowledge representation from reasoning mechanisms and from task-level knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add Explicit vs Derived Knowledge ... K_t^{exp} and K_t^{der,S} with K_t^{der,S}=Cn_S(K_t^{exp}) ... K^{exp}!=K^{der} and Derivability does not imply operational availability. Therefore K^{der,S} != K^{available,S}.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-1 (section 2): defines K_t^exp (explicit) and K_t^der,S = Cn_S(K_t^exp) (derived under reasoning system S) as distinct conceptual layers; states K^exp != K^der and that derivability does not imply operational availability, so K^der,S != K^available,S. Grounded in the Handbook's distinction between explicit beliefs and logical-closure consequences, and the problem of logical omniscience. Status: STRONG.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add the Reasoning-System parameter S ... K |-_S p ... S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B) ... We should not claim this tuple is the final KnowledgeOS definition of a ReasoningSystem ... neg Derive_S(K,p) does not entail neg p. And neg Derive_S(K,p) does not even necessarily entail neg Derivable_S(K,p). That distinction is extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-2 (section 3): derivability should be indexed by a reasoning regime, Derive_S(K,p) rather than absolute K|-p, with S conceptually = (L representation language, Sigma vocabulary/signature, R inference rules, Sem semantics, B computational/resource boundary) explicitly NOT claimed as the final KnowledgeOS ReasoningSystem definition. Important consequence: not-Derive_S(K,p) entails neither not-p nor not-Derivable_S(K,p) -- a distinction flagged as extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Query != Evaluation != Determination ... ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal ... Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination ... We must not define Sat = ASK or Sat = Truth or Determination = Truth. This should become an explicit KnowledgeOS invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-3 (section 4): promotes Query != Evaluation != Determination from research observation to theory principle, with ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult, Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal, Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination as the three distinct operations; explicitly forbids Sat=ASK, Sat=Truth, and Determination=Truth as an invariant, motivated by the Handbook's model-based-reasoning distinction between obtaining predictions, comparing to observations, and drawing conclusions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Computationally Bounded Knowledge ... Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K) ... Explicit != Derivable != Available ... This is not UNKNOWN in the same sense as absence of representation. It is a computational boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-4 (section 5): distinguishes Cn_S(K) (all consequences) from Avail_S(K,B) (what a bounded reasoning process can actually compute), with Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), giving a three-way distinction Explicit != Derivable != Available; a proposition can be derivable-but-unavailable, which is a computational-boundary phenomenon, explicitly NOT the same kind of UNKNOWN as absence of representation. Flagged as feeding the future Zero/Evaluation model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement non-monotonic knowledge evolution ... Classical accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient ... p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} ... Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic ... someone could incorrectly interpret K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse.' It may instead be Correction or Retraction or World Update.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-6 (section 7): classical monotone accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient; the theory must permit p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} (Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic), grounded in the Handbook's nonmonotonic-reasoning treatment of withdrawable conclusions. Warns explicitly against misreading K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse' -- it may instead be Correction, Retraction, or World Update.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Representation Adequacy ... pi: X -> Y ... x1 != x2 can nevertheless satisfy pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... Adequacy(pi,Q) means the projection preserves every distinction required by question Q ... Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. I would now consider this a core KnowledgeOS theory principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-7 (section 8): formalizes Representation Adequacy for a projection pi:X->Y, defining the induced equivalence x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2), and Adequacy(pi,Q) meaning pi preserves every distinction required by question Q; integrates with existing Projection work into the sequence Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. Elevated to a core KnowledgeOS theory principle, grounded in the Handbook's qualitative-representation/abstraction treatment. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE -> promote.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'failure to derive' as a typed epistemic distinction ... U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope ... We do not need to make these six values of one enum ... we should not flatten them. Instead EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) remains the better direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. Grounded in the Handbook's observation that incomplete reasoning and incomplete knowledge can have different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Revision Lineage ... if p->q and p supports q, then removing p can invalidate the derivation of q. Therefore derived content should retain a dependency structure: Support(q)={p, p->q, ...} ... This is not merely provenance ... It is derivation dependency ... DerivationLineage as a candidate theory concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-8 (section 10): if p->q and p supports q, removing p can invalidate the derivation of q; derived content should retain a dependency structure Support(q) = {p, p->q, ...}, named DerivationLineage and distinguished from ordinary provenance (it is derivation dependency, stronger than provenance-of-origin), grounded in the Handbook's belief-revision discussion. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Temporal Persistence as distinct from Knowledge ... An entity/state can persist because no terminating event has been represented, but that is not equivalent to knowing that it persists ... Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange not=> NoChange. This is important for our future delta.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-9 (section 12): persistence (an entity/state persisting because no terminating event has been represented) is distinct from knowing that it persists; states Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange does not imply NoChange, drawn from the Handbook's Event Calculus inertia/release treatment; flagged as important for the future delta definition. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement temporal qualification ... p@t or p@[t1,t2] ... Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction ... Epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction. This is especially important for our recent cross-frame contradiction work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 13: proposes temporal qualification p@t or p@[t1,t2] (instants, intervals, granularity as distinct representation choices, per the Handbook) so Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction; states the principle 'epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction', flagged as important for the corpus's cross-frame contradiction work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement distributed evidence -- but not distributed knowledge logic ... E1 union E2 union E3 may jointly support a determination even when Det(E1)=U, Det(E2)=U, Det(E3)=U ... JointEvidence != sum IndividualDeterminations ... do not import epistemic logic's D_G, common knowledge, or agent semantics into the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-11 (section 14): union of individually-undetermined evidence sources (Det(E1)=Det(E2)=Det(E3)=U) may jointly support a determination, drawn from the Handbook's distributed-knowledge treatment; proposes the weaker KnowledgeOS principle JointEvidence != sum(IndividualDeterminations) and JointSupport(E_G,p|Gamma), while explicitly forbidding import of epistemic logic's distributed-knowledge operator D_G, common knowledge, or full agent semantics into the kernel. Status: CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Task Knowledge as a separate theoretical layer ... DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism ... PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput ... otherwise KnowledgeOS risks treating every reasoning process as generic.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-10 (section 15): drawing on the Handbook's Problem-Solving Method (PSM) material as highly DDD-compatible, proposes DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism, with PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput, and a DDD interpretation chain BoundedContext -> DomainKnowledge -> Task -> PSM -> Reasoning -> Determination; motivated by the risk that KnowledgeOS otherwise treats every reasoning process as generic. Recorded as candidate theory structure, not kernel primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement model multiplicity as a determination concept ... M(K,Gamma) ... |M|=0 could indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics ... |M|=1 could indicate model-level uniqueness ... |M|>1 indicates underdetermination ... |M|=1 does not automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition ... ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-12 (section 16): defines M(K,Gamma) as the set of models compatible with current knowledge and context: |M|=0 may indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics, |M|=1 model-level uniqueness, |M|>1 underdetermination; explicit warning that |M|=1 does NOT automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition (model space and reasoning capability still matter), yielding ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination. Status: RESEARCH CANDIDATE, upgraded to 'very strong candidate'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement diagnosability as an evidence-quality property ... A useful observation/test is one that discriminates among competing hypotheses ... DiscriminativePower(e,H) ... this does not revive N_eff. Our previous negative result remains: PairwiseDistinguishability not=> FamilyComplexity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 17: proposes DiscriminativePower(e,H) as a candidate evidence-quality property (a useful observation/test discriminates among competing hypotheses, per the Handbook's model-based reasoning chapter), explicitly noting this does NOT revive the previously-rejected N_eff metric, and reaffirms the standing negative result PairwiseDistinguishability does not imply FamilyComplexity; final principle: evidence can be evaluated by the distinctions it preserves among admissible hypotheses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The resulting KnowledgeOS theory structure ... Truth/World State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation (Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning S -> Evaluation Eval_c -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation' ... Orthogonal dimensions: Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary ... And state change: K_t -> Revision / Contraction / World Update / New Observation / New Reasoning Capability -> K_t+1
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 19 assembles the whole review into one restructured theory diagram: a linear pipeline Truth/World-State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation(Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning-S -> Evaluation(Eval_c) -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation', six orthogonal dimensions (Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary), and a five-way state-change fan-out from K_t (Revision, Contraction, World Update, New Observation, New Reasoning Capability) into K_t+1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If I reduce the entire book to the minimum theory contribution, I would make this the new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: Evidence is not directly Knowledge. More formally: E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det, with Truth, Context, Time, Provenance, Authority remaining orthogonal dimensions. And knowledge evolution is not one operation: Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 21, the review's single most-reduced claim, proposed as a new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: 'Evidence is not directly Knowledge', formalized as the chain E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det with Truth/Context/Time/Provenance/Authority as orthogonal dimensions, and knowledge evolution decomposed as Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning; judged to be what can actually be implemented into the theory now without violating existing epistemic discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not call this Theory v1.3 yet. Instead create a controlled research artifact: KR-HR -- KnowledgeOS Theory Integration from Handbook of Knowledge Representation ... FR-1-FR-7: eligible for theory promotion after corpus reconciliation ... FR-8-FR-10: strong candidates requiring one additional validation pass ... FR-11-FR-12: research candidates ... Contr / Zero / Sat / Equality / delta: remain open ... Kernel selection: unchanged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommended status/governance discipline: explicitly declines to name this Theory v1.3, instead proposing the bounded research artifact KR-HR with graded eligibility (FR-1..FR-7 eligible for promotion after corpus reconciliation; FR-8..FR-10 strong candidates needing one more validation pass; FR-11..FR-12 research candidates), while Contr/Zero/Sat/Equality/delta remain open and kernel selection stays unchanged -- preserving the archaeology -> evidence -> determination -> ratification discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Commission Edition 2 as a HYBRID full-depth technical book (form D, sec3)... Scope decision recommended: OPTION A -- commission Parts III->II->IV now (sources already deep), run the kernel full-read research as a parallel commissioned track, and gate Part I's expansion on its completion
a_rows_sample.statement: The plan's executive recommendation: commission Edition 2 as a HYBRID full-depth technical book (form D -- monograph structure with mandatory research-status marking, rejecting pure-monograph form A, engineering-reference form B, and pure-research form C), built atop the frozen/accepted Edition 1 (its 25 essays become chapter abstracts); scope Option A -- commission Parts III/II/IV now (sources already deep) while kernel full-read research runs as a parallel commissioned track gating Part I.3's expansion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What it merely names (DEPTH sec6-7): M49, BC_Governance, the 8 K_t primitives, the 4 Zero arms, the 7 EXP-01 properties, the 6 DC components. What it defines: nothing in block form... What it derives: nothing
a_rows_sample.statement: Edition 1 is reassessed: it merely names six concept clusters without block-form definitions (M49, BC_Governance, 8 K_t primitives, 4 Zero arms, 7 EXP-01 properties, 6 DC components), derives nothing (five derivations are reproducible from sources but none is reproduced), and cites evidence only in evidence-maps rather than prose; explicitly 'Edition 1 is not reinterpreted as defective -- it is the correct artifact of its ratified specification, and it is the wrong artifact for the full-depth goal.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: "Certifying an election result" -- chosen because it is native to this repository's domain, rich enough to exercise every object, and cleanly separable from product specifics.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single running example -- 'certifying an election result' -- is proposed to thread Part III end-to-end: Goal G (the result is trustworthy) -> IdealState -> EC=eta(G,IdealState) -> K_t populated across the eight primitives -> Zero(K,EC) typed gaps (unknown/conflicting/missing/invalid) -> evidence arriving (duplicates must not triple confidence per I-5; dependency per I-6) -> the claim's admission-ladder walk (Candidate->Supported->Accepted, stopping short of Committed until an authority act per A6) -> a filled Decision Contract for 'publish certification' -> the action loop closing to K_t+1; classified throughout as [INTERPRETATION]/[EDITORIAL] illustration, never evidence for the architecture, with a mandated 'three-voice discipline' (conceptual model / architecture / implementation-honesty) at every step.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Per-connection classification (sec9 vocabulary...): Measure theory as live foundation -- 5 . unsupported speculation... Probability distributions over evidence -- 6 . research candidate... Topology / metric spaces on K_t -- 6 . research candidate...
a_rows_sample.statement: A per-connection classification table rates each proposed DeepSeek mathematical connection (measure theory as foundation: 5=unsupported speculation, only 3=explanatory analogy historically; probability distributions over evidence: 6=research candidate, gated by the seven EXP-01 properties; topology/metric on K_t: 6=research candidate; 'Zero as boundary operator': 4=new theoretical proposition at best; 'Lord as generator'/'Sarathi as projection': 3=explanatory analogy only; 'KnowledgeOS as transition operator': 4=new theoretical proposition; category theory/functional analysis: 5->6); none is found already established by KnowledgeOS evidence (class 1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 scope creep from "explaining" into "deciding" (OQ pressure)... R2 the D-2 failure mode at scale (paraphrasing ratified wording)... R6 effort: this is a 90-140k-word programme; phase gates keep it stoppable at every boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six risks are recorded for the Edition-2 programme: scope creep from explaining into deciding (OQ pressure); the D-2 failure mode recurring at scale (paraphrasing ratified wording, mitigated by a verbatim rule); kernel research underdelivering (accepted, I.3 ships thin with its caveat); the running example drifting into product design (mitigated by three-voice discipline); external-math pressure leaking in through diagrams/interpretation sections; and sheer effort (90-140k words, mitigated by stoppable phase gates).

a_rows_sample.anchor: EDITION 2 COMMISSIONING -- 1) AMEND Book Architecture per BA-ED2-01...10 ... 2) AUTHORIZE Edition-2 production (Option A scope) ... 3) COMMISSION kernel full-read research (38 docs)
a_rows_sample.statement: A proposed (not made) three-part HPA ruling skeleton: (1) amend Book Architecture per BA-ED2-01..10 [AUTHORIZE/AMEND/HOLD]; (2) authorize Edition-2 production under Option A scope [AUTHORIZE/AMEND/HOLD]; (3) commission kernel full-read research on the 38 remaining documents as a separate track feeding I.3 and OQ-2 background [AUTHORIZE/HOLD]. The document ends: 'STOP. Nothing implemented; nothing amended; nothing written into the book.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Goal / IdealState / EC / Kt / Zero / Evidence / Admission / Decision / Authorization / Action / Outcome / Kt+1 / potentially Policy change / governance ... turn the book from an architecture catalogue into something people can actually learn from.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes threading a single coherent running example (the election-certification example already started in Part III) end-to-end through the sequence Goal -> IdealState -> EC -> K_t -> Zero -> Evidence -> Admission -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> K_t+1 -> (potentially) Policy change/governance, rather than leaving separate disconnected examples per chapter, explicitly framed as what could turn the book from an architecture catalogue into a learnable text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Depth (BA-ED2-01): XL 6,000-10,000 target; delivered 3,096 words -- see report; recorded deviation, justification: all mandated elements present... density per GN-42 final rule.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms a recurring, explicitly disclosed and justified depth-deviation pattern across Edition-2 Part III chapters: each chapter is assigned a target word-count range by depth class (BA-ED2-01) but is consistently delivered shorter (e.g. III.5: XL 6,000-10,000 target, 3,096 words delivered), justified each time by a density-over-padding rule (GN-42's final rule) rather than treated as a silent shortfall, with the substantive-depth question explicitly delegated to the Part III review gate rather than self-certified by the chapter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The book may explain the architecture more deeply, but deeper explanation must never silently expand, repair, or redefine the architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Edition 2 has no authority to change the KnowledgeOS architecture; deeper explanation of the architecture must never silently expand, repair, or redefine it. Any architectural change requires a separate governance act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM ↓ SOURCE ↓ GRADE ↓ FORMAL MEANING ↓ ARCHITECTURAL MEANING ↓ EXAMPLE ↓ LIMITATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Edition-2 book-writing methodology for a mentor role: before writing a chapter, ask what the reader must learn, the chapter's boundary, its authoritative sources, existing mathematical/formal material, what is established vs open, which findings affect the chapter, and which interfaces with previous chapters must stay consistent. During writing, follow the chain CLAIM -> SOURCE -> GRADE -> FORMAL MEANING -> ARCHITECTURAL MEANING -> EXAMPLE -> LIMITATION. After writing, run provenance, terminology, mathematical-strength, architecture-boundary, open-question, running-example, relation-status, no-hindsight, and forbidden-status-vocabulary checks, rerun after any substantive edit. When a difficult concept is encountered, the only permitted choices are: EXPLAIN EXISTING MODEL, EXPOSE OPEN QUESTION, REPORT FINDING, or REQUEST GOVERNANCE -- never 'INVENT A BETTER ARCHITECTURE' without an explicit research/governance commission.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal X_t = ( Q_t, K_t, U_t, N_t, X_t, A_t, D_t, G_t, \Delta_t, H_t )
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the complete operational state as a 10-field tuple X_t=(Q,K,U,N,X,A,D,G,Δ,H): Q question/inquiry, K knowledge, U understanding, N normative, X domain/reality, A actor, D decision, G guidance/investigation, Δ structured discrepancy, H historical/lineage; with transition X_{t+1}=T(X_t,Event_t,Policy_t). Accompanied by a full pipeline diagram (Purpose->Question->Inquiry->Semantics->Knowledge->{Understanding,Normative,Domain}->Zero->Discrepancy->Lord->Sārathi->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation, feeding back to Knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_t = ( World_t, Knowledge_t, Understanding_t, Norms_t, Agent_t, Context_t )
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the ten-field X_t=(Q,K,U,N,X,A,D,G,Δ,H) as 'too overloaded' with a leaner domain-state/evaluation split: S_t=(World_t,Knowledge_t,Understanding_t,Norms_t,Agent_t,Context_t); Evaluation E_t=Evaluate(S_t,Criteria_t); Discrepancy Δ_t=Diff(S_t,Criteria_t); Guidance G_t=Guide(S_t,Δ_t); Decision D_t=Decide(S_t,G_t); Action A_t=Execute(D_t); complete transition S_{t+1}=T(S_t,A_t,O_{t+1}); full loop S_t->Evaluate->Discrepancy->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->S_{t+1}, called 'the model I would now prefer'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S=(W,K,U,N,A,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Freezes the mathematical core going forward: State S=(W,K,U,N,A,C) [world, knowledge, understanding, normative environment, agent condition, context]; Evaluation E=Evaluate(S,P); Discrepancy Δ=Diff(E); Guidance G=Guide(S,Δ); Decision D=Decide(S,G); Action a=Execute(D); Transition S'=T(S,a,o). Re-formalizes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as capabilities not domain entities: Z(S,P)->Δ (detect/diagnose), L(K,N,U,C)->R (orient/interpret/resolve/synthesize, R an authoritative reasoning/resolution structure), S_a(S,R)->G (contextualize/guide), then G->D->a. Adds the deepest DDD conclusion: ActionMeaning=f(Actor,Role,Context,Knowledge,Understanding,Norms,Intention,Authority) — the semantic center of the model is not Knowledge but the relationship between Actor, Normative Context, Situation, Understanding and intended Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across successive knowledge states, while its knowledge, understanding, observations, and forms may change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Ātma A_K as the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across a sequence of knowledge states K_0,K_1,...,K_t, satisfying A_K(t1)=A_K(t2) while K_t1≠K_t2 in general — 'the Ātma remains invariant while the knowledge state evolves'. Explicitly NOT defined as 'all knowledge' or as the Ideal State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Knowledge Ātma}\neq K_t\neq I_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three distinct concepts that must not collapse: Knowledge Ātma (who/what persists through knowledge-state changes), Knowledge State K_t (what is currently known/represented), Ideal State I_t (what should be known/understood/achieved for the current purpose) — Knowledge Ātma ≠ K_t ≠ I_t, called 'a very strong architectural separation'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq\mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a potentially unbounded Knowledge Space 𝒦 of which the current Knowledge State is only a finite/partial representation, K_t⊆𝒦; Knowledge Ātma is not 𝒦 itself but the persistent identity undertaking an 'epistemic journey' A_K --epistemic journey--> K_t⊆𝒦 across K_0->K_1->K_2->... indefinitely. Layered architecture diagram: Ātma=persistence/identity, Knowledge State=current manifestation, Zero=reveals the boundary of what is currently known, Lord=expands the possible knowledge horizon, Sārathi=navigates the transition, Knower=experiences/evaluates/decides.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural and mathematical abstraction inspired by the philosophical concept of Ātman. It is not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman described in the Bhagavad Gītā.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit disclaimer required before using the term in formal theory: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural/mathematical abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman — protecting the model from a category error. Notes that introducing Knowledge Ātma changes the ontology of the complete KnowledgeOS model, requiring formal distinction of identity, state, knowledge, understanding, ideal, and evolution, and recommends exploring this before Question 20.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is the persistent Knower whose identity remains invariant while its knowledge, understanding, observations, experiences, and represented states change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles 'Ātma = invariant identity underlying changing states' with 'Ātma = the Knower' into one definition: Ātma = the persistent Knower, invariant (A_t1=A_t2) while its knowledge state K_t changes (K_t1≠K_t2). 'Knower' names its role, 'invariant/persistent' names its mathematical property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \underbrace{\text{Ātma}}_{\text{Who knows}} \quad \underbrace{K_t}_{\text{What is known}} \quad \underbrace{I_t}_{\text{What should be known}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a clean three-way separation Ātma ('who knows') / K_t ('what is known') / I_t ('what should be known'), judged much cleaner than identifying Ātma with the Knowledge State itself; repeats the caution that this is a KnowledgeOS mathematical/architectural abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a claim of having mathematically captured the metaphysical Ātman of the Gītā.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that KnowledgeOS Ātma is literally a second Ātman
b_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating KnowledgeOS Ātma as literally a second metaphysical Ātman — that would move from architectural analogy to metaphysical claim. Defines 𝒜_H := Human Knower abstraction and 𝒜_K := KnowledgeOS persistent system identity; the shared word 'Ātma' expresses the analogy of persistence/invariant identity, not metaphysical identity between the two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A_H \neq \mathcal A_K \neq K_t \subseteq \mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the four-way separation Knower Ātma ≠ Knowledge Ātma, Knowledge Ātma ≠ Knowledge State, Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Space, giving 𝒜_H ≠ 𝒜_K ≠ K_t ⊆ 𝒦. Models the Arjuna-Sārathi interaction as 𝒜_H --Intent--> 𝒜_K --Investigation--> K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> next inquiry, worked through 'show me whom I have to fight' discovering new dimensions {Kinship, Teacher, Elder,...} via parsing/semantic reconstruction rather than the Knower pre-specifying them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the architecture as Human Knower <-> KnowledgeOS Ātma <-> Knowledge Space, with Zero/Lord/Sārathi operating between the current state and the expanding knowledge horizon, and proposes that the next formal question should be 'what is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?' rather than continuing with an isolated mathematical object — called 'a significant conceptual milestone'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \widehat K_t = \text{best available reconstruction from }O_{\le t}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'we try our best but never reach the best' as K̂_t = best available reconstruction from O_≤t, with K̂_t ≠ K_t possibly persisting even as observations accumulate (O_≤t1 ⊆ O_≤t2 may give a better but still imperfect K̂_t2). Draws a careful analogy to least-squares/Gaussian estimation (x̂=argmin_x‖Ax-b‖²): 'best approximation under a criterion' does not guarantee x̂=x_true, giving 'Best reconstruction under regime R ≠ complete underlying Knowledge'. Places measure/probability theory specifically at the Observations->probabilistic reconstruction step (P(K_t|F_t), E[X_t|F_t]), with K_t itself 'conceptually prior' to the probabilistic extraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātman should not be modeled as an "Ideal State" itself. It is better modeled as the invariant identity underlying changing states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed equation of Ātman with the Ideal State, offering instead 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' ℐ with ℐ_{t+1}=ℐ_t while K_{t+1}≠K_t and I_{t+1}≠I_t in general, giving Identity ≠ Current State ≠ Ideal State — 'a very important refinement'. K_t = State(ℐ,t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_0 \subseteq? K_1 \subseteq? K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution K_0->K_1->K_2->... within K_t⊆𝒦 is NOT necessarily monotonic — an assertion can be accepted, then questioned, then rejected, so K_{t+1} may contain less information than K_t in one sense while being epistemically better, reinforcing the earlier distinction between knowledge quantity and knowledge quality/coherence. Also cautions against assuming lim_{t->∞} K_t = 𝒦 as a mathematical fact rather than an assumption.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Ātman doctrine} \rightarrow \text{philosophical inspiration} \rightarrow \text{Invariant Identity abstraction}
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit philosophy/mathematics firewall: 'The Gītā teaches that Ātman is not destroyed' does NOT mathematically imply 'our model proves an invariant identity exists' — Ātman doctrine -> philosophical inspiration -> Invariant Identity abstraction, never Ātman doctrine ⇒ mathematical theorem. Recommends adding 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' as a new theoretical concept (not folding Ātman into Ideal State), with a suggested documentation sentence: 'The concept of Ātman provides a philosophical analogue for the architectural concept of persistent identity... KnowledgeOS may use this as a conceptual inspiration, but does not claim to computationally model Ātman or establish its metaphysical truth.'
