b_rows_sample.anchor: I would write Step 285 as a formal research step, not as a philosophical essay. The Gita should provide a conceptual lens and design hypothesis, while the mathematical/DDD work determines what can actually enter KnowledgeOS theory. In particular, we should not treat Gita concepts as axioms unless the derivation explicitly justifies that move.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opening methodological ruling establishing that Step 285 is a formal research artifact, not philosophical prose, and that the Bhagavad Gita may only supply a conceptual lens/design hypothesis — mathematics and DDD derivation alone determine canonical KnowledgeOS content; explicitly bars treating Gita concepts as axioms absent justified derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gita insight ≠ KnowledgeOS theorem ... A philosophical correspondence may: generate a hypothesis; expose a modelling distinction; suggest a useful analogy; challenge an implicit assumption. It may not, by itself: establish a mathematical axiom; prove an invariant; select the canonical K; select an operation; establish a governance rule. ... ANALOGY / HEURISTIC / DESIGN HYPOTHESIS / FORMAL DERIVATION / GOVERNANCE DECISION. Only the final two can establish normative KnowledgeOS semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strict epistemic rule governing all Gita-to-KnowledgeOS correspondences in this research programme: a philosophical analogy can generate hypotheses/heuristics/distinctions but never by itself establishes an axiom, invariant, canonical state choice, operation, or governance rule; requires every mapping to be tagged ANALOGY/HEURISTIC/DESIGN HYPOTHESIS/FORMAL DERIVATION/GOVERNANCE DECISION, with only the latter two counting as normative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The eight preceding per-chapter HPA analyses in this same batch (S2046-S2053) each present boxed Gita-derived formalizations and declare every 'gap' category 'Solved'/'Complete' without applying any ANALOGY/HEURISTIC/HYPOTHESIS/DERIVATION/GOVERNANCE classification, despite this document's explicit rule (same date, same research thread, referenced as 'Next' step by all of them) that only FORMAL DERIVATION or GOVERNANCE DECISION may establish normative KnowledgeOS semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extraction-agent cross-document observation (not a claim made within either source document itself): Step 285's own no-philosophical-derivation constraint is in direct methodological tension with the practice followed by every one of the eight per-chapter HPA analysis files that chronologically/thematically precede it in this batch and explicitly point forward to 'STEP 285 — CANONICAL THEORY RECONCILIATION' as their own next step — none of those eight files classified their Gita-derived formalizations as ANALOGY/HEURISTIC/HYPOTHESIS, and all declared their results 'Solved'/'Complete' outright.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematician: Step 285 uses this material as a conceptual lens... Its usable output is a set of non-identity claims — K ≠ Operation, K ≠ History, K ≠ Evidence, K ≠ GovernanceAct, K ≠ Inquiry. Those are well-formed and testable... Statistician: Evidence ≠ State and the latent-state/observation separation restate a distinction the corpus already holds. No new measurement content... DDD architect: [the non-collapse discipline] is a bounded-context discipline stated in another idiom. Useful as a design heuristic; it is not a governance act and cannot select a K. Gap effect: none. WRITE ONLY AS RESEARCH HISTORY.
b_rows_sample.statement: Delivers a formal three-lens (mathematician, statistician, DDD architect) evaluation of the entire ~420KB / 18-file Gita chapter analysis corpus: mathematically its only usable output is five well-formed, testable non-identity claims already consistent with prior dependency exclusions; statistically it contributes no new measurement content beyond the corpus's existing Evidence≠State distinction; architecturally its non-collapse discipline restates bounded-context practice in Gita idiom and 'is not a governance act and cannot select a K.' Net verdict: 'Gap effect: none', classified for the book as 'WRITE ONLY AS RESEARCH HISTORY' — independently corroborating (from outside those documents) the same no-philosophical-derivation discipline that Step 285 stated internally, and functioning as the formal Lane-A adjudication of the Lane-B per-chapter HPA series in this same batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The review correctly detects that Step 285 should use the Gītā more deeply, but it makes a serious methodological mistake: it turns Gītā philosophy into a proposed KnowledgeOS mathematical ontology too quickly. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a prior ('the previous review') improvement suggestion for Step 285 for prematurely converting Gita philosophy directly into KnowledgeOS mathematical ontology, restating the governing principle that the Gita may supply premises/distinctions/analogies/hypotheses but never by itself state variables, operators, invariants, or theorems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Gītā provides the philosophical vocabulary and conceptual lens; KnowledgeOS provides the formal vocabulary. The translation between them is a research mapping, not an identity claim. ... This register should become an input to the hypothesis programme, not part of the canonical kernel until individual mappings survive the derivation and governance gates.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the register's governing principle and its intended lifecycle: it is explicitly scoped as an input to a future hypothesis programme, with individual mappings required to separately survive derivation and governance gates before any could enter the canonical kernel — placing this document firmly within the disciplined (Lane-A-adjacent) side of the Gita-integration sub-series.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The objective is not to prove that the Bhagavad Gītā explains KnowledgeOS. The objective is to determine whether any Gītā-derived conceptual correspondence survives independent philosophical, mathematical, epistemic, DDD, architectural, and falsification tests. ... A correspondence becomes interesting precisely when it survives without requiring us to distort either the Gītā or KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the programme's central governing principle in its clearest form across the entire Gita sub-series: success is not proving the Gita explains KnowledgeOS, but finding correspondences that survive rigorous testing without distorting either source — the sharpest formulation of the discipline that the per-chapter HPA analyses (S2046-S2053) and the 'source code' synthesis (S2059) violate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No invariant, operation, primitive or state component in D285-1…7 is derived from scripture. The Gītā appears in this research as: one ratified convergence it predates, one negative result, one corroboration, one vocabulary loan, and five corrections.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing discipline statement certifying that none of the formal Step-285 deliverables derive any invariant, operation, primitive, or state component from scripture, and summarizing the Gita's entire actual role in the research in five categories (a convergence it predates, a negative/refutation result, a corroboration, a vocabulary loan, and five corrections) -- the definitive closure of the Gita-integration research thread within this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a claim that the Bhagavad-gita describes KnowledgeOS. It is a philosophical model constructed by reflecting Gita concepts through the KnowledgeOS problem ... philosophical material is not required to establish the core equality/kernel results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit framing discipline opening the full 18-chapter synthesis: this is not a claim the Gita describes KnowledgeOS but a philosophical model constructed by reflecting Gita concepts through the KnowledgeOS problem, with math/statistics/epistemology/DDD used to test resulting hypotheses; philosophical material is not required to establish the corpus's core equality/kernel results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Detecting a contradiction != resolving a contradiction. KnowledgeOS must be able to detect and preserve unresolved conflict without inventing an answer
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central principle distinguishing contradiction detection from resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_i. The organization therefore has mathcal K = {K_1,K_2,...,K_n}. There is no requirement that K_1=K_2
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the multi-context knowledge collection with no equality requirement between contexts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A in K_1 and B in K_2. We cannot immediately say A and B is contradictory. We first need semantic translation T_{1->*}(A) and T_{2->*}(B)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires semantic translation before evaluating cross-context contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Compatible(A,B,C). Possible values: {Compatible, Contradictory, Conditional, Unknown, NotApplicable}. This is preferable to a binary relation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a graded five-value compatibility relation, preferable to binary contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A genuine contradiction occurs when, under a common semantic interpretation and compatible conditions, A=>P and B=>not P. Then A perp B under the relevant context
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines genuine contradiction requiring common interpretation and compatible conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A perp B under C_1 but not under C_2. Therefore contradiction must carry Context
a_rows_sample.statement: States contradiction is itself contextual.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The service is available vs The service is unavailable ... Availability_Production and Availability_Test ... A not-perp B. The apparent contradiction was caused by missing context
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked production-vs-test availability example showing an apparent contradiction dissolved by context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before declaring contradiction, KnowledgeOS should attempt ContextResolution. This is another epistemic investigation
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires context disambiguation as an epistemic investigation prior to declaring contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ServerIP=10.61.133.85 at t_1. ServerIP=10.61.133.90 at t_2. These are not contradictory if t_1 != t_2 and the state changed. TemporalAlignment must precede contradiction detection
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked temporal-alignment example requiring time alignment prior to contradiction evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A(t_1)=True and B(t_2)=True. This demonstrates Truth can be indexed by time
a_rows_sample.statement: States truth can be time-indexed, both statements can be simultaneously true at their respective times.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System supports TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_1. System does not support TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_2. the apparent contradiction disappears when conditions are represented
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked TLS-configuration example of conditional (non-genuine) contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Align(A,B) = (Entity, Time, Context, Scope, Semantics, Conditions). Only after sufficient alignment should contradiction be evaluated
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the six-dimension alignment required before contradiction evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim A -> Context/Time/Entity/Scope/Semantics -> ALIGNMENT <- Claim B/Translation -> Compatibility Analysis -> Yes/No/Unknown -> OK/Conflict/Investigate
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a contradiction-detection pipeline diagram.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two contexts can conflict operationally without making logically contradictory statements ... DeployImmediately and DeployOnlyAfterApproval. These are conflicting prescriptions. But they are not necessarily factual contradictions
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes operational/normative conflict from factual contradiction, worked with a deployment-policy example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Factual conflict: P versus not P. Semantic conflict: Same term, incompatible meanings. Normative conflict: Different rules prescribe incompatible actions. Conflict != Contradiction
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines three conflict classes (factual/semantic/normative) distinct from logical contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_1: A->Action_1 and Rule_2: A->Action_2 where Action_1 != Action_2. Then there is a policy conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes normative conflict as incompatible rule-prescribed actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_A comes from ArchitectureBoard and Rule_B comes from ProjectTeam. They may have different authority levels. Authority(Source,Rule,Context) becomes relevant
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces source-and-context-relative authority for resolving normative conflicts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A senior authority can issue an incorrect factual statement. Authority != Truth. Authority determines what is binding, not necessarily what is factually true
a_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial distinction that authority determines bindingness, not truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TruthStatus and BindingStatus. TruthStatus=Unknown while BindingStatus=Mandatory. A governance rule may be mandatory even while its underlying assumptions remain uncertain
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes separate truth-status and binding-status dimensions for a claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Board mandates All production changes require approval. Even if someone argues that approval provides little technical value, the rule remains binding ... KnowledgeOS should represent Binding=True. It should not silently override the rule based on an optimization calculation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked governance-mandate example warning against silently overriding binding rules via optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference asks what can we conclude from what we know. Step 34 asks What should we learn next? ... a fundamentally different problem
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference from information-acquisition selection as fundamentally different problems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10^6 uncertain assertions ... impossible and unnecessary to validate all of them immediately ... Choose the information acquisition action that produces the greatest useful improvement relative to its cost
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS should not investigate everything, requiring a cost-relative optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: QueryCMDB, InspectRuntime, AskDomainExpert, RunTest, PerformExperiment, RetrieveDocument, CompareIndependentSource ... produces an observation Y_I
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the information-gathering action set with seven worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cost(I) ... Time, Money, Compute, HumanAttention, OperationalRisk ... information is not free
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Cost(I) across five components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVPI=L_0-L_{PI} ... an upper bound on the value of information
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Perfect Information as an upper bound.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=L_0-E_Y[\min_d E[L(d,\theta)\mid K,Y]] ... NVOI(I)=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) ... the core mathematical idea
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Expected Value of Sample Information and net value of information as the step's core idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I^*=\arg\max_{I\in\mathcal I}NVOI(I) ... our first formal definition of NextBestEpistemicAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the first formal Next-Best-Epistemic-Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: InformationValue\neq UncertaintyReduction ... A has no influence on any important decision ... UncertaintyReduction(A) may have almost zero practical value
b_rows_sample.statement: States the subtle principle that information value is not the same as uncertainty reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionSensitivity(A,D) ... Information about A is valuable if learning A can change d^*
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines DecisionSensitivity as the criterion for information value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nexus has 31 GB RAM ... migration architecture does not depend on RAM beyond a very large safety margin ... almost no decision value
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of low-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (RAM precision beyond safety margin).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Production database backup is restorable ... DecisionSensitivity(B,D) is very high ... validating B may have extremely high VOI
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting example of high-decision-sensitivity uncertainty (backup restorability).

b_rows_sample.anchor: d^*=f(K) ... If perturbing A does not change f(K), then A has low local decision sensitivity
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a decision-relevance partition via perturbation of the decision function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Closure(A) ... A\rightarrow B\rightarrow D ... DependencyClosure+DecisionCriticality=EpistemicPrioritization
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines Step 32's dependency closure with decision dependency, giving a prioritization formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Criticality(D) ... Low, Medium, High, Critical ... should be domain-owned. KnowledgeOS can consume it but should not invent the business meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a domain-owned Criticality classification, not invented by KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL(d)=E[L(d,\theta)\mid K] ... d^*=\arg\min_d EL(d) ... d_1 expected loss 10, d_2 expected loss 12 ... investigation may reveal a high-risk state in which d_2 becomes preferable
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected loss and current-optimal decision, worked with a two-decision expected-loss-reversal example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk<5\%\Rightarrow AutomaticApproval ... Risk\in[3\%,8\%] ... DecisionBoundaryUncertainty. Uncertainty far from a decision boundary may be harmless. Uncertainty near a boundary can be critical
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DecisionBoundaryUncertainty, worked with a threshold-straddling risk-interval example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk\in[1\%,2\%] ... no urgent investigation ... Risk\in[4\%,7\%] crosses the decision boundary ... additional evidence is valuable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked contrasting examples of harmless-far and critical-boundary-straddling risk intervals.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(A)\propto DecisionImpact(A)\times Uncertainty(A) ... conceptual, not yet a universal formula
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual, not-yet-universal epistemic-triage priority formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI(I)=10, Cost(I)=2, NVOI(I)=8 ... EVSI=12, Cost=20, NVOI=-8 ... should not be prioritized merely because it provides more information
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked arithmetic example showing higher-EVSI investigations can have lower net value once cost is subtracted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HumanAttention is an epistemic resource ... 2 hours of a senior architect's time may be more expensive than a machine-readable check
b_rows_sample.statement: States human attention is itself a costed epistemic resource, worked with a comparison example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `K = (𝒜, ℛ)` has **no recognised-dimension set `D_t`**.
a_rows_sample.statement: The one genuinely missing component: K=(𝒜,ℛ) has no recognised-dimension set D_t, so 'a dimension never assessed' and 'a dimension assessed with no result' both render identically and are provably indistinguishable in K, though the pre-existing Zero model already carries the needed layer and resolves the distinction in O(n); the distinction is load-bearing because the theory's own admissibility law blocks on Unknown (42.12) and a gate that cannot tell Unknown from not-asked will block identically on a question nobody posed and a question that defeated investigation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **1** | **`ℛ` restored to `(E₁,E₂,T,R,Q,E,Σ,τ)`, n-ary** | nothing | **CORPUS ESTABLISHES ×4** |
a_rows_sample.statement: The six smallest missing things are ranked in dependency order: (1) restore ℛ to its 8-tuple form — closes 4 gaps, invents nothing, the smallest/cheapest/highest-yield fix; (2) add D_t to K; (3) give AuthorityAct identity (genuinely 0 corpus occurrences, absent, not merely lost); (4) supply Qualify's body; (5) restore (W,Ω); (6) fix Σ's value set and str rule (exactly what Step 272 was commissioned to do). Only #3 and #4 require genuine invention; the rest require only restoration or adoption of material the corpus already established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus says 'nobody ever asked'. ... Seven of eight are directly covered; the eighth is partial. The audit reported zero of five.
b_rows_sample.statement: A six-way Zero-lens dimension/value taxonomy (known / unknown Zero-A / not-assessed / absent / not-applicable / unresolved Zero-B) with five non-collapse laws (UNKNOWN!=ABSENT, UNRESOLVED!=INVALID, NOT_ASSESSED!=LOW_CONFIDENCE, NOT_APPLICABLE!=UNKNOWN, NO_EVIDENCE!=INVALID_EVIDENCE) plus a sixth boxed law (UnknownValue(D)!=UnknownDimension(D)), together with an independently-committed Abhava ontological absence typology (Pragabhava/Pradhvamsabhava/Atyantabhava/Anyonyabhava) and an AbsenceClaim record shape, jointly cover seven of the mandate's eight missingness cases directly and one partially -- versus the audit's report of zero of five covered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
b_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: VERIFIER RECOMMENDS -- not CORPUS ESTABLISHES. K = (D_t, A, R) ... with id = H(P, e_refs, c, t, Pi) where e_refs projects out the mutable state. ... Nothing here is adopted. This is a proposal, and it is smaller than the three the corpus already contains -- which should be consumed first (ES-005.4).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes (explicitly labelled VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not adopted) a minimal repair K=(D_t,A,R) adding the recognised-dimension set D_t and redefining id=H(P,e_refs,c,t,Pi) to project out the mutable state field, arguing this closes the missingness gap (7/8 cases), removes the identity/mutability contradiction, and makes a dedup operator definable by unioning Pi and e on (P,c,t); explicitly states this does not repair non-identifiability (needs a W,Omega layer beneath K) or uncertainty (needs U(H)), and that the corpus's own existing three constructions should be consumed first per ES-005.4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Empty != ContradictoryEvidence. ... Missing != False. ... EvalPolicy may need a third result: Undetermined.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues no-evidence must be distinguished from conflicting-evidence when assigning Sigma=Unknown, and that a missing required measurement (x=?) cannot be inferred as False; proposes a candidate three-valued policy-decision output {Permit, Deny, Undetermined} as a bridge between missingness and policy, explicitly marked as a candidate requiring corpus confirmation, not a final decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three exclusions were a discovery failure, not a mathematical limit. They are absent from the AUTHORIZED MODEL v0.2 ... so the finding is real, and it is a GOVERNANCE finding: the constructions exist and were never promoted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior verdict ('THEORY CLOSED AGAINST THE STATED CRITERIA -- NOT COMPLETE IN EVERY RESPECT', with 'a theory that cannot say nobody ever asked is closed, not finished') by showing the corpus does say 'nobody ever asked' (the not-assessed Zero-lens dimension state, committed one day before this programme began) and does have formal, typed constructions for non-identifiability and uncertainty; reclassifies the three exclusions as a discovery failure rather than a mathematical limit, and as a governance finding since these constructions are measured absent (zero grep occurrences of unknown/absent/not assessed/uncertain/identifiab) from the authorized v0.2 model despite existing in the raw corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: - **`Missingness` — 0.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Three concepts have exactly zero definitional occurrences corpus-wide: Missingness (the concept exists richly under other names — Zero, abhāva, Missing, 'not assessed' — so this is a vocabulary gap masquerading as a theory gap), Admissibility (its two laws are cited constantly, 42.9/42.41, but the term itself is never defined), and AuthorityAct (confirming, by whole-corpus scan rather than targeted grep, that the object the entire governance model turns on has no type).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
**First, the vocabulary fact that explains why this looked unresolved:** the word **`Missingness`
 has 0 definitional occurrences corpus-wide**
b_rows_sample.statement: 8 of 9 mandated missingness distinctions (not-asked, asked-but-no-answer, unknown, absent, no-evidence-found, searched-but-insufficient, deliberately-omitted, deleted; only 'never existed'/Prāgabhāva lacks one) have a named corpus construct across the Zero taxonomy and the Sanskrit abhāva typology, and 4 of them (unknown, absent, insufficient, not-applicable) are executable, tested, passing code in zero_reference.py (8/8 tests); the word 'Missingness' itself has 0 definitional occurrences, so searching for the word finds nothing while the capability exists richly under other names.

b_rows_sample.anchor: With D_t: "not assessed" is D ∈ D_t ∧ ¬∃a ∈ 𝒜 : a.P.D = D — decidable in O(n).
b_rows_sample.statement: The Zero model's D_t (recognised-dimension set) plus Z_t=Omega\Represented(K_t) layer, already present in the corpus, makes 'not assessed' a decidable O(n) predicate (D in D_t and no assertion covers D), and this is proposed as the minimum additional structural component needed -- not invented, but recovered from the corpus's own Zero-lens construction.

b_notations: not assessed / absent / not applicable / unresolved

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'D_t'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Best action \neq action that merely reduces discrepancy most. An action has cost, risk, reversibility, authority requirements, information value, and consequences.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the naive assumption that the best action is the one that maximally reduces discrepancy: actions carry cost, risk, reversibility, authority requirements, information value, and consequences.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The fundamental problem ... a^*=\arg\min_a Distance(K_{t+1},I). Why? Because some actions are dangerous; expensive; irreversible; unauthorized; unnecessary; poorly understood. action selection is a decision problem under uncertainty and constraints.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a1*=argmin_a Distance(K_{t+1},I) as insufficient given actions can be dangerous/expensive/irreversible/unauthorized/unnecessary/poorly understood — action selection is a decision problem under uncertainty and constraints.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action is not knowledge ... Knowledge\neq Action and Recommendation\neq Execution. "Changing the firewall rule is likely to solve the discrepancy." That does not mean "Change the firewall rule." There is a governance boundary between those two statements.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Knowledge ≠ Action and Recommendation ≠ Execution as a governance boundary between a diagnostic statement and a directive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define an Action ... a=(Intent,Preconditions,Effects,Cost,Risk,Reversibility,Authority,EvidenceRequirements,Context). An action is therefore a structured domain object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Action as a structured domain object a=(Intent,Preconditions,Effects,Cost,Risk,Reversibility,Authority,EvidenceRequirements,Context).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action Preconditions ... Migrate Nexus may require q_1=Backup verified, q_2=Rollback available, q_3=Dependencies identified. Preconditions(a) must be evaluated against K_t. If a critical precondition is unknown Executable(a)=False unless an explicit governance policy permits otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Preconditions(a) evaluated against K_t (worked with three migration preconditions), with Executable(a)=False by default when a critical precondition is unknown, absent explicit governance override.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action effects ... Transition_a(X_t)\rightarrow X_{t+1} where X is the domain state. But we may not know the exact outcome. X_{t+1} may be probabilistic or uncertain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines action effects as a (possibly probabilistic/uncertain) domain-state transition Transition_a(X_t)→X_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expected outcome ... o_1,o_2,\ldots,o_m with probabilities P(o_i\mid a,K_t). EU(a) = \sum_i P(o_i\mid a,K_t)U(o_i) where U is the utility function. This is standard expected-utility reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines standard expected utility EU(a)=Σ_i P(o_i|a,K_t)U(o_i) over possible action outcomes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Information has value ... inspect firewall logs. Its direct operational effect may be \Delta_{operational}=0. But it may greatly reduce uncertainty. Information itself has decision value.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Information itself has decision value, illustrated by an inspection action with zero direct operational effect but high uncertainty reduction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Value of Information ... EVSI(q) = \mathbb E_r[\max_a EU(a\mid K_{t+1}(r))] - \max_a EU(a\mid K_t) where EVSI is the Expected Value of Sample Information. This is a very useful formalization for Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Expected Value of Sample Information EVSI(q)=E_r[max_a EU(a|K_{t+1}(r))]-max_a EU(a|K_t), a formal decision-theoretic value-of-information measure for Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Simpler KnowledgeOS formulation ... VOI(q) = ExpectedDecisionImprovement(q) - Cost(q) as a policy-level approximation. q^* = \arg\max_q VOI(q). Subject to Risk(q)\leq RiskLimit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a simpler policy-level VOI(q)=ExpectedDecisionImprovement(q)-Cost(q), with q*=argmax_q VOI(q) subject to a risk limit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This changes the role of Lord ... Generate candidate actions and investigations that have high expected value for reducing relevant uncertainty, discrepancy, or decision risk. Lord: (K_t,I_t,\Delta_t) \rightarrow \mathcal A_t with each candidate annotated by ExpectedBenefit, Cost, Risk, VOI, Reversi
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Lord: (K_t,I_t,Δ_t)→A_t, with each candidate action annotated by ExpectedBenefit, Cost, Risk, VOI, and Reversibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi is the decision function ... Sārathi: (K_t,I_t,\Delta_t,\mathcal A_t,\rho) \rightarrow Decision ... Decision\in\{Execute,Investigate,Defer,Reject,Escalate,RequestApproval\}. This is important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Sārathi:(K_t,I_t,Δ_t,A_t,ρ)→Decision, with Decision∈{Execute,Investigate,Defer,Reject,Escalate,RequestApproval}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi does not have unlimited authority ... production firewall change. Authority(a)=ArchitectureBoard. Therefore Sārathi should produce RequestApproval(a). Not Execute(a). Decision capability\neq Execution authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Decision capability ≠ Execution authority, illustrated by a production firewall change requiring Sārathi to produce RequestApproval rather than Execute even when it is the best-evaluated action.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision feasibility ... Feasible(a,K_t,\rho) = Preconditions \land Authority \land Constraints \land Safety. Only feasible actions enter the final decision set. \mathcal A^{feasible} \subseteq \mathcal A.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Feasible(a,K_t,ρ)=Preconditions∧Authority∧Constraints∧Safety, filtering the candidate set to A^feasible⊆A before decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Constrained optimization ... a^* = \arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A^{feasible}} EU(a) subject to Risk(a)\leq R_{max} and Cost(a)\leq C_{max}. This is already a computationally well-defined problem when the relevant quantities are available.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes constrained action optimization a*=argmax_{a∈A^feasible} EU(a) subject to Risk(a)≤R_max and Cost(a)≤C_max.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But utility is not universal ... There is no universal U(a). For one organization Cost may dominate. For another Safety may dominate. For an incident TimeToRecovery may dominate. UtilityFunction is policy/purpose dependent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues there is no universal utility function U(a); it is policy/purpose dependent (cost-dominant vs safety-dominant vs recovery-time-dominant organizations).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-objective decision making ... Objectives=\{Cost,Risk,Time,Quality,Compliance,Security,Availability\}. There may be no single naturally correct ordering. \mathbf U(a)=(u_1(a),\ldots,u_n(a)). U_\rho(a) = F_\rho(\mathbf U(a)).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a multi-objective utility vector U(a)=(u1(a),...,un(a)) over seven named objectives (Cost/Risk/Time/Quality/Compliance/Security/Availability), aggregated by a policy-specific function F_ρ.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pareto optimality ... Action a_1 dominates a_2 if u_i(a_1)\geq u_i(a_2) for every criterion i, and strictly better for at least one. The Pareto frontier is \mathcal P = \{a\mid \nexists b:b\succ a\}. Sārathi can present the Pareto-optimal choices to the human decision-maker. This is often better tha
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Pareto dominance and the Pareto frontier P={a|∄b:b≻a}, recommending Sārathi present the Pareto set to a human decision-maker rather than pretend to know exact utility weights.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Example ... Inspect logs Low Very Low High Yes ... Change firewall Medium High Low Partly ... Do nothing Zero High None Yes. A naive optimizer might choose DoNothing because Cost=0. A purely discrepancy-driven system might choose ChangeFirewall. A proper decision system may choose InspectLogs becaus
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked five-action decision table (inspect logs/ask owner/run test/change firewall/do nothing) showing a naive cost-minimizer picks DoNothing and a naive discrepancy-minimizer picks ChangeFirewall, while the intended system correctly picks InspectLogs for its high information value at low risk.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exploration versus exploitation ... Exploration Acquire information a_{explore} ... Exploitation Act on current knowledge a_{exploit} ... Sārathi must balance InformationGain vs ImmediateBenefit. This is closely related to sequential decision theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the exploration (acquire information) vs exploitation (act on current knowledge) tradeoff Sārathi must balance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Given everything currently known, what should happen next? ... Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,C)\rightarrow a_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Lord's fundamental operator: Lord(K_t, Z_t=Zero(K_t,EC), G, C) -> a_t, the next action; framed as needing to answer 'given everything currently known, what should happen next?' without letting Lord become 'an uncontrolled LLM planner.'

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x ZeroResult x Goal x Constraints

b_rows_sample.anchor: Action=EpistemicAction\cup OperationalAction
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates two action categories: Epistemic action q: K_t -> K_{t+1} (e.g. query database, inspect configuration, search documentation, ask human, run test, verify firewall, compare documents) and Operational action a: W_t -> W_{t+1} (e.g. deploy, migrate, restart, modify configuration, create infrastructure); Action = EpistemicAction ∪ OperationalAction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord selects; Governance authorizes; Executor executes ... much safer than LLM\rightarrow Shell
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord proposes a CandidateAction; a governed execution layer separately checks Authorized?/Safe?/ContractSatisfied?/Allowed?; therefore 'Lord selects; Governance authorizes; Executor executes,' explicitly contrasted as much safer than a direct LLM -> Shell architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A(K_t) ... Lord cannot choose an action outside \mathcal A
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a bounded candidate action space A(K_t) (e.g. {QueryFirewall, InspectBackup, AskArchitect, RunRestoreTest, MigrateNexus, DoNothing}); Lord cannot choose an action outside this set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a^*=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A} VOI(a) ... insufficient
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a naive first formulation a*=argmax_a VOI(a) as insufficient because VOI captures only information/decision value and ignores authorization, safety, cost, urgency, dependencies, and reversibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A=(Purpose,ExpectedGain,Cost,Risk,Urgency,Reversibility,Authorization,Dependencies,Deadline) ... resist prematurely creating Score(A)=0.83
b_rows_sample.statement: Represents an action as a nine-dimensional vector A=(Purpose, ExpectedGain, Cost, Risk, Urgency, Reversibility, Authorization, Dependencies, Deadline), explicitly warning against prematurely collapsing it to a scalar Score(A)=0.83 which 'would hide semantics.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Feasible(a,K_t,C) ... RunRestoreTest ... Feasible=True ... MigrateNexus RollbackVerified=unknown ... Feasible=False
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Feasible(a,K_t,C), worked with two examples: RunRestoreTest is Feasible=True (all preconditions available/acceptable), while MigrateNexus is Feasible=False when RollbackVerified=unknown is a blocking condition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_{feasible}=\{a\in A\mid Feasible(a,K,C)\} ... a^*=Select(A_{feasible},Objective)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the two-stage algorithm: first compute A_feasible = {a in A | Feasible(a,K,C)}, then a* = Select(A_feasible, Objective); Lord's two responsibilities are therefore (1) remove impossible/unauthorized actions, (2) choose among the remaining — 'Feasibility -> Optimization.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero={RollbackUnknown, FirewallConflicted, ApprovalMissing} ... ApprovalMissing is a hard governance blocker ... MigrateNexus is infeasible
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: given three concurrent Zero gaps and four candidate actions (run restore test, query firewall, ask Architecture Board, execute migration), a hard governance blocker (ApprovalMissing) renders MigrateNexus infeasible, so Lord must choose among the information/governance actions instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RootGap(Z)=r_1 ... Lord should not necessarily target r_3. It should target the root gap
b_rows_sample.statement: Root-gap analysis reusing the dependency chain r1=BackupExists -> r2=RestoreValidated -> r3=RollbackVerified: if r3=Unknown is caused by r1=Unknown, Lord should target RootGap(Z)=r1, not r3 — described as 'graph reasoning, not LLM intuition,' making Lord 'more efficient.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: BackupExists -> RestoreEnvironmentAvailable -> RestoreTest -> RollbackVerified -> MigrationEligible
b_rows_sample.statement: Depicts the action dependency graph Lord can traverse to reach the root-gap-resolving action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_q) ... VOI(q) ... depends on a model ... ExpectedOutcomeModel(q)
b_rows_sample.statement: For an epistemic action q, defines K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_q) and states VOI(q) requires access to an ExpectedOutcomeModel(q), reiterating that VOI depends on a model (as established in the prior evidence/VOI thread).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Outcome(q)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\} with probabilities or qualitative likelihoods where appropriate
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes expected from guaranteed outcomes: querying a database has an expected result (record found) but may fail; Outcome(q) is a set of possible outcomes with probabilities or qualitative likelihoods, letting Lord evaluate expected consequences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(q)=\sum_e P(e\mid q,K)\max_a EU(a\mid K,e) ... VOI(q)=EU(q)-EU(a^*) ... optional specialized engine, not part of the epistemic kernel
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the classical statistical/decision-theoretic version: EU(q)=sum_e P(e|q,K) max_a EU(a|K,e); VOI(q)=EU(q)-EU(a*); explicitly classified as 'an optional specialized engine, not part of the epistemic kernel.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: HighValue>MediumValue>LowValue ... q_1\succeq q_2 ... KnowledgeOS should not manufacture probabilities
b_rows_sample.statement: Where probabilities are unavailable, proposes a qualitative ordering (HighValue > MediumValue > LowValue) or a partial preference relation q1 ⪰ q2, motivated by the principle that 'KnowledgeOS should not manufacture probabilities.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: q_1: resolve governance blocker ... q_2: collect additional architecture detail ... q_1\succ q_2 ... No numerical score is needed
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing a qualitative preference (q1 directly unblocks the goal, q2 does not, so q1 ≻ q2) can be established without any numerical score — 'preferable when quantitative utility is unavailable.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prefer(a_1,a_2\mid K,G,C) ... rather than assuming Score(a) ... a_1\succ a_2, a_2\succ a_1, or a_1\sim a_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Lord's decision relation Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) with outcomes {a1≻a2, a2≻a1, a1~a2} rather than assuming a scalar Score(a); a1~a2 means 'both are equally defensible under current knowledge.'

type_signature.domain: Action x Action x KnowledgeState x Goal x Constraints

b_rows_sample.anchor: IndeterminatePreference\rightarrow HumanDecision ... rather than arbitrary AI selection
b_rows_sample.statement: When a1~a2 and the system cannot distinguish them by governed criteria, Lord may ask for human preference: IndeterminatePreference -> HumanDecision, rather than arbitrary AI selection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Safety(a,K,C) must hold ... RollbackVerified=Unknown ... Safety=False ... MigrateNexus\notin A_{feasible}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Safety(a,K,C) as a required precondition before selecting an operational action; e.g. ProductionMigration requiring RollbackVerified=True fails Safety when RollbackVerified=Unknown, excluding MigrateNexus from A_feasible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authorized(a,C) must be true ... rm -rf ... Authorized=False ... Capability\neq Authority
b_rows_sample.statement: An AI may be technically capable of an action (e.g. 'rm -rf ...') yet Authorized(a,C)=False makes it non-candidate: 'Capability ≠ Authority' — 'a fundamental separation.'

a_notations: Sarathi: Lord's selected action -> actual behavior
a_aliases: Step 15: Decision Theory, Value of Information, Action Selection, and Sārathi

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'formal-lord-action-selection-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi' (batch B0022). Note: S0899's Step 25G: the first fully formal treatment of Lord specifically as a governed action-selection operator (feasibility gate, preference relation, termination algebra, seven falsification tests), distinct from B0021's broader decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi (S0871/Step 15) and from B0019's earlier informal lord-lens-horizon-expansion.

explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'decision-theory-action-selection-sarathi' POSSIBLY relates to 'formal-lord-action-selection-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: Recurring label across S0898/S0899 for the Lord (action-selection) / Sarathi (action-execution/conversion of selected action into actual behavior) architecture and its end-to-end diagram; closely related to, and possibly identical with, the already-registered formal-lord-action-selection-algebra and formal-sarathi-decision-algebra labels. Added here to satisfy the batch's own label-registration requirement; a future merge review should determine whether this collapses into those two existing objects.
labels share the alias 'Formal Lord Algebra'

a_rows_sample.anchor: most probable outcome\Rightarrow best action ... mathematically wrong in general ... Knowledge\rightarrow Prediction\rightarrow Consequences\rightarrow Utility/Risk\rightarrow Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the implicit assumption 'most probable outcome => best action' as mathematically wrong in general, establishing the correct chain Knowledge->Prediction->Consequences->Utility/Risk->Decision, plus a Decision<->ValueOfInformation relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision is not inference ... S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\} ... A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\} ... decision theory evaluates a\in A under uncertainty about s\in S
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference ('what do we believe?') from decision ('what should we do?'), formalizing state space S and action space A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(a,s) ... EU(a\mid E)=\sum_s P(s\mid E)U(a,s) ... a^*=\arg\max_a EU(a\mid E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines utility U(a,s), expected utility EU(a|E)=sum_s P(s|E)U(a,s), and the rational-choice rule a*=argmax_a EU(a|E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(Outage\mid Upgrade)=0.05 ... tells us almost nothing ... U(Upgrade,Outage) and U(DoNothing,Outage) ... the decision emerges from the whole consequence structure
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example/table showing a bare 5% outage probability tells almost nothing about whether to upgrade absent the full action/outcome/consequence structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Risk=Probability ... ExpectedLoss=\sum_s P(s\mid E)L(a,s) ... real risk can involve multiple outcomes; uncertainty intervals; catastrophic tails; irreversibility; regulatory consequences; opportunity costs
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects reducing Risk to Probability, defining ExpectedLoss=sum_s P(s|E)L(a,s) and listing six additional real-risk dimensions beyond a single probability number.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action A: P(Loss=10000)=0.10 ... Action B: P(Loss=1000000)=0.001 ... same expected loss ... TailRisk is dramatically larger ... ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked tail-risk example: two actions with identical expected loss (1000) but vastly different catastrophic-tail severity may be rationally treated differently — 'ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient'; risk policy must specify how severe/irreversible outcomes are treated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(\euro x)=\sqrt{x} ... UtilityFunction is a normative choice. KnowledgeOS should not secretly invent one
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes utility functions (e.g. sqrt(x)) can encode risk aversion but are a normative organizational choice that KnowledgeOS must not secretly invent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionContract=(Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) ... a very important DDD concept
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-field DecisionContract (Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) as an important DDD concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a_1)>EU(a_2) but Authorized(a_1)=False ... a^*=\arg\max_{a\in A_{admissible}}EU(a) ... Optimization occurs within admissible actions
a_rows_sample.statement: States optimization occurs within admissible actions only: an unauthorized highest-utility action must not execute — a*=argmax over A_admissible, not all of A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalRiskTooHigh or GovernanceAuthorizationMissing or EvidenceInsufficient ... DecisionStatus: blocked, Reason: governance_authorization_missing
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires Sarathi to distinguish blocking-failure reasons (technical risk, governance authorization missing, evidence insufficient) via a structured DecisionStatus=blocked+Reason record, rather than a bare 'decision=no.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: a^*=Upgrade [recommendation] ... does not necessarily mean Decision=Approved ... Recommendation\neq Decision\neq Authorization
a_rows_sample.statement: States Recommendation ≠ Decision ≠ Authorization: an AI-computed optimum is only a Recommendation until an authorized human/body decides.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi as a decision-support/decision-orchestration intelligence, not as an autonomous source of authority ... Sarathi:(K,Models,Constraints)\rightarrow DecisionCandidate ... Authorize(DecisionCandidate)
a_rows_sample.statement: Characterizes Sarathi as decision-support/orchestration intelligence producing a DecisionCandidate, with governance separately determining Authorize(DecisionCandidate).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord may choose between Action and InformationAcquisition ... Option 1 make decision now ... Option 4 ask human expert ... the system therefore performs meta-decision-making
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord's role as choosing between Action and InformationAcquisition, worked with a four-option example (decide now, collect observation, run simulation, ask human expert) — 'the system performs meta-decision-making.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: VOI=EU(\text{best decision after information})-EU(\text{best decision now}) ... VOI(E)=E_e[\max_a EU(a\mid E,e)]-\max_a EU(a\mid E) ... one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Value of Information via two equivalent expressions, called 'one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(Upgrade)=100, EU(DoNothing)=95 ... VOI(Inspection)=20, Cost(Inspection)=5 ... NetVOI=20-5=15>0 ... AcquireInformation is itself the rational action ... gives Zero a mathematical foundation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: given EU(Upgrade)=100 vs EU(DoNothing)=95, a candidate inspection with VOI=20 and Cost=5 yields NetVOI=15>0, making AcquireInformation itself rational — 'gives Zero a mathematical foundation.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{epistemic} from Zero_{decision} ... a missing fact matters only if resolving it could change something important ... DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero into Zero_epistemic vs Zero_decision: a knowledge gap matters only if resolving it could change something important — DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap is more important than arbitrary missing information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which Linux kernel version is installed on a test server? ... VOI\approx0 ... Lord should do nothing ... prevents KnowledgeOS from endlessly trying to make itself complete
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a genuine knowledge gap with VOI≈0 for the current decision means Lord should take no action — prevents pursuing exhaustive completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: should not optimize for CompleteKnowledge. We should optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision ... much more realistic
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision, not CompleteKnowledge — 'both computationally and operationally much more realistic.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\} ... ReadConfiguration, AskHumanExpert, RunTest, QueryAPI, RunSimulation ... i^*=\arg\max_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] ... a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes information-gathering actions as a candidate set I with per-action Cost and VOI, giving i*=argmax_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] as 'a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Restart production server to verify configuration ... Risk(Restart)>0 ... NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) ... Lord cannot blindly maximize information
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing an information-gathering action (production restart) can itself carry risk, extending net value to NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) — 'Lord cannot blindly maximize information.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence_total = Confidence_1 x Confidence_2 x Confidence_3 ... That is generally wrong
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects naive multiplication of stage confidences as generally wrong; the correct propagation depends on uncertainty semantics and dependence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Measurement uncertainty, Sampling uncertainty, Parameter uncertainty, Model uncertainty, Prediction uncertainty, Epistemic uncertainty, Aleatory variability ... must not automatically be collapsed into one number
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes at least seven kinds of uncertainty that must not be collapsed into one number.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Aleatory variability: Variation inherent in the phenomenon ... Epistemic uncertainty: Uncertainty caused by incomplete knowledge ... Randomness != LackOfKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the aleatory-vs-epistemic distinction with a travel-time/traffic example, giving the principle Randomness != LackOfKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=X+epsilon ... E[epsilon]=0 and Var(epsilon)=sigma^2 ... those assumptions themselves require justification
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a basic measurement-error model and warns its moment assumptions require justification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Y=h(X,theta,epsilon) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the measurement model where available
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes to a measurement model KnowledgeOS should preserve, else downstream models may treat measured values as exact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Var(Y) approx J Sigma J^T ... Jacobian ... covariance matrix ... exposes why independent multiplication of confidence values is inadequate
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes first-order error propagation via the Jacobian and covariance matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cov(X_i,X_j) != 0 ... Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y)+2Cov(X,Y) ... Dependence matters
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes covariance's role in propagation, giving the principle that dependence matters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1 and E_2 both come from the same underlying report. Treating them as independent could artificially increase certainty. This is a major risk in AI systems
b_rows_sample.statement: States the evidence-duplication problem as a major risk in AI systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_1=f(S), E_2=g(S) ... E_1 not-perp E_2 ... combining them as independent evidence is invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes correlated evidence sharing a common source and invalidates treating it as independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance -> DependenceStructure -> CorrectUncertaintyPropagation ... This is a major result
b_rows_sample.statement: States provenance's mathematical role: it enables estimating dependency and hence correct uncertainty propagation, called a major result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H)/P(E) ... prior P(H) and likelihood P(E|H) must have explicit provenance and assumptions
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Bayesian updating and requires explicit provenance/assumptions for prior and likelihood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not every knowledge problem has a meaningful prior ... BayesianUpdate must be a typed operation requiring a valid probabilistic model. It should not be the universal inference engine
b_rows_sample.statement: Constrains Bayesian updating to be a typed operation requiring a valid model, not a universal inference engine.

b_rows_sample.anchor: confidence intervals; sampling distributions; hypothesis tests; bootstrap distributions; asymptotic approximations ... theta-hat +- z SE(theta-hat) ... KnowledgeOS should preserve the framework
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists frequentist uncertainty representations and requires preserving the inferential framework used.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A standard confidence interval [L,U] should not automatically be interpreted as P(L<=theta<=U)=0.95. That interpretation is generally Bayesian, not classical frequentist
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against the common misinterpretation of a frequentist confidence interval as a Bayesian probability statement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [L,U] ... Latency in [100ms,150ms] ... No probability distribution is required
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines interval uncertainty requiring no probability distribution, with a latency example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in S where S is a feasible set ... useful when evidence constrains the possibilities without assigning probabilities
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes interval uncertainty to set-valued uncertainty over a feasible set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X in [0,100] but have no justified distribution. The system should not invent X~Uniform(0,100) ... Bounded != Probabilistically Specified
b_rows_sample.statement: Forbids inventing a uniform distribution over a bounded but unjustified range, giving the principle Bounded != Probabilistically Specified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: theta in Theta_I ... PartiallyIdentified. This is stronger than simply saying uncertain
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces partial identification as a distinct, stronger-than-generic-uncertainty statistical concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10<=X<=20 and Y=2X ... 20<=Y<=40 ... propagated a set-valued constraint without inventing a probability distribution
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example of set-valued constraint propagation without inventing a distribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_1,X_2 -> Y -> Z ... KnowledgeOS should preserve DependencyGraph. Then uncertainty can be propagated through the graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a dependency graph structure for propagating uncertainty through a network.
