b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant I10 — Idempotency ... Register(E) twice. State(Register(E,E)) = State(Register(E)). Otherwise duplicated ingestion could artificially increase evidence. PASS conceptually, assuming stable evidence identity. But that phrase exposes another unresolved problem: How do we determine evidence id
b_rows_sample.statement: Attacks I10 (idempotency, PASS conceptually) but flags the assumption of stable evidence identity as itself an unresolved problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Counterexample candidate #2 — Evidence identity ... Document A: "Nexus version 3.69" and Document B: "Nexus version is 3.69." Are these SameEvidence? Not necessarily. They may be independent; copied; semantically equivalent; derived from the same system; completely unrelated. Therefore EvidenceIdent
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a second genuine counterexample: two textually-similar documents are not automatically the same evidence (five distinct possible relationships), so EvidenceIdentity cannot simply be Hash(Text) — deferred to a later identity-resolution problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant I11 — No hindsight ... this wasn't in the original ten, but the experiment shows it deserves promotion. KnowledgeBasis(D_t)=K_t. Not K_{current}. Attack: Change current knowledge dramatically. Recalculate historical decision. Expected D_t remains unchanged. PASS conceptually.
b_rows_sample.statement: Promotes a new invariant I11 (no hindsight): KnowledgeBasis(D_t)=K_t, never K_current, attacked and PASSing conceptually.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant I12 — World/knowledge independence ... Generate WorldEvent(W_t\rightarrow W_{t+1}) without an observation. Then K_t=K_{t+1}. This must be allowed. Conversely K_t\rightarrow K_{t+1} may occur while W_t=W_{t+1}. This must also be allowed. PASS conceptually. This is one of the foundational pr
b_rows_sample.statement: Promotes invariant I12 (world/knowledge independence, both directions), attacked and PASSing conceptually, called one of the foundational properties of the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant I13 — Revision must not imply falsehood ... A=True then invalidate its only evidence. Correct result: A=Unknown. Not A=False. PASS conceptually. This is especially important for statistical reasoning. ... Invariant I14 — Conflict resolution must preserve history ... Resolution chooses A_2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Promotes invariants I13 (revision must not imply falsehood — Known→Unknown not →False) and I14 (conflict resolution preserves history via Superseded status), both attacked and PASSing conceptually.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now we have discovered two genuine threats ... Threat 1 CircularDependencies. Threat 2 EvidenceIdentity. Both can cause incorrect computation if implemented naively. This is exactly what we wanted from 25A.5.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the two genuine unresolved threats found (CircularDependencies, EvidenceIdentity), explicitly the intended outcome of the falsification exercise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A third threat appears ... A_1\rightarrow A_2\rightarrow A_3\rightarrow A_4 ... with thousands or millions of derived assertions. A single invalidation can cause O(N+M) recomputation. Therefore KnowledgeOS may eventually require dependency indexes; incremental recomputation; cached assessments; affe
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a third threat: at scale, invalidation-driven recomputation could reach O(N+M), requiring eventual indexes/incremental recomputation/caching/subgraph calculation, while deliberately deprioritizing optimization until correctness is established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fourth threat — stale rules ... A_1 was derived under RuleVersion=r_1. Later RuleVersion=r_2. If we recompute A_1, we may obtain a different result. Therefore provenance must eventually include not just evidence, but RuleVersion and potentially ModelVersion. This is extremely important. Knowledge is
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a fourth threat: recomputing a derived assertion under a later rule version can produce a different result, requiring RuleVersion and ModelVersion be part of provenance — knowledge is derived under a computational context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fifth threat — changing ontology ... an assertion was interpreted using ontology version O_1. Later O_2 changes the meaning of an entity or relationship. Then old derived knowledge may need reassessment. Ontology is not merely static metadata. It can become part of epistemic lineage.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a fifth threat: ontology version changes can require reassessing old derived knowledge, meaning ontology is part of epistemic lineage, not static metadata.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sixth threat — source authority changes ... E_1 was supported by an authoritative source. Later that source loses authority. Does the evidence become false? No. But its current applicability may change. Truth\neq Authority and Authority(t) may itself be temporal. This suggests Authority needs tempor
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a sixth threat: a source losing authority does not falsify its prior evidence but changes current applicability, requiring temporal semantics for Authority itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Falsification summary ... Surviving principles: WorldState\neq KnowledgeState, HistoricalKnowledgeImmutable, Unknown preserved, Conflict explicit, LLMOutput\neq Knowledge, Provenance required, TemporalValidity required, Revision explicit, Replayability required, Decision history protected. ... Newly
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates ten surviving principles and six newly discovered requirements (EvidenceIdentity, DependencyCycleHandling, RuleVersionLineage, ModelVersionLineage, OntologyVersionLineage, TemporalAuthority) exposed by the falsification exercise, not yet elevated to bounded contexts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXT-BIOCOMM-2026-09 ... Status: [EXT][RESEARCH LENS] — FROZEN
a_rows_sample.statement: A finalized external research-lens specification (Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens) investigating observable reciprocal interaction sequences in biological systems as a source of structural hypotheses for KnowledgeOS, explicitly NOT treating biology as an implementation of KnowledgeOS; Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no Knowledge Algebra axioms added.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation ≠ Interpretation and Interpretation ≠ Determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: An observed behaviour (e.g. animal A approaching animal B) does not by itself license an interpretive conclusion (e.g. 'A wants X'); any interpretation enters the research pipeline only as an explicitly identified hypothesis.

The fundamental observation unit (actor, observable signal, observable response, temporal position, observable context) forms an ordered, order-sensitive interaction trace, examined at four structural levels: Element, Relation, Sequence, and Contextual interaction (explicitly a research decomposition, not a KnowledgeOS kernel-level claim).

a_rows_sample.anchor: B → A(B) → S(A) → KOS(S)
a_rows_sample.statement: A four-layer 'defensive translation architecture' (biological observation -> abstract directed-graph structure -> multi-agent software analogue -> KnowledgeOS evaluation) is required before any KnowledgeOS construct (state transformation, preservation, eliminability, hypothesis transitions, determination, decision stability, historical divergence) may be applied, to prevent biological terminology from silently becoming KnowledgeOS ontology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T,Π}(S;D) ⟺ Π(T(D)) = Π(T(E_S(D))) ... an apparently insignificant event can become indispensable when the preservation contract changes.
a_rows_sample.statement: Zero is explicitly not assigned biologically (ignored != Zero, rejected != non-Zero); it is evaluated only after the transformation and preservation contract (Pi_1 immediate state, Pi_2 terminal outcome, Pi_3 targeted historical provenance, which must not silently become 'preserve everything') are specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 — Non-Elementarity ... R6 — Historical Divergence
a_rows_sample.statement: Six frozen research questions with explicit witness conditions and explicit non-overclaim caveats: whether element-level Zero determines sequence-level Zero (R1), order sensitivity of Zero under segment exchange (R2), contract-relative Zero for the same element (R3), hypothesis-space dynamics after a response (R4, sign of change not predetermined), decision stability despite unresolved causal hypothesis (R5, explicitly not to be read as biological rationality/intentionality), and whether different interaction histories can converge on the same terminal state (R6, testing TerminalStateEquivalence not implying HistoricalEquivalence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The following substitutions are prohibited unless independently justified: Signal⇒Intent, Silence⇒Rejection, Approach⇒Desire, Withdrawal⇒Refusal, Response⇒Acceptance, Behaviour⇒Knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: An explicit anti-anthropomorphism rule and a companion anti-leakage rule (no biological observation may directly become a KnowledgeOS axiom; [EXT]->[PROP] does not imply [PROP]->[CORE]) bound the lens as behavioural-structural rather than a theory of animal mental states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not immediately create another theory document. ... Lens Freeze → Pre-registration → O-F* → Synthetic Witness Generator → Controls → Execution → Adjudication
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 as the next artifact — a pre-registration plus synthetic witness generator running the R1-R6 tests on controlled synthetic traces first, biological examples serving only as structural inspiration, explicitly citing the O-F* protocol as part of the required execution order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) ... observable signal != semantic message ... response != epistemic acceptance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the primitive biological interaction event e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) (sender, observable signal/behavior, observable receiver response, temporal position, context) and an ordered interaction episode C^{t:n}=[e_1,...,e_n], with the explicit boundary that observable signal != semantic message and response != epistemic acceptance until later interpretation layers assign meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: B -> A(B) -> S(A) -> KOS(S) ... This prevents animal behavior -> KnowledgeOS primitive from happening implicitly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer interpretation pipeline B (biological observation) -> A(B) (abstract structure, e.g. G=(V,E)) -> S(A) (software analogue trace) -> KOS(S) (KnowledgeOS evaluation of Zero, H, Determination, Decision, State Transition), explicitly to prevent animal-behavior-to-KnowledgeOS-primitive inference from happening implicitly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: absence of observed response != knowledge of rejection ... response classification != epistemic classification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues non-response (R_B=empty_observed following A's signal M) must not be inferred as 'B ignored M'; the hypothesis space instead includes not-perceived, perceived-but-no-response, response-outside-observation-channel, environmental-constraint, competing-behavior, etc., giving 'absence of observed response != knowledge of rejection' and, symmetrically for opposing responses, 'response classification != epistemic classification.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 Non-elementarity ... R2 Order sensitivity ... R3 Contract relativity ... R4 Hypothesis-space transformation ... R5 Decision stability ... R6 History divergence
a_rows_sample.statement: Reduces the lens's prior five research questions to six (R1 non-elementarity, R2 order sensitivity, R3 contract relativity, R4 hypothesis-space transformation measuring both |H_{t+1}|-|H_t| and the transition relation R without assuming direction, R5 decision stability, R6 history divergence K1~=K2 while Hist1 not-equiv_{Pi_prov} Hist2), and specifies what the lens MAY generate (candidate operators/distinctions/algebraic properties, counterexamples, DDD vocabulary) versus MAY NOT establish (axioms, kernel membership, truth conditions, universal animal intentions, mathematical laws via metaphor).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Graph != Knowledge State != Knowledge Algebra. ... I would replace the old name "Courtship Signalling Lens" with Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates Knowledge Graph (representation of the interaction) from Knowledge State from Knowledge Algebra (what can legitimately be concluded from the graph), and renames the lens from 'Courtship Signalling Lens' to 'Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens', treating courtship as its first experimental domain rather than its definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Yes. I would rewrite it as a Biological Communication Research Lens, rather than a "courtship metaphor."
a_rows_sample.statement: This file duplicates S2826's 'Biological Communication Research Lens' content verbatim, and duplicates it again within itself; it contributes no content beyond what S2826 already records (observation event e_i, B->A(B)->S(A)->KOS(S) pipeline, non-response boundary, R1-R6, renaming to Biological Reciprocal Communication Lens).

a_rows_sample.anchor: e_i = (A_i, sigma_i, O_i, t_i, C_i) ... Hypothesis formulation H occurs only inside the explicit interpretation layer (Interpretation(sigma_i, O_i, C_i) -> H)
a_rows_sample.statement: De-biologizes the observation unit from e_i=(S_i,M_i,R_i,t_i,C_i) to e_i=(A_i,sigma_i,O_i,t_i,C_i) (observed actor, observable signal, observable response, time, context), explicitly isolating observables and requiring hypothesis formulation H to occur only inside an explicit interpretation layer Interpretation(sigma_i,O_i,C_i)->H, to protect KnowledgeOS primitives from assumed intentions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 (Non-Elementarity) ... R2 (Order Sensitivity vs. Non-Commutativity) ... R3 (Contract Relativity) ... R4 (Hypothesis Dynamics) ... R5 (Action Stability) ... R6 (Historical Identity)
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents refined R1-R6 witness criteria: R1 tests z(C1)=z(C2) and Zero(C1)!=Zero(C2); R2 formally bounds Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) as an observational order witness, not intrinsic algebraic non-commutativity; R3 tests Pi2 (terminal) vs Pi3 (provenance-preserving) contracts to show Outcome Equivalence != Historical Equivalence; R4 bounds Delta|H| in {<0,=0,>0} without assuming a direction; R5 replaces 'epistemic closure' with policy invariance |H_Q|>1 and |pi(H_Q)|=1; R6 tests T(K0,C1)=T(K0,C2) with Hist(C1) not-equiv_{Pi3} Hist(C2).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would change the wording in R3 ... to: A positive witness establishes, within the tested domain, that eliminability varies with preservation contract. Likewise R6
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects R3's and R6's overclaiming wording ('proves that eliminability varies by preservation contract'; 'establishes that state equivalence does not imply historical identity') to witness-relative statements ('a positive witness establishes, within the tested domain/representation/provenance contract, that ...'), preserving the distinction between an experimental witness and a universal theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Element => Relation => Sequence => History ... information sufficient at one level may be insufficient at the next.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that Knowledge Algebra may have a structure where Element does not imply Relation does not imply Sequence does not imply History: Z1=[Zero(e1),Zero(e2),...] might not determine Z2=Zero(e1,e2), which might not determine Z3=Zero(C^{t:n}), which itself might not determine historical provenance; connects this directly to prior Zero-algebra results where group/sequence Zero could not reliably be inferred from singleton Zero, while noting the biological lens does not itself establish this, only provides an independent test domain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Biological Lens Principle: Biological reciprocal interaction is used as an external generator of observable relational, sequential, and historical structures. No biological interpretation is promoted into KnowledgeOS semantics unless it survives explicit abstraction, formalization, and independent capability testing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Freezes the 'Biological Lens Principle': biological reciprocal interaction is used only as an external generator of observable relational/sequential/historical structures, and no biological interpretation is promoted into KnowledgeOS semantics unless it survives explicit abstraction, formalization, and independent capability testing; the research chain is Biological Observation -> Abstract Structure -> Software Realization -> KnowledgeOS Experiment -> Witness -> Independent Replication, never Biology -> KnowledgeOS Axiom directly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G_t = representational structure ... K_t = epistemic state ... Theta = state transformation ... with Zero evaluating preservation
a_rows_sample.statement: Ties the biological interaction graph representation to existing architecture by distinguishing G_t (representational structure, what is connected) from K_t (epistemic state) from Theta (state transformation), with Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) evaluating preservation across them; the graph tells us what is connected, KnowledgeOS machinery determines what those connections mean epistemically.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0_i != empty != Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) unless a later experiment establishes a structure-preserving correspondence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that algebraic zero (0_i in D_i with x (+)_i 0_i = x), epistemic absence/omission (k_i=empty or not represented), and preservation-relative Zero (Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D)))) are three distinct notions that must not be identified unless a structure-preserving correspondence is demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_S^restrict(K): a dimension-truncating operation ... P_S^0(K): an ambient-preserving projection mapping ... k_i -> 0_i for i not in S.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes restriction P_S^restrict(K): product_i D_i -> product_{i in S} D_i (changes ambient dimensionality) from zero projection P_S^0(K): product_i D_i -> product_i D_i (ambient-preserving, mapping k_i to 0_i for i not in S); testing whether P_S^restrict(K) equiv P_S^0(K) under an observational query Q determines whether epistemic silence can be faithfully modeled by an algebraic zero element.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HZ_1 (Identity Law) ... HZ_2 (Projection Idempotence) ... HZ_3 (Projection Intersection) ... HZ_4 (Restriction Equivalence) ... HZ_5 (Resolution Atomicity) ... HZ_6 (Emergent Observational Relevance)
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the original six hypotheses for the initial 'KR-ZOOM-01 (Algebraic Zero & Recursive Zoom)' protocol: HZ1 identity law x(+)_i 0_i=x; HZ2 idempotence P_S^0(P_S^0(K))=P_S^0(K); HZ3 intersection P_S^0(P_T^0(K))=P_{S∩T}^0(K); HZ4 restriction equivalence Obs_Q(P_S^0(K)) equiv Obs_Q(P_S^restrict(K)); HZ5 resolution atomicity (an irreducible x_r expands to a nested space with k>1 dimensions on zoom); HZ6 emergent observational relevance (a dimension Zero under query Q_r maps to a nested dimension non-Zero under Q_{r+1}).

b_rows_sample.anchor: HZ1 should become: HZ1 -- Domain Algebra Existence ... Does a tested knowledge-domain representation admit a composition operation (+)_i and distinguished element 0_i satisfying an empirically and semantically justified identity law?
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects HZ1 from an assumed identity law x(+)_i0_i=x to an open existence question: does a tested knowledge-domain representation admit a composition operation and distinguished element satisfying an empirically and semantically justified identity law, since algebra must be discovered from behaviour, not imposed on the problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_S^0P_T^0 =? P_T^0P_S^0. Do not assume commutativity merely because the notation suggests it.
b_rows_sample.statement: HZ2/HZ3 are corrected to be recognized as properties of a specific constructed coordinate-zeroing operator rather than discovered KnowledgeOS properties (risk of circularity), and the intersection test HZ3 must also explicitly test order (P_S^0 P_T^0 =? P_T^0 P_S^0) rather than assuming commutativity from notation, especially given the corpus's existing order-sensitivity findings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Atomic_r(x) does not imply Atomic_{r+1}(Z_r(x)). ... x_r in D^(r) is representation-atomic under the current resolution, while a refinement map Z_r ... may expose a richer structure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects HZ5 to avoid conflating atomicity of representation with atomicity of knowledge: x_r is representation-atomic under the current resolution, while a refinement map Z_r:D^(r)->K^(r+1) may expose a richer structure, giving Atomic_r(x) does not imply Atomic_{r+1}(Z_r(x)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would call this: Resolution-relative eliminability rather than "Zero alteration." Because nothing has changed about Zero itself. The carrier and inquiry have changed
b_rows_sample.statement: Renames HZ6's phenomenon from 'Zero alteration' to 'resolution-relative eliminability': Zero itself is unchanged, only the carrier and inquiry have changed ((D^(r),Q_r,Pi_r) -> (D^(r+1),Q_{r+1},Pi_{r+1})), giving Zero_r(x) does not imply Zero_{r+1}(x').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Algebra <-> Zoom/Resolution <-> Biological Reciprocal Communication ... none of the three gets to dictate the others.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a triangle of three mutually-informing but non-dictating research programmes: Zero Algebra (eliminability tests), Zoom/Resolution (resolution changes), and Biological Reciprocal Communication (relational sequences), all evaluated through Knowledge Theory's epistemic semantics and contracts, with none entitled to define the KnowledgeOS kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HZ1-HZ6 should be treated as candidate hypotheses, not as a package whose truth is expected to converge toward an algebra. ... HZ4 should be the first experiment
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the framing of HZ1-HZ6: they are candidate hypotheses, not a package expected to converge toward a proven algebra; HZ4 (does P_S^0 faithfully mimic P_S^restrict under O_{Q,Pi}) is designated the first, gating experiment because it tests the bridge between representational omission and algebraic zeroing -- if it fails, HZ1-HZ3 may still hold for some domain but cannot model KnowledgeOS omission without additional structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO-RESOLUTION-2026-09 ... Status [PROP][OPEN][RESEARCH ARTIFACT] ... Objective: Test whether three notions can be related: AlgebraicZero <-> RepresentationalOmission <-> PreservationZero without assuming their equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the artifact KR-ZERO-RESOLUTION-2026-09 (status [PROP][OPEN][RESEARCH ARTIFACT], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no new algebraic axioms), replacing the earlier draft's reuse of the 'KR-ZOOM-01' ID which collided with the pre-existing distinct KR-ZOOM-01 experiment; its objective is to test whether AlgebraicZero, RepresentationalOmission, and PreservationZero can be related without assuming their equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 -- HZ4 first ... Phase 2 -- test the projection algebra ... Phase 3 -- domain algebra ... Phase 4 -- recursive resolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Lays out a four-phase execution architecture: Phase 1 tests HZ4 (O_{Q,Pi}(P_S^0(K)) =? O_{Q,Pi}(P_S^restr(K))), proceeding to Phase 2 (HZ2 idempotence, HZ3 intersection AND order P_S^0 P_T^0 =? P_T^0 P_S^0) only if Phase 1 survives; Phase 3 tests HZ1 domain-algebra existence as a control independent of KnowledgeOS (could show domain algebra valid while Algebraic Zero != KnowledgeOS Zero); Phase 4 tests the recursive Zoom hypothesis x^(r) -Z-> K_x^(r+1), asking whether Zero_r(x)=1 can coexist with exists x' in K_x^(r+1): Zero_{r+1}(x')=0, correctly interpreted as 'a preservation judgment at resolution r does not necessarily determine preservation judgments over the refined carrier at resolution r+1', not 'Zero becoming non-Zero.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: At coarse resolution C^(r)=[sigma_1,rho_1,sigma_2,rho_2] might be eliminable ... Zooming in ... can expose distinctions that were invisible at the coarse level. Therefore Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the resolution-relative-eliminability idea to a concrete courtship-sequence example: at coarse resolution the sequence [sigma1,rho1,sigma2,rho2] might be eliminable with respect to a terminal-state inquiry, while a finer resolution exposing orientation/distance/timing/repeated-approach/avoidance can reveal distinctions invisible at the coarse level, giving both Zero^(r)(C)=1 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=1 and its converse Zero^(r)(C)=0 does not imply Zero^(r+1)(C)=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HZ6 tests whether eliminability changes across resolution levels under explicitly paired carriers and preservation contracts. Because the experiment can falsify HZ6. It cannot start by saying it proves it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the document's assertive framing ('HZ6 proves eliminability changes with carrier & contract scale') to a testable, falsifiable framing ('HZ6 tests whether eliminability changes across resolution levels under explicitly paired carriers and preservation contracts'), and similarly corrects HZ4's framing from a universal determination claim to a claim relative to the tested carrier/transformation/observation/inquiry/contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: primitive inputs ──①──► assertion/proposition ──②──► knowledge state ──③──► transformation ──④──► resulting state ──⑤──► invariants ──⑥──► assessment/validation ──⑦──► governance/authority ──⑧──► observable evidence ... Six of eight arrows are closed and executed. The chain breaks at ⑥.
a_rows_sample.statement: An eight-arrow dependency chain from primitive inputs to observable evidence is interrogated arrow by arrow: arrows 1-5 (proposition/assertion typing, knowledge-state construction, transformation signature, resulting-state closure/determinism/congruence, invariants) are YES/executed; arrow 6 (Assessment with Policy semantics) is NO (gap G-2); arrow 7 (governance/authority) is YES for the Gamma value set but only partially modeled for authority; arrow 8 (observation-to-evidence qualification) is PARTIAL (gap G-4) — six of eight arrows are closed and executed, and the chain breaks precisely at Assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-1 | What is Σ? | a signed ordinal scale, or Q14's vector, or neither | ... OPEN — both candidates refuted on different axes ... BLOCKING
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-1 (BLOCKING): the formal shape of epistemic status Sigma is undetermined — both the signed-ordinal-scale candidate and Q14's five-dimensional vector candidate have been refuted on different axes; status is derived on every read, so the wrong shape corrupts every assessment; resolution route is to derive it from a policy-parameterised assessment once G-2 closes, tested by a 10-case audit re-run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-2 | What is a Policy, formally? | Policy as a mathematical object: how it maps an evidence set to a support level | Assessment is well-typed but uncomputable without it; G-1 depends on it ... knowledge-schema.yaml IS an executing policy — a model exists ... BLOCKING
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-2 (BLOCKING, and the root blocker): Policy has no formal mathematical definition (how it maps an evidence set to a support level), leaving Assessment well-typed but uncomputable, and G-1 depends on it; the running EKP's knowledge-schema.yaml is noted to already BE an executing policy, giving an existing model to generalise from; resolution route is generalising from the EKP's schema-as-policy, tested by running assessment under at least two policies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-3 | What is uncertainty? | a representation; no (Ω,ℱ,P) in 1468 files | step 246 asserts KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution with no measurable space ... OPEN — leaning DROP
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-3 (not blocking): no measure-theoretic uncertainty representation (Omega,F,P) exists anywhere across 1468 files despite step 246 asserting 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution'; step 199.19 rules out a scalar representation; Sigma already works without it; verdict leans toward DROPPING the probabilistic claim unless a derivation of (Omega,F,P) is produced, with an ordinal scale possibly sufficing instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-4 | When does an observation become evidence? | the qualification predicate in Evidence = QualifiedObservation | 253 names the concept; nothing says what qualifies ... EvidenceSet (other BC) requires non-blank, non-duplicate refs — a partial rule ... OPEN
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-4 (not blocking): step 253 names Evidence=QualifiedObservation but never specifies the qualification predicate itself; a separate bounded context's EvidenceSet independently supplies a partial rule (non-blank, non-duplicate references); resolution route is deriving the full predicate from the EKP plus EvidenceSet's discipline, tested by injecting an unqualified observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-5 | Is Q (epistemic qualification) inside K? | a decision procedure between two consistent normalisations | Claude derives external; step 253 puts it inside ... falsifier exists: does stored status diverge from recomputed? ... OPEN — genuinely undecided
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-5 (not blocking, but flagged as the one candidate that may become genuinely normative): whether epistemic qualification Q belongs inside K has two mutually consistent normalisations (one external-derivation model, step 253's inside-K model) with no decision procedure between them; a concrete falsifier exists (does stored status ever diverge from recomputed status?), so it is treated as an empirical question first, deferred to artifact I test 12 rather than escalated to the human prematurely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-6 | Acyclicity of supersedes | none — theorem proven; implementation does not enforce it | a cycle makes "which is current?" undefined ... EKP circular_dependency is a warning over requires/depends_on only ... PROVEN ... NOT CONFORMANT ... ACTIONABLE ENGINEERING FIX
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-6 (not blocking, but an ACTIONABLE ENGINEERING FIX): the acyclicity-of-supersedes theorem is PROVEN, but the EKP's circular_dependency check is only a warning scoped to requires/depends_on, leaving supersession cycles unenforced (currently vacuous, 0 edges); resolution is to extend the lint rule and raise its severity, tested by closing a supersession cycle and re-running lint.

a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-7 (not blocking): the retract operation is found to break step 254's own commuting-square adequacy criterion F-compose-That = T-compose-F, evidenced by both a corpus citation (step 254) and an independently executed cascade-lossiness demonstration; the recommended resolution is to adopt an append-only model with tombstones (matching a separate ReplayAssertion immutability invariant) rather than excluding retract outright, tested by a commuting-square test specifically on retract.

a_rows_sample.statement: Second final-gate verdict, on empirical conformance: PARTIALLY ENGINEERINGALLY CONFORMANT; the mathematical-completeness verdict (FORMALLY INCOMPLETE) and the engineering-conformance verdict are deliberately kept separate and not collapsed into one score, since the theory is mathematically more complete than the EKP implements, while the EKP enforces more governance invariants than the theory currently has — neither representation dominates the other.

A Value can exist in KnowledgeOS without being a numerical measurement. ... prevents the theory from making the earlier dangerous leap: Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Representation-theorem principle: a measurement is a structure-preserving homomorphism from a relational system into a numerical (or other) representation, so Measurement != Value — a KnowledgeOS Value can exist without being a numerical measurement at all; this directly blocks the earlier dangerous claim 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution', already separately contested (gap G-3) because no underlying probability space (Omega,F,P) exists in the corpus.

a_rows_sample.statement: Direct, load-bearing consequence for the epistemic-status gap (G-1): since the audit's surviving epistemic 'strength' component is ordinal with no interval structure, averaging, summing, or weighted combination of strength values (e.g. (Strength1+Strength2)/2) is formally inadmissible regardless of computational convenience — the scale semantics, not ease of implementation, must authorize any such operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VALUE-SPACE SEMANTICS: SUBSTANTIALLY ESTABLISHED. ... Type(D)→Φ_D→Meaningfulness_D→AllowedOperations_D. ... Q14's classification of Version as Interval should not currently be promoted as mathematically valid. ... the theory's remaining blockers are now Σ, Assurance, Uncertainty, and Assessment/poli
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 264 verdict: VALUE-SPACE SEMANTICS SUBSTANTIALLY ESTABLISHED, with the mathematical chain Type(D) -> admissible transformations Phi_D -> Meaningfulness_D -> AllowedOperations_D as the central result; the corrective note that Version-as-Interval should not be promoted as mathematically valid is retained; the broader audit is cited as identifying the theory's remaining blockers as Sigma, Assurance, Uncertainty, and Assessment/policy semantics — no longer the basic P=(E,D,V) construction, which is now considered essentially settled.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy : K × Context → Criterion | REJECTED — makes a policy state-dependent ... Policy : Observation → Decision | REJECTED — skips proposition, evidence and authority; conflates policy with decision ... Policy : Claim × Evidence × Context → Assessment | REJECTED as the TYPE — this is the signature
a_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate Policy signatures are eliminated with executed reasoning: Policy:K x Context->Criterion is rejected because it makes policy state-dependent and unversionable/unauditable; Policy:Observation->Decision is rejected for skipping proposition/evidence/authority and conflating policy with decision (already refuted at corpus steps 202/206); Policy:Claim x Evidence x Context->Assessment is rejected as confusing Policy with Assessment's own signature (Assessment takes a Policy as a parameter); and 'Policy = a set of predicates' is subsumed by (not wrong, just incomplete versus) the Rules component, since it omits temporal applicability and unknown-handling.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy = (id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior) ... Gates : SET of three-valued predicates g : Decision → {True, False, Unknown} ... ValidityInterval : [vf, vt) ... ResolutionBehavior : Unknown → Block | Allow ... Apply(p,d) = False if ∃g∈p.Gates: g(d)=False ← strict conjunction,
a_rows_sample.statement: The derived canonical Policy type: Policy=(id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior), where Gates is a set of three-valued predicates over a Decision, ValidityInterval is a half-open temporal window, and ResolutionBehavior maps Unknown to Block or Allow; the Apply function is a strict three-valued conjunction over Gates (False if any gate is False, ResolutionBehavior(Unknown) if any gate is Unknown and none is False, True otherwise, with no averaging), and Applicable(p,t) checks temporal membership in the validity interval — this directly answers gap G-2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy was never undefined. It is defined at step 57.47 as a three-component tuple, and its evaluation semantics are defined at step 42.9 and IMPLEMENTED in an executable reference file that I ran successfully. The blocker was a coverage failure, not an absence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding reframing gap G-2: Policy was never conceptually undefined in the corpus — its type (step 57.47) and its evaluation semantics (step 42.9) both already exist, the latter already implemented in an executable reference file; the true blocker was a coverage failure (the definitions not yet being found and run), not an actual absence of a Policy formalization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the measurement regime belongs to the Dimension, not to the numerical representation of an individual Value. ... What mathematical structure does V_D carry, and which operations on its values are actually legitimate? This is where the theory moves from a typed proposition to a typed measurement sema
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 264 narrows Step 263's typed-proposition result to a measurement-semantics question: since the measurement regime belongs to the Dimension rather than to an individual Value's numeric representation, the task is to determine what mathematical structure V_D carries and which operations on it are legitimate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V_D={v1,v2,v3,…} ... principal value-space types: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio, Boolean, Text, Complex. Type(D) determines the mathematical meaning of V_D.
b_rows_sample.statement: Canonical value-space definition: V_D is a set of admissible values typed by one of seven principal value-space categories (Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio, Boolean, Text, Complex); the dimension's type, not the machine representation, determines V_D's mathematical meaning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MachineType(v) ≠ MeasurementScale(D). ... requires a representation theorem plus a uniqueness theorem for a measurement quantity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Foundational invariant: a value's machine/storage type (e.g. float, string) never determines its measurement scale type; the corpus's measurement research requires a representation theorem and a uniqueness theorem to establish a genuine measurement quantity, distinguishing numerical representation from quantitative measurement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nominal ... admissible transformations are arbitrary one-to-one mappings ... Ordinal ... admissible transformations are strictly monotone ... Interval ... φ(x)=αx+β, α>0 ... differences preserved up to scale ... ratios are not invariant ... Ratio ... φ(x)=αx, α>0 ... ratios are invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: The four core measurement scales are formally defined by their admissible-transformation groups and preserved structure: Nominal (arbitrary bijections; only equality/classification preserved, e.g. Red!=Blue meaningful but Red<Blue is not), Ordinal (strictly monotone transformations; ordering preserved, e.g. Low<Medium<High, but differences not generally meaningful), Interval (phi(x)=ax+b, a>0; differences preserved up to scale but ratios are not invariant because they depend on b), Ratio (phi(x)=ax, a>0; ratios are invariant because the zero point is fixed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus also contains Absolute, Log-Interval and Difference scales in the broader Roberts-based treatment. Therefore we should not silently collapse the complete measurement framework to only four scales.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit warning against collapsing the measurement framework to only the four Q14 scales (Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio): the broader corpus measurement research (Roberts-based) additionally contains Absolute, Log-Interval, and Difference scales.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Meaningful_D(S) ⟺ ∀φ∈Φ_D: Truth(S)=Truth(φ(S)). The corpus states this explicitly as Roberts' definition of meaningfulness. This is much stronger than simply saying 'This number looks reasonable.' It gives KnowledgeOS a formal criterion for permitted reasoning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Roberts' meaningfulness criterion is adopted as KnowledgeOS's formal test for legitimate measurement-based reasoning: a statement S about measured values is meaningful for dimension D iff its truth value is invariant under every admissible transformation phi in Phi_D — replacing informal plausibility judgments with a formal invariance criterion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AllowedOperations(D) = f(ScaleType(D)). ... Ordinal: allowed <,>,=; not generally allowed +,-,×,/,average. Interval: allowed -,average under common scale; x/y not generally meaningful. Ratio: allowed -,+,×,/ subject to domain/unit constraints. The corpus explicitly requires KnowledgeOS to forbid or
b_rows_sample.statement: Architecture rule: the operations allowed on a value are a function of its dimension's scale type, not of its representation — ordinal permits comparison but not arithmetic/averaging, interval permits subtraction/averaging under a common scale but not division, ratio permits the full arithmetic set subject to unit constraints; KnowledgeOS is required to forbid or flag scale-illegitimate operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ValidOperation(D,o) as a deterministic predicate. ... ValidOperation(D_Confidence,×) may be false if ScaleType(D_Confidence)=Ordinal. ... an attempted inference can produce NOT_APPLICABLE rather than a numerically computed but semantically invalid result. This aligns directly with the corpus's Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: ValidOperation(D,o) is defined as a deterministic predicate over a dimension and an operation, illustrated by multiplication on an ordinal Confidence dimension being invalid — allowing an attempted inference to correctly return NOT_APPLICABLE rather than a numerically computed but semantically meaningless result, aligning with the corpus's Zero Lens boundary-condition discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RepresentationType(D) and ScaleType(D). For Version: RepresentationType=String/StructuredVersion while ScaleType=Ordinal is the proposed semantic interpretation. ... Type(D) cannot be reduced to programming-language type.
b_rows_sample.statement: A dimension's RepresentationType (its storage/syntactic form, e.g. String/StructuredVersion for Version) is distinguished from its ScaleType (its measurement semantics, e.g. proposed Ordinal for Version) — a dimension's semantic Type cannot be reduced to a programming-language type.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Length=3m and Length=300cm. These have different representations but can denote the same physical quantity. Therefore we need Unit(D) or an equivalent dimensional semantics. ... semantic equality cannot always be v1=v2 as raw representations. We may require v1≡_D v2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Units are identified as a further semantic layer beyond scale type: 3m and 300cm are different raw representations of the same physical quantity, requiring a Unit(D)/dimensional-semantics component and a value-level semantic equivalence v1 equiv_D v2 distinct from raw structural equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1 =_str v2 ... v1 ≡_D v2. Structural equality means identical representation. Semantic equality means equivalence under the semantics of dimension D. Example: 3m ≠_str 300cm but 3m ≡_D 300cm. This distinction must propagate to proposition equality: P1=(E,D,v1) and P2=(E,D,v2). They may be structura
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural value equality (identical representation, e.g. 3m !=_str 300cm) is formally distinguished from semantic value equality under a dimension's normalization semantics (3m equiv_D 300cm), and this distinction is required to propagate up to proposition equality: two propositions with the same entity and dimension but structurally different values can still be semantically equivalent propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WF(P) ⟺ E∈𝓔 ∧ D∈𝓓 ∧ V∈V_D ∧ SemanticValid_D(V). The first three conjuncts are corpus-established. The final formulation is a derived refinement, not yet a corpus theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Well-formedness is refined to add a fourth conjunct, SemanticValid_D(V) (the value belongs to the dimension's declared semantic value space, not merely something the programming language accepts), explicitly flagged as a derived refinement rather than an already-proven corpus theorem.

For example, semantic versions such as 3.10 and
b_rows_sample.statement: The 'most important adversarial test' of the step: Q14's classification of Version as Interval would license a meaningless difference (3.69-3.68=0.01) and conflicts with the fact that semantic-version ordering (3.10 succeeds 3.9) disagrees with naive decimal ordering — Version must not be treated as an ordinary real number.

b_rows_sample.statement: Recommended resolution of the Version-scale dispute: Version=StructuredOrdinal (ordering meaningful under semantic-version precedence, but differences not), explicitly classified as a verifier recommendation, not yet a corpus-established correction, since the corpus's own Q14 material still classifies Version as Interval.

b_rows_sample.statement: Representation-theorem principle: a measurement is a structure-preserving homomorphism from a relational system into a numerical (or other) representation, so Measurement != Value — a KnowledgeOS Value can exist without being a numerical measurement at all; this directly blocks the earlier dangerous claim 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution', already separately contested (gap G-3) because no underlying probability space (Omega,F,P) exists in the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the kernel should preserve: relational system; sufficient structure for measurement; historical records; context and regime; scale-type information; perfect-substitute relations. But it should not preserve as primitive kernel structure: measurements themselves; scale values generated by regimes; adm
b_rows_sample.statement: Kernel-design implication drawn from measurement theory: the kernel should preserve the underlying relational system, sufficient structure to support future measurement, historical records, context/regime, scale-type information, and perfect-substitute relations, but should NOT preserve as primitive kernel structure the measurements themselves, regime-generated scale values, admissible transformations, or meaningfulness judgments — these are derived, not stored.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D=(id,name,domain,V_D,σ) where σ is the measurement/scale structure. ... σ∈{Nominal,Ordinal,Interval,Ratio,…}. This does not mean σ is an additional component of the proposition. It remains metadata/structure of the Dimension.
b_rows_sample.statement: Dimension is refined to a five-field candidate object D=(id,name,domain,V_D,sigma), where sigma is the measurement/scale-structure tag (Nominal/Ordinal/Interval/Ratio/...); sigma is explicitly Dimension metadata, not an additional field of the Proposition triple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Meaningful_D(Q) iff ∀φ∈Φ_D: Q(v1,...,vn) ⟺ Q(φ(v1),...,φ(vn)). This gives a precise mathematical foundation for 'Is this reasoning legitimate?' rather than merely 'Can the software execute this operation?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Meaningfulness is generalized from single statements to arbitrary n-ary predicates over values: a predicate Q is meaningful for dimension D iff its truth value is invariant under every admissible transformation in Phi_D — reframing 'is this reasoning legitimate' as a precise mathematical question distinct from mere executability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus gives confidence as a candidate quantity whose scale may be ordinal or interval depending on the declared regime. ... The meaning of a value is not intrinsic to its label. It depends on the declared dimension and measurement regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked confidence example: whether C(A)>C(B) or C(A)=2*C(B) is meaningful depends entirely on whether Confidence is declared ordinal or ratio — establishing that a value's meaning is never intrinsic to its label alone, only to its declared dimension and measurement regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would add the Sanskrit/Paninian lens — but I would not turn it into a fifth constitutional ARB lens. ... strengthening semantic identity, transformation, reasoning representation, and AI interpretation rather than introducing a new constitutional dimension.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit governance decision to keep the ARB decision four-dimensional (Ganesha/Leonardo/Krishna/Shani) while adding Paninian and Topology as diagnostic-only supporting lenses, not new voting dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore add Zero as a foundational lens ... but I would put Zero first. ZERO -> GANESHA -> LEONARDO -> KRISHNA -> PANINI -> TOPOLOGY -> SHANI.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finalizes the review sequence into seven lenses with Zero placed first, ahead of the previously-established four ARB lenses (Ganesha/Leonardo/Krishna/Shani) and the diagnostic Panini/Topology lenses: Zero observes first, then define/discover/justify/model-transformation/analyze-structure/establish-invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pramana lens: By what legitimate epistemic route did we arrive at this claim? That last lens fills an important hole.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates ten accumulated research lenses each with a defining question (Dhatu: what transformation/process generates the expression; Zero: what invariant remains after representation changes; Ganesha: is the concept actually clear; Leonardo: what assumptions/alternatives remain hidden; Krishna: why does this knowledge matter and what decision does it support; Shani: what must never become false; Consciousness: how does perception become interpretation/self-understanding; Temporal: how does the knowledge state change over time; Hofstadter: can the system represent/reason about its own knowledge; Pramana: by what legitimate epistemic route did we arrive at this claim), identifying Pramana as filling a gap the other nine left open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The article's broader claims ... are the author's polemical interpretation, not something we should absorb into our KnowledgeOS epistemology. ... PRIMARY/STRONG ... SECONDARY ... NOT IMPORT ... that discipline is itself an application of the Pramana + Shani + Leonardo lenses
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the source article's civilizational/religious-superiority and 'ancient texts contain modern physics' claims, retaining only the pramana taxonomy, epistemic pathways, debate structure, and evidence-vs-assertion distinction, sorted into PRIMARY/STRONG, SECONDARY, and NOT-IMPORT tiers; identifies this filtering discipline itself as an application of the Pramana + Shani + Leonardo lenses, calling it possibly the most important methodological lesson of the file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKI-1 Evidence integrity ... EKI-7 Authority separation ... much closer to the constitutional invariants we have already been designing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Shani lens ('what must never become false?') to derive seven epistemic invariants: EKI-1 Evidence integrity (a claim cannot strengthen without corresponding evidence), EKI-2 Provenance integrity (every claim retains how it was obtained), EKI-3 Temporal integrity (a current claim cannot rewrite its historical validity), EKI-4 Refutability (an empirically-testable claim must expose what could falsify it), EKI-5 Uncertainty preservation (lack of evidence cannot silently become certainty), EKI-6 Perspective separation (interpretation cannot be stored as observation), EKI-7 Authority separation (authority cannot substitute for evidence where empirical verification is required); stated to be close to the project's existing constitutional invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ScientificMethod ≠ Science ... Evidence ≠ Knowledge ... Knowledge ≠ Certainty
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Ganesha lens ('what exactly are we talking about?') to the source's terminology (science, scientific method, empirical evidence, knowledge, belief, religious doctrine, scriptural testimony, direct experience, refutation, truth), asserting three essential non-collapses: ScientificMethod != Science, Evidence != Knowledge, Knowledge != Certainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not ingest those claims as facts merely because the article says them. ... The article becomes evidence about an author's interpretation, not automatically evidence for every historical claim it makes.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Leonardo lens to the source's own comparative claim (that Abrahamic religions treat scripture as unquestionable while Hindu traditions permit open refutation), refusing to ingest it as fact; instead treats the claim itself as CLAIM->source=author->epistemic status=secondary interpretation->requires independent verification, presented as a live demonstration of the system being built.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim -> Method of knowing -> Evidence -> Verification -> Challenge -> Revision ... The domain changes. The epistemic mechanism remains.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Krishna lens ('why are we studying this?') to conclude the source contributes a domain-independent epistemic operating model (Claim->Method of knowing->Evidence->Verification->Challenge->Revision) applicable across engineering, scientific, organizational, AI-generated, architectural-decision, governance and historical knowledge -- the domain changes but the epistemic mechanism remains.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic uncertainty ≠ permission to destroy provenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates the Shani lens for multi-valued logic: asks which invariants must hold regardless of epistemic state, giving the example that every claim must preserve its evidence provenance whether the claim is true/false/both/undetermined, formalized as 'epistemic uncertainty != permission to destroy provenance', proposed as a constitutional principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction = information, not merely error.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Leonardo lens to argue that under binary logic a contradiction (P and not-P) is treated as a problem to eliminate, but under a richer epistemic system it becomes a discovery signal that something about the model, scope, time, definitions, or evidence is wrong or incomplete: contradiction = information, not merely error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Clarify the proposition before evaluating its truth. ... AMBIGUOUS CLAIM -> GANESHA -> PRAMĀṆA -> LEONARDO -> LOGIC -> SHANI -> KNOWLEDGE STATE
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Ganesha lens to warn that an apparent 'Both' (P and not-P) result may indicate semantic ambiguity rather than genuine contradiction, illustrated by two auditors disagreeing on 'the system is compliant' because they mean GDPR vs constitutional compliance; proposes a six-stage resolution pipeline: Ambiguous Claim -> Ganesha (define proposition) -> Pramana (identify evidence routes) -> Leonardo (search assumptions/contradictions) -> Logic (determine epistemic state) -> Shani (check invariant violations) -> Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision logic ≠ Knowledge logic. ... UNDETERMINED → DO NOT APPROVE. The decision isn't "Candidate is false." It is "The evidence does not establish eligibility sufficiently for this decision."
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Krishna lens to separate decision logic (approve/reject) from knowledge logic (true/false/both/undetermined): a governance rule mapping UNDETERMINED to DO-NOT-APPROVE is a decision about insufficient evidence, not an assertion that the underlying claim is false, described as much more defensible architecturally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lens 1 — Ganesha ... Lens 10 — Statistical
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a ten-lens extraction engine, each with a name and defining question: Ganesha (definition -- what exactly is the proposition), Pramana (epistemic origin -- how did we obtain it), Leonardo (critical discovery -- assumptions/alternatives/contradictions), Krishna (purpose -- what decision this knowledge serves), Shani (invariants -- what must not be violated), Zero (invariant structure -- what remains across representations/perspectives), Dhatu (generation -- what transformations generate the observed state), Temporal (evolution -- how the knowledge state changes through time), Hofstadter (self-reference -- what the system knows about its own knowledge), Statistical (quantification -- evidence/uncertainty/convergence/contradiction measurement).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge does not merely answer: What is? It supports: What could be? What would happen if? What should we do? This means our knowledge model needs modal status.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Krishna lens: knowledge exists partly to support decisions among possible actions leading to different future states, so the knowledge model needs modal status, not just current-state facts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: W1 = W0 - {A} + {¬A} ... Which architectural conclusions survive in both worlds? And suddenly this connects directly to Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Leonardo lens as counterfactual reasoning: changing one assumption A in the current model W0 to not-A produces alternative world W1=W0-{A}+{not-A}; asks what consequences follow in W1, illustrated by a Kafka-required-vs-not architecture example, and observes this connects to the Zero lens (what survives across both worlds).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ArchitecturalInvariant = property preserved across admissible transformations ... I(S) = I(T(S)) for all admissible T.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines Shani ('what must never break?') and Zero ('what survives transformation?') into a near-formal definition: ArchitecturalInvariant = a property preserved across admissible transformations, i.e. property I is invariant if I(S)=I(T(S)) for all admissible transformations T, described as moving from a philosophical lens toward something formally testable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality = WorldModel = KnowledgeState = PossibleWorld = Narrative ... A possible world is not evidence that reality is that way. ... EKI-08 — Modal Integrity: Possible(P) ⇏ Actual(P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Ganesha lens to insist Reality, WorldModel, KnowledgeState, PossibleWorld and Narrative must not be conflated (Reality -> observed via limited channels -> Observation -> interpreted -> Knowledge State -> used to construct -> World Model -> transformed/simulated -> Possible Worlds), asserting a possible world is not evidence reality is that way, and formalizing EKI-08 Modal Integrity: Possible(P) does not imply Actual(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What world model must be true for this conclusion to follow? ... C | W ... If the conclusion survives many reasonable models, it becomes more robust. That gives us model robustness as another potential quantitative property.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the Leonardo lens from 'what assumptions are hidden?' to 'what world model must be true for this conclusion to follow?', reframing claim C as conditioned on world model, C|W, then testing across alternative models W1..Wn to see if the conclusion C(Wi) survives, proposing 'model robustness' as a candidate quantitative property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Model artifact — conclusion produced primarily by assumptions of (W). ... Assumption disguised as conclusion. Leonardo should explicitly search for this.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the not-knowledge taxonomy with eight categories (Fact candidate, Inference, Model-dependent conclusion, Speculation, Analogy, Contradiction, Unknown, Model artifact), highlighting 'Model artifact' as a conclusion produced primarily by W's own assumptions -- an assumption disguised as a conclusion -- which the Leonardo lens should explicitly search for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What happens when evidence disappears? ... What happens when its own self-model is wrong? Those are epistemic death conditions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines Shani ('what must never become false?') with the eschatological question ('what happens at a terminal/extreme condition?') into five required 'epistemic death condition' tests a robust KnowledgeOS must define: evidence disappearing, a core assumption being falsified, all available explanations conflicting, the system discovering it cannot answer a question, and its own self-model being wrong.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 — Representation ... representation ≠ reality; representation ≠ knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: H1: knowledge may be represented through language and other formal/structured representations (Reality->Observation/Interpretation->Representation->Proposition/Model), but representation is neither reality nor knowledge itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H2 — Knowledge is not a document. A document is an artifact that can contain, express, reference, constrain, or evidence knowledge. It is not itself necessarily knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: H2: a document is an artifact that can contain/express/reference/constrain/evidence knowledge without itself being knowledge; a Constitution may have authority to define a rule while an observation has authority to establish an observed fact -- different authority dimensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H3 — Knowledge is dynamic ... K(P,t,c,E) ... I would not yet make this mathematical expression part of the kernel. It is a modelling lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: H3: knowledge state may change as observations/evidence/interpretations/context/time change, tentatively K(P,t,c,E) (proposition, temporal state, context, evidence), explicitly held back as a modelling lens, not yet kernel-level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H4 — Knowledge space is potentially unbounded ... KnowledgeOS governs bounded portions of an effectively unbounded knowledge space.
b_rows_sample.statement: H4: knowledge can expand through breadth, depth, connections, abstraction, and specialization with no obvious finite 'KnowledgeOS universe'; KnowledgeOS governs bounded portions of an effectively unbounded knowledge space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H5 — Knowledge domains require boundaries ... A topic is potentially informal. A domain has a governed boundary. ... H6 — Boundaries are not walls ... boundary crossing as a first-class relationship.
b_rows_sample.statement: H5: a knowledge domain requires a declared scope within which concepts/claims/relationships/responsibilities are meaningful (distinguishing informal 'topic' from governed 'domain'); H6 corrects 'boundary' from meaning 'outside = inaccessible' to determining what belongs/does-not-belong/is-externally-referenced/is-dependent, making boundary crossing a first-class relationship.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H7 — The Kernel validates admissibility, not truth ... Boundary validation / Epistemic validation / Authority validation / Temporal validation ... These must remain separate.
b_rows_sample.statement: H7: the Kernel should answer 'is this representation admissible within this knowledge boundary?', not 'is this statement true?', separating boundary validation, epistemic validation, authority validation, and temporal validation as four distinct, non-collapsible questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H8 — Knowledge has expressive capacity ... A domain is partly defined by what it can meaningfully express. ... H9 — Vocabulary is not the boundary ... Lexical boundary ≠ Conceptual boundary ≠ Relational boundary ≠ Propositional boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: H8: a domain's expressive capacity is vocabulary+concepts+types+relations+constraints+permissible propositions+abstractions+context, generalizing a prior 'subset of words and sentences' idea. H9 corrects the assumption that knowing every word in a sentence makes it valid in a domain: a valid relationship (e.g. voter--submits-->ballot) is also required, distinguishing lexical, conceptual, relational, and propositional boundaries as four non-identical things -- called probably the most important thing missing from the original model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H10 — Knowledge has structure ... CLAIM: subject, predicate, object, context, temporal validity, provenance, epistemic state, relationships ... a modelling candidate, not yet a prescribed aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: H10: knowledge is not merely words+sentences but Concept+Relation+State+Context+Time+Evidence, sketching a candidate CLAIM unit (subject, predicate, object, context, temporal validity, provenance, epistemic state, relationships), explicitly not yet a prescribed aggregate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing Dimension 1 — Identity ... What gives a knowledge object stable identity? ... Missing Dimension 2 — Context ... What dimensions constitute context? ... Missing Dimension 3 — Time ... observed_at, asserted_at, valid_from, valid_until, verified_at ... should not automatically collapse into one timestamp.
b_rows_sample.statement: Missing Dimensions 1-3: (1) Identity -- without stable identity ('Payment Service' vs PaymentService:v1/v2/Production/Development) a proposition may be syntactically valid but unanchorable; (2) Context -- the same sentence (e.g. 'the system allows voting') can mean a constitutional rule, software capability, current runtime state, historical behavior, or future requirement depending on domain/environment/role/jurisdiction/purpose/scenario/time; (3) Time -- observed_at, asserted_at, valid_from, valid_until, and verified_at must not automatically collapse into one timestamp.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing Dimension 4 — Provenance ... Can every knowledge claim trace its lineage back to its originating observations or assertions? ... Missing Dimension 5 — Epistemic status ... "This statement exists" is not equivalent to "we know this statement to be true." ... Missing Dimension 6 — Authority ... semantic admissibility ≠ epistemic validity ≠ authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Missing Dimensions 4-6: (4) Provenance -- knowledge origin (human assertion, source code, runtime observation, document, experiment, inference, another claim) plus derivation kind (direct/derived/transformed/aggregated/generated), posing the question of whether every claim can trace lineage back to originating observations, especially important for AI-generated knowledge; (5) Epistemic status -- observed/asserted/hypothesized/inferred/supported/verified/contradicted/unknown/obsolete, since a statement's existence is not equivalent to its being known true; (6) Authority -- who may define a concept/boundary/rule/fact/classification/decision, keeping semantic admissibility, epistemic validity, and authority strictly separate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing Dimension 7 — Lifecycle ... verified + superseded is perfectly possible. A verified statement can become obsolete without ever becoming false. ... Missing Dimension 8 — Contradiction and plurality ... the Kernel should probably preserve epistemic plurality rather than prematurely collapse it. ... Missing Dimension 9 — Questions ... a knowledge system should know what it does not know. ... Missing Dimension 10 — Purpose ... Relevance is contextual and purposive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Missing Dimensions 7-10: (7) Lifecycle (candidate->proposed->accepted->verified->active->superseded->retired) is a distinct dimension from epistemic state -- 'verified + superseded' is coherent, a verified statement can become obsolete without becoming false; (8) Contradiction/plurality -- conflicting claims (Service uses Kafka / Service does not use Kafka) must be preserved with who-claimed-what/when/context/evidence rather than prematurely resolved, connecting to the multi-valued-logic research; (9) Questions -- knowledge includes unresolved status (e.g. 'does the Voting Context enforce device continuity?' = unresolved), giving a Knowledge Space of known/unknown/disputed/uncertain/unexplored, important for the statistical/inverse approach; (10) Purpose -- the same fact has different relevance depending on task (architecture review, security audit, implementation, governance, legal dispute, AI agent task), so relevance is contextual and purposive, important for bounded knowledge delivery to AI agents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would therefore redraw the model ... Not as a hierarchy, but as orthogonal dimensions around a claim: SEMANTICS / EPISTEMICS / CONTEXT / TIME / AUTHORITY / LIFECYCLE / BOUNDARY-SCOPE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redraws the conceptual model as seven orthogonal dimensions clustered around a CLAIM (Semantics: vocabulary/concepts/relations/meaning; Epistemics: evidence/confidence/provenance/uncertainty; Context: domain/purpose/scenario/audience; Time: validity/observation/supersession/verification; Authority: ownership/jurisdiction/decision-rights/governance; Lifecycle: proposed/active/superseded/retired), all nested inside a Boundary/Scope with Internal/External sub-division.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel preserves and validates the structural integrity of bounded knowledge representations while keeping semantic, epistemic, temporal, authority, and lifecycle dimensions distinct. ... I would not yet decide that a "claim" is the fundamental KnowledgeOS aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Kernel's role away from 'the thing that verifies knowledge' toward preserving/validating structural integrity of bounded knowledge representations while keeping semantic/epistemic/temporal/authority/lifecycle dimensions distinct, delegating evidence/verification/governance/temporal/evaluation to specialized mechanisms; explicitly declines to decide yet whether the fundamental KnowledgeOS aggregate is a claim, proposition, knowledge assertion, state of affairs, or a combination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Conceptual Model Discovery Questions ... A. Ontology ... B. Boundary ... C. Dynamics ... D. Epistemology ... E. Authority ... F. Representation ... G. Quantification ... H. AI
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses 42 numbered discovery questions across eight categories (Ontology, Boundary, Dynamics, Epistemology, Authority, Representation, Quantification, AI), e.g. 'what is the smallest thing that can meaningfully be knowledge?', 'can two domains legitimately overlap?', 'can knowledge be superseded without becoming false?', 'can KnowledgeOS represent we don't know?', 'is an LLM-generated sentence knowledge?', 'what exactly are we trying to quantify?' (listing amount of information/uncertainty/coverage/depth/breadth/consistency/confidence/evidence strength/completeness/expressive capacity as distinct candidate quantities), and 'what does an AI agent actually receive from KnowledgeOS?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is knowledge fundamentally a property of a statement, or a property of a relationship between a statement and reality under a context? ... My architectural intuition is strongly toward Model B, but I would not make it a decision yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the file's most fundamental open question -- is knowledge a property of a statement (Model A: Knowledge->Statement) or a relationship between representation, reality, evidence, and context (Model B: Representation<->Evidence, both under Context, correspondence to Reality, yielding Knowledge State)? -- leaning toward Model B as an architectural intuition without yet deciding, proposing to freeze the whole review as a conceptual hypothesis and run it through thirteen accumulated lenses (Vani, Paninian, Karaka, Pramana, Wittgenstein, Shannon, Topological, Statistical, Shani, Ganesha, Leonardo, Krishna, Governance) asking 'what is the minimum ontology that survives all lenses without mixing dimensions?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Representation ≠ Proposition ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge state ... KS = <p, r, c, τ, e, a, λ, σ> ... a descriptive tuple, not yet a domain object or aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Perplexity's review agrees KnowledgeOS should not implement a 'knowledge' aggregate or universal truth-verification kernel yet, formalizing Representation != Proposition != Evidence != Knowledge state, and proposing a provisional descriptive (not aggregate) tuple KS=<p,r,c,tau,e,a,lambda,sigma> (proposition, representation, context, time, evidence, authority, lifecycle, epistemic status).

b_rows_sample.anchor: verified + superseded ... authoritative + historically invalid ... structurally admissible + epistemically unsupported ... semantically valid + contextually inapplicable ... disputed + highly evidenced ... are all coherent combinations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates twelve knowledge dimensions (semantics, ontology, representation, context, epistemics, evidence, provenance, authority, time, boundary, lifecycle, purpose), each with a core question and example, and gives five coherent cross-dimensional combinations that a single collapsed status field would wrongly forbid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposed minimum conceptual ontology: 1. Semantic object ... 2. Representation ... 3. Assertion ... A1(p,c1,t1,a1), A2(p,c2,t2,a2) ... 4. Evidence ... 5. Context ... 6. Boundary ... 7. Knowledge state ... a derived view.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes seven minimum-ontology candidates: Semantic object (concept/relation/type/proposition/rule/question/model, interpretable independently of representation); Representation (document/source file/diagram/dataset/event/observation record/embedding/generated text, carrying provenance but not automatically inheriting epistemic status); Assertion (a contextual act of presenting a proposition, formalized as A1(p,c1,t1,a1) and A2(p,c2,t2,a2) where the same proposition p may have differing contexts/times/authorities); Evidence (typed and directional: supports/contradicts/qualifies/derives/contextualizes/supersedes); Context (domain/jurisdiction/environment/scenario/actor-role/audience/purpose/temporal frame/version, not one opaque value); Boundary (a set of constraints on vocabulary/concept membership/permitted relations/proposition forms/authority/external references/dependency direction/ownership/context applicability); Knowledge state (a derived view over the other six, avoiding treating 'knowledge' as a too-early primitive).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Kernel preserves identity, provenance, structural integrity, boundary conformance, and cross-dimensional consistency for governed knowledge representations. It does not independently establish truth. ... Non-kernel responsibilities: evidential strength; reproducibility; truth or falsity; ... agent-specific retrieval.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the Kernel boundary: the Kernel validates identity uniqueness/reference integrity, representation-to-semantic-object linkage, well-formed subject/predicate/object, permitted relation types, boundary membership/crossings, context completeness, temporal interval consistency, provenance graph integrity, authority compatibility, lifecycle transition legality, preservation of contradictory assertions, and immutable historical records; explicitly excludes evidential strength, reproducibility, truth/falsity, legal legitimacy, confidence, relevance, inference, statistical uncertainty, and agent-specific retrieval as non-kernel (specialized-service) responsibilities -- important for AI-generated content that may be structurally admissible yet unverified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Representation independence ... 2. Assertion multiplicity ... 3. Status orthogonality ... 4. Contradiction preservation ... 5. Boundary explicitness ... 6. Temporal distinction ... 7. Provenance closure ... 8. Authority specificity ... 9. Unknown as first-class state ... 10. No epistemic upgrade by transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines ten candidate core invariants: (1) multiple representations may express one semantic object and vice versa; (2) the same proposition may be asserted by multiple authorities in different contexts/times; (3) epistemic status, lifecycle status, authority, and temporal validity must not collapse into one state machine; (4) contradictory assertions must be representable without automatic destructive resolution; (5) cross-boundary references must be explicit/typed/traceable; (6) assertion/observation/validity/verification/supersession time must remain distinguishable; (7) derived/transformed representations must retain links to immediate inputs and transformation activities; (8) authority must be scoped to the kind of act performed (defining/asserting/verifying/classifying/governing); (9) an unresolved question/knowledge gap must be representable without becoming a false proposition; (10) extraction/summarization/embedding/generation must not automatically increase epistemic status.
