a_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā Chapter 3 \rightarrow rich semantic test case \rightarrow architecture validation
a_rows_sample.statement: States the epistemic status of the exercise: NOT claiming Bhagavad-gita = formal specification of KnowledgeOS, but using Chapter 3's narrative/conceptual structure as a rich semantic test case to ask whether the model can faithfully represent the epistemic situation, reasoning, conflict, guidance and action without losing distinctions; notes the source itself frames Arjuna's problem as conflicting instructions and a request for decisive determination of what is most beneficial.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q = (Intent, Context, Purpose, Alternatives, Uncertainty, DecisionNeed)
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 3 shows Question->Intent->DimensionDiscovery is insufficient: Arjuna's actual problem combines conflicting interpretations, uncertain action, personal purpose and a request for determination, requiring Q=(Intent,Context,Purpose,Alternatives,Uncertainty,DecisionNeed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Synthesis(A_1,A_2,Context) \rightarrow A_3
a_rows_sample.statement: Validates MoreEvidence ⇏ Resolution and Support ⊥ Resolution (Q16), and reveals a missing concept: Synthesis — resolution is sometimes not 'choose A instead of B' but A+B -> HigherOrderConcept, illustrated by Knowledge+RightlyOrientedAction=Karma-Yoga resolving the apparent Knowledge-vs-Action opposition. Adds Synthesis as a sixth Resolution strategy alongside Evidence, Reinterpretation, Prioritization, Acceptance, Deferral.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question \rightarrow Intent \rightarrow Context \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Understanding \rightarrow NormativeAssessment \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow Guidance \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Observation
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the old Knowledge->Gap->Action loop with a longer, cyclic loop (Question->Intent->Context->Knowledge->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Discrepancy->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation), formalized as a closed epistemic control loop S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Action_t,Outcome_t,Observation_{t+1}) — action produces consequences, consequences become observations, observations update knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Our theory                          | Chapter 3                                                  | Verdict
a_rows_sample.statement: A 19-row final validation matrix scoring prior theory claims (multidimensional epistemic state, conflict is relational, support≠resolution, question has purpose, understanding≠knowledge, ideal state, structured discrepancy, scalar distance secondary, Zero/Lord/Sārathi abstractions, decision readiness, action, agency, norms, role, authority, lineage, transition system) against Chapter 3 evidence, verdicts ranging 'Strongly validated' to 'Major missing concept' (Norms, Role, Authority) to 'Needs extension' (Action, Agency).

a_rows_sample.anchor: An Epistemic–Normative–Decision–Action System
a_rows_sample.statement: Deepest conclusion: KnowledgeOS was thought to be a Knowledge State model but is actually 'An Epistemic-Normative-Decision-Action System' whose central problem is how an agent moves from imperfect understanding through knowledge, interpretation, norms, discrepancy and guidance to authorized action while preserving epistemic provenance and never confusing knowledge, recommendation and decision. Chapter 3's arc is summarized as Confusion->Question->Clarification->Knowledge->Understanding->Norm->Duty->Guidance->Decision->Action. Recommends freezing Purpose/Role/Duty/NormativeState/Authority/Intention/Agency/ActorState/LearningReadiness/Synthesis/PerceivedConflict/DecisionGap/NormativeGap and revising Q16-19 before proceeding to Q20, since Q20 would otherwise formalize a state model missing normative and agency dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 does not directly prove our KnowledgeOS architecture. It provides a highly structured conceptual domain from which we can derive architectural abstractions. Those abstractions must be explicitly separated from what the text actually says.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens a second, more critical review of Chapter 3 (re-read in full rather than via search snippets) with a governing methodological correction: the text does not directly prove the KnowledgeOS architecture; it supplies a structured domain from which architectural abstractions may be derived, and these must stay explicitly separated from what the text literally says — essential for both mathematical rigor and DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 = Action Theory with an Epistemic Dimension
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects S0807's framing of Chapter 3 as primarily epistemic: the chapter is titled Karma-yoga and its central problem is Knowledge/Discernment vs Action/Duty, proceeding through two paths, unavoidable action, prescribed duty, yajña, a reciprocal cosmic/social cycle, exceptional self-realized persons, action for social example, role-specific duty, desire, and regulation of senses/mind/intelligence — so 'Chapter 3 = Action Theory with an Epistemic Dimension', not 'Chapter 3 = Epistemic Theory'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ❌ "Chapter 3 proves six discrepancy dimensions"
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit 'do not freeze yet' checklist rejecting eight overclaims: Chapter 3 proves six discrepancy dimensions; proves an affective state; proves LearningReadiness as a state variable; proves Event Sourcing; Senses->Mind->Intelligence->Soul is our epistemic hierarchy; Lord/Sārathi/Zero are literally equivalent to software components; decision requires zero discrepancy; all unresolved discrepancies can be ignored. Companion 'what I WOULD freeze' list gives thirteen invariants with strong support: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding≠Decision, Decision≠Action, ObservedAction≠ActionMeaning, Role≠Duty, Duty≠Goal, Norm≠Evidence, Authority≠Source, CanAct≠ShouldAct, PerceivedConflict≠ActualConflict, Guidance≠Decision, Action->Outcome->StateChange, Discrepancy=typed findings relative to criteria.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source observation \rightarrow semantic concept \rightarrow architectural inference \rightarrow formalization
a_rows_sample.statement: Final self-assessment: grades the previous (S0807) analysis by area (A for Knowledge≠Understanding, A- for normative dimension recognition, down to C+ for 'separation of source vs inference'), diagnosing the main weakness as over-formalization too early — good concepts promoted directly to mathematical dimensions. Prescribes a mandatory four-stage gate: Source observation -> semantic concept -> architectural inference -> formalization, and proposes establishing a four-column Chapter-3 extraction table (Verse -> Source concept -> Architectural concept -> Formal status [axiom/derived invariant/heuristic/analogy]) as the rigorous bridge before revising Questions 16-19, presenting a revised bounded-context pipeline diagram (Context->Actor/Knowledge/World->Understanding->{Norms,Criteria}->Zero->Discrepancy->Lord->Sārathi->Decision->Action->Outcome->World/Knowledge update) as the new baseline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 is strong conceptual evidence for the architecture's core semantic relationships. It is not a proof of our particular software architecture or mathematical formalization.
a_rows_sample.statement: A ten-row table rates Chapter 3's support as 'Strong' for: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding->Action, Role->Duty, Normative knowledge, Authority->Guidance, Guidance≠Action, Action->Outcome->changed situation, Observed action≠semantic meaning, Agent condition affects action/knowledge, and Context-dependence of applicable duty — called the 'semantic skeleton' of the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 \rightarrow Semantic Principles \rightarrow DDD Model \rightarrow Mathematical Model \rightarrow KnowledgeOS Architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a three-layer epistemic classification for how the Gita evidence licenses claims: Layer 1 source-supported semantic principles (Knowledge->Understanding->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome, governed by Role+Norm+Context+Authority — 'strongly supported'); Layer 2 mathematical abstraction (S_t, Δ_t, D_t, S_{t+1}=T(...) — 'motivated but not proven'); Layer 3 KnowledgeOS implementation architecture (bounded contexts, Zero/Lord/Sārathi as components — 'not proven, requires independent validation'). Gives a derivation chain Chapter 3 -> Semantic Principles -> DDD Model -> Mathematical Model -> KnowledgeOS Architecture where each arrow is a derivation step, not a claim the source contains the software architecture. Final confidence ratings: core conceptual architecture and DDD concepts strongly supported/motivated; mathematical modelling well-motivated but needing independent validation; specific equations derived-by-us-not-source-proven; fixed discrepancy vector explicitly 'do not freeze'; concrete component architecture requires separate architectural evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discrepancy is a Typed Set, Not a Fixed Vector ... Delta(S,C,P) = Diff(S, Expected(C,P)) where Delta is a typed set of findings ... This allows a single finding to be both Semantic and Normative; No assumption of orthogonality or separability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the discrepancy model from a fixed orthogonal vector Delta=(Delta_E,Delta_U,Delta_N,Delta_D,Delta_Decision,Delta_A) into a typed set of findings Delta(S,C,P)=Diff(S,Expected(C,P)), where each finding carries one or more types (Epistemic, Semantic, Normative, Domain, Decision, Operational, etc.) and no orthogonality/separability is assumed -- justified by the observation that a single conflict (e.g. in Arjuna's understanding) can be simultaneously epistemic, semantic, normative and decisional.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action = (Actor, Role, Operation, Duty, Intention, Orientation, Context, Outcome) ... ObservedAction != ActionMeaning; CanAct != ShouldAct != WillAct
a_rows_sample.statement: Expands the Action formalization from (Actor, Operation, Result) into an eight-field structure (Actor, Role, Operation, Duty, Intention, Orientation, Context, Outcome), with new invariants ObservedAction != ActionMeaning (the same observable action can carry different semantic status depending on orientation/intention/duty) and CanAct != ShouldAct != WillAct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Freeze the theory as defined in this document ... The theory is now complete, defensible, and ready for construction.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's own closing recommendation is to freeze this theory, create a semantic extraction table for future chapters, formalize transition semantics for the clean state model S=(W,K,U,N,A,C), define an algebra of operations for Z/L/Sa, and proceed directly to implementation -- an unadjudicated self-assessment by the external-research source, not a project governance ruling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document contains many useful conceptual correspondences between Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4 and KnowledgeOS, but most of the displayed equations are not mathematical derivations from the verses. They are newly invented quantitative models. Several are mathematically under-specified, and some are outright invalid as stated.
b_rows_sample.statement: A systematic mathematical audit of S1321 rejects its central framing claim (that Chapter 4 provides a 'complete mathematical foundation' culminating in a formula for KnowledgeOS) and works through specific defects: exponential knowledge decay K_t^decayed = K_0*e^(-lambda*t) has no basis in the verses and lambda is never defined from observations, so 'lineage = useful architectural lens' but 'exponential decay = invented hypothesis'; the memory integral M(t) = integral_0^t K(tau) dtau is unjustified unless K(tau) is defined as measurable and the measure and meaning of integration are specified, and is replaced by a cleaner subset relation AccessibleHistory_t subset-or-equal HistoricalState_t; the intervention threshold I(t)=1 iff Delta(K_t,I_t)>theta invents an arbitrary scalar threshold with no textual basis, so 'condition-triggered intervention' is retained as a research lens while 'the specific threshold equation' is rejected as a derivation; the multiple-evidence-paths summation (sum W_i = Total Evidence) is judged particularly problematic because the corpus's own EXP-01 work already established that dependency and evidence relationships matter before aggregation and a simple sum can double-count dependent evidence, so the formula is 'not acceptable as an evidence calculus without a dependence model'; the Faith(K_t)=Confidence(K_t)/Uncertainty(K_t) ratio is rejected because it requires undefined semantics for both quantities and becomes undefined when Uncertainty=0 (the code's return of infinity is called 'a programming convention, not a mathematical derivation'); the wise-state vector W=(0,0,C,infinity) is rejected as not a valid mathematical structure until the vector space, coordinates, codomain, and whether infinity is legitimate in that space are all defined, and should be treated as metaphorical notation; and the final closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment) is rejected outright: no defined units or domains, no derivation, no normalization, no reason KnowledgeOS should be a scalar, a possibly-zero denominator, and not following from any prior equation -- called 'a metaphorical synthesis presented in equation form,' exactly what the mathematical verification protocol must prevent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `is_verified() = true` cannot simply mean "true knowledge." The document collapses precisely the distinction our architecture worked hard to preserve.
b_rows_sample.statement: Further specific defects identified in S1321: the reward function R(K) treating knowledge.is_verified() as a truth oracle collapses the architecture's own load-bearing distinctions (Evidence != Determination; Accepted != Truth), and is judged a major epistemic issue, not a minor one; the Guna-to-Dimension mapping (Sattva->Knowledge, Rajas->Action, Tamas->Material) and the non-doer Agency(A)=Actor!=Executor claim are not mathematically derived and are philosophical analogy only, which should never be promoted into the architecture without independent evidence; the non-attachment derivative Attachment(A) = partial(Outcome)/partial(Expectation) is called a classic example of 'mathematical decoration replacing mathematical derivation,' since outcome-as-differentiable-function, units, and domain are all undefined; the action/inaction dual-state additive model A_t = A_physical + A_mental is under-defined (what does addition mean; are physical and mental actions elements of the same algebra) though its underlying conceptual distinction (ObservedExecution != ActionSemantics) is judged genuinely useful; and the learning function K_{t+1}=K_t+L(K_t,Teacher) with Teacher=argmax(Trust*Knowledge) requires many unstated assumptions (K supports addition, teacher knowledge is commensurable with learner state, trust and knowledge are both scalar) though the underlying lens (knowledge acquisition mediated through a source/teacher relationship) is reasonable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I concur with the audit's assessment. ... The audit identifies 17 specific mathematical problems. I accept all of them. Below, I provide the corrected formulation.
b_rows_sample.statement: A formal corrective ruling (dated 2026-08-28, status ACCEPTED AS CORRECTIVE, authority 'Senior Mathematician/Statistician Review') accepts all 17 mathematical problems identified in the audit of S1321, and adopts a five-level status vocabulary to prevent future conflation: conceptual lens (valid, e.g. 'provenance matters'), research hypothesis (valid, e.g. 'action semantics depend on epistemic context'), architectural candidate (valid, e.g. 'accessible history != total history'), metaphorical analogy (analogy only, e.g. Guna -> Dimensions), and mathematical derivation (invalid unless actually proven, e.g. the exponential decay formula). The ruling reclassifies the whole S1321 document from '[implicitly] new architecture' to a non-authoritative research artifact, with a recommended document path research/external/deepseek/gita-chapter-4-conceptual-lenses.md and a final status of PROPOSED, NON-AUTHORITATIVE, RESEARCH HYPOTHESES.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance(A) ≠ ∅ ⇒ Established(A) may hold ... AccessibleHistory(A_t, H_t) ⊆ H_t ... Condition(K_t, G_t, I_t) ⇒ Intervention
b_rows_sample.statement: The corrective ruling replaces six of S1321's equations with corrected, non-quantitative reformulations, each explicitly typed as a research hypothesis or invariant candidate, not a derived theorem: provenance (replacing exponential decay) becomes Provenance(A) != empty-set => Established(A) may hold, an invariant candidate rather than a decay law; memory/history (replacing the integral M(t)) becomes AccessibleHistory(A_t, H_t) subset-or-equal H_t, a set-theoretic relation; intervention (replacing the threshold equation) becomes Condition(K_t, G_t, I_t) => Intervention, a relational trigger with the condition explicitly not specified as a threshold; multiple evidence paths (replacing the weighted sum) becomes a set of approaches {Path_1,...,Path_n} plus the explicit requirement that evidence aggregation must account for dependency between pathways; action/inaction duality (replacing the additive model) becomes the semantic relation ObservedAction != ActionMeaning, with Semantics(Action_t) = f(K_t, Context_t, Authorization_t, Intention_t); and faith/doubt (replacing the ratio) becomes Faith and Doubt as elements of an EpistemicState set, explicitly not necessarily reciprocal or ratio-scaled; the wise-person state (replacing the vector with an infinite component) becomes a labelled attribute record (expectations: None, fears: None, contentment: Present, peace: Complete) rather than a coordinate tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "Conceptual Lenses (Validated as Useful)". I would change that wording. We should say: **Conceptual Lenses — Accepted as Research Candidates** ... the Gītā material establishes the *textual/philosophical pattern*, but it does not establish that the pattern is a correct KnowledgeOS architectural principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: Agrees in substance with the prior corrective ruling's core distinction (the DeepSeek Chapter-4 document is valuable research material but not a mathematical derivation of KnowledgeOS) and endorses its four-stage pipeline (Gita concept -> observed structural property -> abstract pattern -> research hypothesis -> possible KnowledgeOS correspondence) as mathematically and epistemically sound, in place of the rejected Gita concept -> equation -> architecture shortcut. Proposes one wording refinement: the ruling's table header 'Conceptual Lenses (Validated as Useful)' should be changed to 'Conceptual Lenses -- Accepted as Research Candidates' (or 'Considered Useful for Further Investigation'), because the Gita material establishes only a textual/philosophical pattern, not that the pattern is a correct KnowledgeOS architectural principle -- illustrated with AccessibleHistory(A_t,H_t) subset-or-equal H_t, a reasonable abstraction that the Gita does not mathematically prove and KnowledgeOS has not yet ratified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: That equation has no derivation, no defined units, no established scalar semantics, and no relationship to the ratified KnowledgeOS model. Rejecting it is absolutely correct.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly reaffirms which prior formulations to retain and which to reject. Retained as genuinely promising research lines: provenance/lineage as a transmission chain A -> S_0 -> S_1 -> ... -> S_n; history vs accessibility (H_t^accessible subset-or-equal H_t^total), called one of the strongest candidates because it connects directly to the distinction between actual state, observation, and available knowledge; purpose-conditioned intervention (Condition(K_t,G_t,I_t) => Intervention), judged a better abstraction than the earlier arbitrary threshold equation; action semantics (ObservedAction != ActionMeaning, and Semantics(Action_t) = f(K_t,Context_t,Authorization_t,Intention_t)), particularly relevant to the existing open question OQ-4; and faith/doubt as non-scalar epistemic dimensions rather than a ratio. Explicitly reaffirmed as rejected: the exponential decay formula, the memory integral M(t), the weighted evidence sum, the wise-state vector with an infinite component, and especially the final closing equation KnowledgeOS = Wisdom*Action/(Doubt+Attachment) -- which has no derivation, no defined units, no established scalar semantics, and no relationship to the ratified KnowledgeOS model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would **not ask Claude to incorporate this document into Edition 2 now**. Instead, save it exactly as the external research artifact, with the corrective classification attached.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final ruling: ACCEPT the corrective methodology (four-stage pipeline); ACCEPT the conceptual lenses as research candidates (not 'validated'); REJECT the unsupported equations as derivations; DO NOT promote any of them to architecture yet. The document should not be incorporated into Edition 2 now; instead it should be saved as an external research artifact (status: EXTERNAL RESEARCH, NON-AUTHORITATIVE, CONCEPTUAL LENSES, HYPOTHESES), with the corrective classification attached, and a seven-stage discipline preserved before anything could enter architecture: Gita source -> textual interpretation -> structural abstraction -> KnowledgeOS research hypothesis -> mathematical test -> architecture test -> governance decision. After the ongoing Part III mathematical/architectural audit, the Gita-derived hypotheses should be compared against the formal KnowledgeOS model to identify convergences, tensions, and genuinely new questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Knowledge is operationally incomplete if it cannot support discrimination between permissible and impermissible action.** ... **Wisdom is an ongoing discriminative activity, not a stored possession.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 4's wisdom pattern (knowledge/wisdom -> discernment -> what-should/should-not-be-done -> right action) is interpreted architecturally as: knowledge is operationally incomplete if it cannot support discrimination between permissible and impermissible action -- with emphasis on the word 'support', explicitly not claiming that wisdom decides everything, since the architecture deliberately separates Evidence, Determination, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, and Action. The Gita insight is argued to reinforce this separation rather than replace it: wisdom is an ongoing discriminative activity, not a stored possession, suggesting a possible research-stage reformulation Determination -> Discrimination -> Proposal rather than treating knowledge as something that simply sits static in K_t. Explicitly marked as a research hypothesis, not yet a change to architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the verses concerning action, inaction, and forbidden action are essentially saying that **mere observable activity is insufficient to classify action**. ... $$\text{Observed activity} \neq \text{Action meaning} \neq \text{Action consequence}$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the action/inaction/forbidden-action reading into a three-way distinction: Observed activity != Action meaning != Action consequence, directly relevant to the unresolved open question OQ-4, and proposes a research-stage formalization ActionMeaning = f(K_t, Purpose, Intention, Authorization, Context) as more valuable than a bare equation like 'Karma = Action'. Also proposes that Chapter 4 supplies an independent philosophical rationale, not an architectural source, for an existing KnowledgeOS non-collapse principle: Evidence != Determination != Decision != Authorization != Execution -- 'a knowledge system should not move directly from available information to execution without a discriminative stage.' This is framed as a stronger intellectual relationship than manufacturing architecture from scripture: the philosophy independently challenges and illuminates the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DeepSeek's original document tried to do: Gītā verse → KnowledgeOS object → equation → code. We should instead do: Gītā verse / philosophical teaching → philosophical principle → abstract principle → KnowledgeOS question → architecture comparison → mathematical formalization → hypothesis → test
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes replacing DeepSeek's original four-step pipeline (Gita verse -> KnowledgeOS object -> equation -> code, i.e. S1321's method) with an eight-step pipeline: Gita verse/philosophical teaching -> philosophical principle -> abstract principle -> KnowledgeOS question -> architecture comparison -> mathematical formalization -> hypothesis -> test, worked through end-to-end on one example (wisdom discriminates action from non-action -> a knowledge system should support action discrimination, not merely information accumulation -> does K_t->Zero->Proposal->Decision adequately represent action discrimination -> is there a missing explicit distinction between possible action and appropriate action -> only after investigation, a possible formalization D(K_t,G,Policy) -> {PermissibleActions, ImpermissibleActions}, explicitly labelled research, not architecture). Recommends continuing the whole Chapter-4 effort not as 'deriving KnowledgeOS from Chapter 4' but as building a 'Gita -> Philosophy -> Architecture Inquiry', testing philosophical principles against Determination, Proposal, Decision, Authorization, Action, Governance, OQ-4, and the architecture's non-collapse invariants -- framed as potentially more profound than a one-to-one mapping: Chapter 4 as an independent philosophical stress test of the KnowledgeOS theory of action and decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Problem-first ... ✅ Confirmed | Conflict of frames ... ✅ Confirmed | State vs. Frame ... ✅ Confirmed | Equanimity ... ✅ Not reduced | Action relational ... ⚠️ OPEN | Duty ≠ Action ... ⚠️ Candidate | Non-attachment ... ⚠️ Candidate | Yajña ... ✅ Transformation | Provenance ... ✅ Confirmed | Knowledge-Action ... ✅ Confirmed
b_rows_sample.statement: A ten-item test matrix runs each philosophical principle against the actual architecture, each with a textual observation, abstract principle, KnowledgeOS hypothesis, architectural candidate formula, and a test question: (1) problem-first architecture (Information != Determination) -- confirmed, the architecture begins with Knower+Goal+IdealState; (2) conflict of valid frames (Missing != Unknown != Conflicted) -- confirmed, Zero includes Conflict as a first-class object; (3) state vs frame (State != Frame) -- confirmed, Knower/Purpose/IdealState/KnowledgeState are kept separate; (4) equanimity vs signal magnitude (Decision != argmax Utility) -- confirmed, Decision is separated from Action and requires Authorization; (5) action is relational (Meaning(Action_t)=f(Purpose,Role,Context,Policy,Consequences)) -- OPEN, this maps directly onto the existing open question OQ-4; (6) duty != action (Possible != Permissible != Required) -- candidate, the action vocabulary is judged under-specified; (7) non-attachment (Action != Outcome != ExpectedOutcome) -- candidate, the outcome-vs-expectation comparison is under-specified; (8) yajna as transformation (KnowledgeOS is a transformation system, not a repository, S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Event_t,Policy_t)) -- confirmed, already defined in the architecture; (9) provenance and lineage -- confirmed, Provenance is a first-class object; (10) knowledge-action transformation (Action=Execute(Decision,Knowledge,Context,Authorization)) -- confirmed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Weak Point 1: Action Semantics (OQ-4) ... ### Weak Point 2: Action Vocabulary ... `Possible` ... `Permissible` ... `Recommended` ... `Decided` ... `Authorized` ... `Executed` ... ### Weak Point 3: The Feedback Loop
b_rows_sample.statement: Three weak points in the architecture are independently highlighted by the Gita-derived philosophy: (1) action semantics -- OQ-4 is open, action/execution semantics are under-specified, judged a strong candidate for architectural refinement; (2) action vocabulary -- since Possible != Permissible != Required in the text, a six-stage action-status vocabulary is recommended: Possible (technically feasible), Permissible (allowed by policy), Recommended (suggested by Sarathi), Decided (selected by the Knower), Authorized (approved by governance), Executed (actually performed); (3) the feedback loop -- since Action != Outcome != ExpectedOutcome in the text, the feedback loop should be strengthened to Action -> Outcome -> Compare with Expectation -> New Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Wisdom is the active capacity to discriminate among possible actions in relation to purpose, duty, consequences and knowledge.** ... this suggests that what we currently call **Proposal** may be one component of a larger **discernment process**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'discernment' as a candidate concept deeper than mere Knowledge: Wisdom = Knowledge + Discrimination + Appropriate Action, explicitly not proposed as an architecture equation, restated more carefully as 'wisdom is the active capacity to discriminate among possible actions in relation to purpose, duty, consequences and knowledge.' Raises the research question of where KnowledgeOS performs this function, along the existing chain KnowledgeState -> Zero/discrepancy -> Determination -> Proposal -> Decision, suggesting that what the architecture currently calls Proposal may be only one component of a larger discernment process -- flagged as worth investigating, not resolved here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Technical ability to perform an action does not establish normative permission to perform it.** ... $$Capability \neq Authority$$ ... That could be valuable for AI agents.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives from Chapter 3's repeated framing of action in relation to duty/context/role/consequences a candidate invariant: technical ability to perform an action does not establish normative permission to perform it (Action != Permission; Capability != Authority) -- explicitly noted as stronger than the existing Decision != Authorization separation because it introduces a prior stage, Capability. Applied to an AI-safety scenario: an AI agent's technical ability to call delete(), deploy(), approve(), publish(), or modify-policy() does not mean Authorized(Action)=True, and even authorization does not mean Action=AppropriateAction. Proposes a richer AI-safety action chain: Capability -> Proposal -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution -> Observation, framed as a place where Gita philosophy and KnowledgeOS architecture can have a meaningful dialogue without either deriving the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Doubt_t = f(Conflict_t, Missing_t, Ambiguity_t, InsufficientEvidence_t, CompetingFrames_t) ... **Should doubt be represented as a derived condition over unresolved epistemic discrepancies rather than as a scalar?**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reading Chapter 1's paralysis-from-unresolved-conflict together with Chapter 4's call to cut doubt and act, hypothesizes that doubt is not simply the complement of confidence but a function of multiple unresolved epistemic conditions: Doubt_t = f(Conflict_t, Missing_t, Ambiguity_t, InsufficientEvidence_t, CompetingFrames_t) -- explicitly contrasted with and preferred over the earlier rejected formula Doubt = 1 - Confidence (from S1321, the DeepSeek document). Poses the research question directly: should doubt be represented as a derived condition over unresolved epistemic discrepancies rather than as a scalar?

b_rows_sample.anchor: we may discover that the Gītā-derived philosophy independently highlights the **same weak points** Claude's archaeological and mathematical work is finding—particularly **state continuity, action semantics, determination, conflict, provenance, authority, and transformation**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes explicitly comparing the emerging Gita-derived research track against the corpus's own formal findings registers (PF-1..PF-9, AF-F-1..AF-F-23, MV-F-1..MV-F-22), hypothesizing that the philosophically-derived weak points would independently converge on the same architectural weak points the mathematical/archaeological audit work separately finds -- named specifically as state continuity, action semantics, determination, conflict, provenance, authority, and transformation. Framed as a much stronger result than claiming the Gita 'contains KnowledgeOS': independent convergence between two unrelated methodologies (philosophical reading vs formal mathematical audit) would be more persuasive than either alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This remains **outside the architecture**. We should eventually save the DeepSeek material as external research and build the more rigorous research track we discussed
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the project-level disposition of the Gita/DeepSeek research thread as of this snapshot: it remains explicitly outside the ratified architecture, to be saved as external research material and pursued via the more rigorous pipeline discussed elsewhere in this batch (Gita -> philosophical principle -> abstract pattern -> KnowledgeOS question -> mathematical/architectural test), rather than the rejected Gita -> equation -> architecture shortcut -- and the Chapters 1-4 work is explicitly permitted to continue independently of the book production schedule.

Distinct from but structurally parallel to the earlier gita-chapter3-validation-exercise (which treated Chapter 3 as a semantic test case rather than a source for new formal derivations).

a_rows_sample.statement: Bhagavad Gita lens (Ksetra=Field, Ksetrajna=Knower of the field): a knowledge object does not exist independently of the relationship that created it -- Known != Knower.

a_rows_sample.statement: Vedanta Tripuisi lens: Knower / Knowing / Known (Jnata / Jnana / Jneya) is described as one of the strongest conceptual models surfaced so far for KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Krishna** | Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens | $L: \Omega \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ |
a_rows_sample.statement: A nine-row core correspondence table maps Gita concepts to KnowledgeOS concepts and formal notation: Krishna -> Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens (L: Omega -> P(Omega)); Arjuna -> the Knower (Actor State A_t); Wisdom/Jnana -> Knowledge State K_t; Action/Karma -> Epistemic Action/Assertion (a_t in A); Doubt/Samsaya -> Gap/Discrepancy (Delta_t); Faith/Sraddha -> Epistemic Trust/Policy (rho); Teacher/Guru -> Source/Evidence (S in S); Liberation/Moksa -> Decision Readiness (DR_t = 1); Attachment/Raga -> Epistemic Bias (b: K_t -> K_t').

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can give us additional architectural insight, but we should derive it as a set of architectural principles and testable hypotheses—not copy theological statements into the architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: The central methodological rule for using Chapter 4 (and by extension any external/theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input: derive architectural principles and testable hypotheses from the source, never copy theological statements directly into the architecture. Nine principles are derived under this discipline: (1) knowledge has lineage -- K_t should conceptually be (content, provenance, status, history), not a bare object, though this equation is explicitly withheld from v0.2 pending testing; (2) loss of knowledge is not the same as invalid knowledge (NOT KNOWN NOW != NEVER KNOWN; CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE != FALSE), supporting layered epistemic state without determining the exact state algebra; (3) state continuity can exist without state memory (continuity != memory != observability), suggesting a distinction between current state, historical continuity, accessible history, and authoritative history, classified [LENS]/[HYPOTHESIS] not ratified architecture; (4) condition-triggered intervention (a governance trigger pattern: Guard(s)=true => Remediation(s)), with the explicit warning not to jump from the narrative directly to an architecture rule -- test whether KnowledgeOS already contains the same structural pattern first; (5) action, inaction, and forbidden action are different states (not a Boolean), informing the open question OQ-4 via Execution != Consequence and ObservedActivity != ActionSemantics; (6) knowledge changes the meaning of action (MeaningOfAction(x | KnowledgeState), i.e. action is context-dependent, not semantically isolated); (7) knowledge acquisition has a protocol (a governed relationship of trust/inquiry/transformation, reinforcing an existing Extraction != Determination finding, R1); (8) doubt should be a first-class object (Doubt_t = f(K_t, Evidence_t, Contradiction_t, Requirement_t), explicitly marked as a research hypothesis, not to be added to the architecture yet); (9) knowledge and action form a closed loop (K_t -> Z_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Observation -> K_{t+1}), used as a comparative validation lens for an already-existing loop rather than as new architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna → Lord Lens ... That's too strong. A safer mapping is: Gītā concept → structural property → abstract pattern → possible KnowledgeOS correspondence
a_rows_sample.statement: S1321's direct character-to-variable mappings (Krishna -> Lord Lens, Arjuna -> Knower, made at the very beginning of that document) are judged too strong a jump from theological/metaphysical claim straight to software variable, skipping an intermediate abstraction level. A safer four-step mapping discipline is proposed: Gita concept -> structural property (observed in text) -> abstract pattern (generalized) -> possible KnowledgeOS correspondence (candidate) -- rather than Gita concept -> mathematical equation -> KnowledgeOS architecture directly. Example: Krishna's intentional manifestation does not directly imply 'Lord = generator operator'; instead, 'the narrative distinguishes an agent that knowingly intervenes under a purpose and condition,' studied as a structural analogue of purpose-conditioned intervention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can function as an **independent stress-test lens**. That is more valuable than trying to make it a source of architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes going one step further than the corrective ruling: rather than treating Chapter 4 as failing to derive the architecture, use it as an independent stress-test lens, pairing eight existing KnowledgeOS concepts with a Chapter-4-derived stress question each: K_t (can state continuity exist without complete memory?); X_t != Observed(X_t) (can history exist without present observability?); Evidence (can multiple transmission paths remain distinguishable?); Determination (what transforms transmitted information into accepted knowledge?); Authorization (what distinguishes knowing an action from being entitled to perform it?); Action (is action semantics independent of physical execution?); Governance (what triggers intervention when the current state diverges from intended order?); OQ-4 (can execution/consequence be modelled separately from action intent?). This use is judged stronger than treating the text as either a source of architecture or a failed derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not ask: "What KnowledgeOS object corresponds to Krishna, Arjuna, Guru, etc.?" We should ask: **"What philosophical principle is expressed here, and what does that principle teach us about KnowledgeOS?"**
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a five-step philosophical interpretation method for using Chapter 4 (or any theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input, replacing character-to-object mapping: (1) extract the philosophical principle, not names/mythology/literal narrative (e.g. 'knowledge should produce discrimination between action and non-action'); (2) generalize the principle, removing Gita-specific theological context while preserving the underlying idea (e.g. 'a knowledge-bearing system needs discernment concerning possible actions'); (3) compare with KnowledgeOS, asking whether an existing mechanism already expresses the principle (e.g. K_t -> Zero -> Proposal -> Decision as a candidate correspondence); (4) stress-test it, asking a sharper question than simple mapping (e.g. does the current model really distinguish 'what can be done' from 'what should be done'); (5) classify the result into one of five outcomes: CONVERGENT (philosophy independently expresses something already present), REFINING (suggests a distinction the architecture should examine), NEW HYPOTHESIS (introduces a potentially useful concept), NOT APPLICABLE (philosophically interesting but architecturally irrelevant), or CONTRASTING (the philosophical principle exposes a tension with the current model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 1: THE CRISIS ... Chapter 2: THE FRAME ... Chapter 3: THE ACTION SYSTEM ... Chapter 4: THE KNOWLEDGE-ACTION TRANSFORMATION ... This sequence suggests that a KnowledgeOS system should begin with: Problem → Purpose → Knowledge Requirement, not: Data → Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally accepts a shift from 'mapping' (what Gita concept maps to what KnowledgeOS object) to 'testing' (what theory of knowledge/action/decision/responsibility/state/transformation emerges from the text, tested against the architecture). Chapters 1-4 are read as a coherent progression mirroring the KnowledgeOS lifecycle: Chapter 1 the crisis ('I do not know what I should do'), Chapter 2 the frame (nature of self/duty/knowledge/disciplined action), Chapter 3 the action system (interdependence/duty/consequence/responsibility), Chapter 4 the knowledge-action transformation (how knowledge changes the meaning and consequence of action). This progression is read as suggesting a KnowledgeOS system should begin with Problem -> Purpose -> Knowledge Requirement rather than Data -> Knowledge, strengthening the existing architecture's roles (Knower=entity with a problem, Purpose=what must be determined, IdealState=what would constitute resolution, KnowledgeState=what is currently known, Zero=what remains unresolved, Lord=what might be relevant, Sarathi=what action follows).

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Decision-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the causal link between epistemic states and the decisions they inform. When a knowledge state changes, its associated decisions SHALL be flagged for re-evaluation, ensuring that actions do not outlive their justification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gap 1 (Decision Coupling, Knowledge->Action): identifies a missing invariant coupling knowledge states to the decisions/actions they justify, so that a stale/invalidated knowledge state flags dependent decisions for re-evaluation; proposed as H-KOS-Decision-001; without it, truth-seeking is 'useless for engineering or governance'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Revisability-001: No knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized. The kernel MUST provide a governed path for revision (retraction, replacement, or refinement) for every knowledge object, preserving the revision history as part of its identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gap 2 (Revisability as a Constitutional Right / Fallibilism): truth-seeking requires all knowledge remain revisable, turning the earlier TMS/AGM revision research into a constitutional law; proposed as H-KOS-Revisability-001; without it, the system degenerates into a dogma-storage system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Inference-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish between observational knowledge (evidenced externally) and inferential knowledge (evidenced internally via logic). The provenance of inferential knowledge MUST include its entire reasoning chain, and its authority is dependent on the validity of that chain.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gap 3 (Inference vs. Observation boundary): base/observed knowledge (external evidence) and derived/inferred knowledge (internal reasoning-chain evidence) have different authority models and are currently treated uniformly as 'evidence'; proposed as H-KOS-Inference-001; without it, systems conflate 'I read this' with 'I logically deduced this' -- a catastrophic epistemic category error.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-KOS-Justification-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the logical type (monotonic/non-monotonic) and justification strength (deductive, inductive, abductive, probabilistic) of the reasoning applied. This logical metadata SHALL govern how contradictions are resolved and how evidence is weighted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gap 4 (Justification Strength/Type): distinguishes monotonic/deductive (binary valid/invalid) from non-monotonic/defeasible (probabilistic/provisional) justification; proposed as H-KOS-Justification-001; explicit caution against building a full 'logic taxonomy kernel' -- the invariant is to not hide the nature of justification, not to store every logic type.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Decision-001 (Candidate): KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the relationship between a knowledge state and decisions derived from it. Changes to supporting knowledge SHALL trigger epistemic re-evaluation of dependent decisions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 1: 'Very strong candidate'; the invariant is NOT 'knowledge controls action' but 'action must preserve the epistemic basis that justified it'; connects to EKS observation!=decision, PKS assessment!=authority, AIP recommendation!=execution (out-of-group); refined as INV-KOS-Decision-001, status Candidate, needs a P5 domain-independence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The statement: > No knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized. is slightly too strong. ... The better invariant: ## INV-KOS-Revisability-001 (Candidate): KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the possibility of epistemic revision while preserving historical identity and provenance of previous states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 2: 'Extremely strong', close to a constitutional principle; corrects H-KOS-Revisability-001's 'no knowledge state SHALL be irrevocably finalized' as too strong (counterexample: terminal states like archived historical fact, final legal judgment, mathematical proof), refining to INV-KOS-Revisability-001, status Very strong candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Some domains have terminal states: Examples: historical fact after archival closure, legal judgment after final appeal, mathematical proof
b_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample used to soften the Revisability/Fallibilism hypothesis: some domains (archived historical fact, legal judgment after final appeal, mathematical proof) legitimately have terminal, non-revisable states.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Inference-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish observed facts from derived conclusions. Derived knowledge SHALL preserve the reasoning path and premises from which it was generated. Status: Very strong candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 3: 'probably one of the strongest additions', already implicit in existing Evidence!=Authority/Observation!=Decision/Assessment!=Authority/Projection!=Source separations; formalized as INV-KOS-Inference-001 (Observation != Inference), status Very strong candidate; the failure mode named is an AI 'model generated statement treated as observation'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS-Justification-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the nature and strength of justification supporting a conclusion, preventing conclusions derived under different reasoning assumptions from being treated as equivalent. Status: Candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reassessment of Gap 4: 'important, but needs caution' -- risk of accidentally building a 'logic taxonomy kernel'; the invariant is 'do not hide the nature of justification', not 'store all logic types'; formalized as INV-KOS-Justification-001, status Candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision coupling | Strong candidate ... Revisability | Very strong candidate ... Observation vs inference | Very strong candidate ... Justification type | Candidate. They do not yet prove a kernel design.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final classification table of the four new gap-candidates by strength (Decision coupling: Strong; Revisability: Very strong; Observation vs inference: Very strong; Justification type: Candidate); explicitly states they do not yet prove a kernel design, but transform KnowledgeOS's framing from 'a system that preserves knowledge' to 'a constitutional epistemic system that preserves the conditions under which reasoning can approach truth without corrupting itself'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Graph independence != Statistical independence. A dependency graph can provide structural information. It does not create a probability space. ... any function such as I(e)=1/(1+d(e)) must be classified as a STRUCTURAL SCORE, unless the corpus provides a statistical derivation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that a dependency-graph relationship (DependencyDepth) does not establish statistical independence P(E1 intersect E2)=P(E1)P(E2), so any function of graph depth such as I(e)=1/(1+d(e)) must be classified as a structural score rather than an independence measure unless a statistical derivation is separately provided -- pre-figuring the later executed EXP-6 finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the formula assigns e2 (a verbatim copy) and e3 (an independent observation) the SAME weight, because depth is a graph property and independence is a statistical one. => IndependenceFactor is not a measure of independence. CONFIRMED.
b_rows_sample.statement: EXP-6 constructs a verbatim-copy evidence item (e2, depth 1) and a genuinely independent second-source item (e3, also depth 1) and shows IndependenceFactor=1/(1+depth) (Step 270 s270.1) assigns them the identical weight (0.5), while the ground truth is that e2 contributes zero additional information; concludes IndependenceFactor conflates a graph property (path depth) with a statistical property (independence) -- a category error.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence duplication is precisely what the corpus's dependency-normalization work (025c-2, 025c-3, exp01_recheck.py) exists to prevent, and this formula rewards it. ... The formula assigns a verbatim copy and a genuinely independent observation the SAME weight ... It is a path-length discount. Naming it independence is a category error.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding MT-4: re-executes and re-confirms AggregateSupport=sum(s)/(1+log n) is unbounded (100 unit-strength items give 17.84) and non-idempotent (duplicating one evidence item raises support by 18.1%, directly rewarding exactly the duplication the corpus's own dependency-normalization work (025c-2, 025c-3, exp01_recheck.py) exists to prevent), and dimensionally undefined; and re-confirms IndependenceFactor=1/(1+depth) assigns a verbatim-copy item and a genuinely independent item the identical weight (0.5 each), naming this a category error (path-length discount mislabeled as independence) predicted in prose by Step 270 and here executed as a demonstration; both formulas remain usable only as declared engineering heuristics, never as measurements.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four quantitative claims are refuted outright ... All four fail an executed admissibility check. None is salvageable AS A MEASUREMENT; all four are usable as declared engineering heuristics once relabelled. This is a naming discipline problem with a one-line fix per formula, and Step 270 was already heading there.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding FR-4 (F-2, one of the three refutations that matter most): summarizes that averaging over sigma, AggregateSupport, IndependenceFactor, and confidence-as-probability all fail an executed measurement-admissibility check outright and none is salvageable as a measurement, but characterizes this as a naming-discipline problem fixable with a one-line relabelling per formula (as declared engineering heuristics), noting Step 270 was already moving in that direction.
