a_rows_sample.anchor: The one derivation it ever prompted -- the Zero/Sunya chain -- was earned by 1,620,000 assignments, not by the reading.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA-2026-09 experiment executed 1,620,000 assignments in generating its test corpus, and that the Gita text's role was confined to producing questions and lenses, with the actual Zero/Sunya chain result earned entirely by that computation, not by the philosophical reading.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T,Pi}(x) is not an element property. It is a property of an element in a representation, context, transformation, inquiry, and preservation contract.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline interpretation of the executed KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA-2026-09 results: nine of eleven algebraic hypotheses (L^2=L; L_A L_B=L_B L_A; individual-implies-group Zero H5; group-implies-individual Zero H6; reference-independence H7; contract-independence H8; invariant=Zero H9; Remainder=simple-set-subtraction H10; heuristic=counterfactual H11) were refuted, while termination (H3) and monotone decrease (H4) held (tested with 1,200 cases per family, deterministic execution), interpreted not as a failed theory but as evidence the counterfactual definition of Zero is correct while the assumption that x is the fundamental carrier is wrong.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D=[x,x] ... individual: {x}->Zero, {x}->Zero; group: {x1,x2}->NOT Zero ... D=[+c,-c] ... group: {+c,-c}->Zero
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the two generated minimal witnesses refuting element-wise Zero in both directions: a duplicate/redundancy case D=[x,x] where each x is individually Zero but the pair jointly is not (Zero(x,D) & Zero(y,D) does not imply Zero({x,y},D)); and a cancellation case D=[+c,-c] where neither element is individually Zero but the pair is jointly eliminable (the converse failure), together establishing that Zero is potentially a property of a subset S subseteq D rather than an element predicate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The heuristic and counterfactual paths agree only 55.75%. ... 1559 elements were removed by the heuristic despite not satisfying the counterfactual criterion, whereas only 301 true Zero elements were retained.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the PATH-A (formal counterfactual) vs PATH-B (declared heuristic rule) agreement rate of 55.75%, with a strongly asymmetric error pattern -- 1,559 over-removed by the heuristic against only 301 true-Zero elements the heuristic failed to remove -- establishing an empirical over-elimination bias and the concrete distinction HeuristicElimination != CounterfactualZero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: terminating but non-confluent rewriting ... We didn't choose rewriting theory. The experiment is telling us that rewriting theory may be the appropriate mathematical regime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Interprets the combined termination+non-confluence result as evidence the elimination process is better modelled as a terminating, non-confluent rewriting system (where different orderings L_A L_B(D) != L_B L_A(D) reach different normal forms) than as a classical commutative algebra or idempotent projection, framed as an instance of discovering the required mathematical structure from behaviour rather than choosing it in advance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO-GROUP-2026-09 ... What is the minimal mathematical structure of group-level eliminability?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a follow-on experiment KR-ZERO-GROUP-2026-09 to test Zero(S;D) for subsets S subseteq D directly, investigating singleton-vs-group Zero, pairwise-vs-higher-order Zero, cancellation, redundancy, order-dependence, minimal/maximal eliminable subsets, overlapping Zero subsets, and whether the resulting family structure is better described by rewriting systems, hypergraphs, closure systems, or lattices -- deferring any algebra question until after this experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment directly tested the definition on 4,203 element cases and found that the heuristic and counterfactual notions agree only 55.75% ... The report explicitly records 131 and 63 witnesses respectively.
a_rows_sample.statement: Precise figures for the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA executed results: 4,203 element-level test cases; 131 redundancy witnesses (D=[x,x] shape) and 63 cancellation witnesses (D=[+c,-c] shape), both falsifying element-wise Zero in opposite directions; the process is terminating and monotone but non-confluent, with simultaneous/forward-sequential/reverse-sequential processing diverging in 169 of 1,189 cases, traced concretely to removing token 'ref1' causing two 'c' tokens to become adjacent and activate a context-dependent transformation rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1,223 cases where the visible result remained unchanged after removal, but 196 of those were rejected once the full boundary contract was considered. That's 16.03%.
a_rows_sample.statement: Precise boundary-preservation result: of 1,223 cases where removing a candidate left the visible answer unchanged, 196 (16.03%) were rejected once provenance/uncertainty/scope/contradiction were added to the preservation contract, taken as direct experimental confirmation that 'same visible result does not imply same epistemic state.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: A = D - Eliminated and contract-unresolved material C agree exactly in all 1,182 tested cases. But transformation residual B differs.
a_rows_sample.statement: H10 result: of three candidate Remainder constructions (A = D minus eliminated elements; B = transformation residual; C = contract-relevant unresolved material), A and C coincide exactly across all 1,182 tested cases while B differs, establishing that the original three-way Invariant⊕Difference⊕Remainder decomposition is inappropriate and that Remainder is better understood as multiple empirically distinct observables produced by different questions rather than a single algebraic component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Is the missing mathematics a richer number system, or a richer carrier? ... the failures are increasingly about structure, not cardinality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the experiment's failures ([x,x] requiring contextual multiplicity, [+c,-c] requiring interaction/cancellation, the boundary result requiring a tuple (Value,Boundary,Provenance,...)) are about representational STRUCTURE rather than the number of available values, so a 30-valued scalar algebra could still fail where a small relational structure succeeds -- reframing the original 'which number base' question as 'is the missing mathematics a richer number system or a richer carrier', to be tested empirically rather than assumed either way.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero fails in both directions between the element level and the set level. It is therefore not an irrelevance relation in the graphoid sense ... [x,x] ... redundancy ... [+c,-c] ... emergent eliminability
a_rows_sample.statement: States that Zero fails both graphoid-axiom directions (composition: 131 violations; decomposition: 63 violations), with the two canonical counterexample shapes named as the whole concept: [x,x] (redundancy, a composition failure) and [+c,-c] (emergent eliminability under a cancelling contract, a decomposition failure).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A - Eliminated \equiv C in 1182/1182 -- exactly ... B is a different object. The transformation residual is not what the contract leaves unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Remainder trichotomy's exact positive identity: 'not eliminated' equals exactly 'contract-relevant unresolved material' without exception in 1182/1182 tested cases, while the transformation residual (B) is a genuinely different object, separating the residue of the operation from the residue of the concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One elimination in six is blocked by boundary information alone ... the rule-based and counterfactual notions of eliminability agree only 55.75% of the time ... 1559 elements the rule would remove are not Zero, against 301 that are Zero but the rule keeps.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the asymmetric-bias finding as a concept-level warning: a rule-over-field-types eliminability heuristic is wrong far more often in the dangerous over-elimination direction than the safe direction, so eliminability must never be implemented as such a rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L is not a projection and not an interior operator. It is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process. ... Which normal form you reach depends on the order you eliminate in.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that repeated-elimination L is reductive, terminating and iteration-monotone-decreasing but non-confluent (11/1162 non-commuting) and only operator-relative idempotent; concludes 'eliminate everything eliminable' names no unique object unless an order is fixed and declared.

a_rows_sample.anchor: So the proper terminology is: Proposition candidate ... Element-level Zero does not determine sequence-level Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: The claimed derivation that cancellation-loop or non-linear-interaction cases prove emergent (in)dispensability is not a proof but a constructive witness; the rigorous reformulation is an existential witness search: does there exist f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} such that Zero(S)=f(Zero(s_1),...,Zero(s_n)) for every admissible sequence ('element-wise compositional'), tested by seeking two sequences with identical element-level Zero signatures z(S1)=z(S2) but Zero(S1)!=Zero(S2), which would show element-level Zero information is insufficient; connects to the prior finding that group Zero cannot generally be reconstructed from singleton Zero status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This document models; it decides nothing. ... the standing rule is: resolve ownership of every invariant BEFORE protecting it.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the document's own status (`[DESIGN]`, kernel NOT SELECTED) and the governing rule that ownership of every invariant must be resolved before any tactical protection of it is designed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Read-disjointness is a constitutional invariant. No context owns it. Every context preserves it. ... its provenance map is what makes the invariant checkable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues read-disjointness (relating Pi, Q, T simultaneously) cannot be owned by Inquiry, Eliminability or Transformation individually, and must instead be a shared constitutional invariant every bounded context preserves, echoing the anonymity-invariant shape found in a sibling platform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence & Contradiction has unresolved ownership because DECISION-02 -- is phi a semantic evaluation frame or an evidence partition? -- is open. The model must not proceed to tactical work there.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly leaves the Evidence & Contradiction bounded context's ownership unresolved pending an open governance decision, refusing to proceed to tactical modelling there.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EliminationAssessment must carry its contract and reference. Zero is contract-relative (495/4049 verdicts flip) and reference-relative (541/4260). ... There is no EliminableCore aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives two aggregate-boundary design rules directly from prior experimental numbers: a stored Zero verdict must carry its full (contract, reference) index or it is not a fact when reused, and no 'EliminableCore' aggregate may cache minimal eliminable sets and close upward since Z is not generated by its minimal elements (286/826 failures).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Treating "eliminate everything eliminable" as well-defined -- L is non-confluent; the normal form depends on order. ... Letting a ticket accrete into architecture -- architecture produces tickets; tickets do not become architecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight named anti-patterns each traced to a specific earlier experimental finding, including treating full elimination as well-defined, a single scalar 'reduction size', re-fitting a decoder after seeing R, and letting tickets silently accrete into architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is the question "can this be removed without changing what I have chosen to observe?" -- and every word of that sentence is load-bearing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the canonical one-sentence definition of Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) with a word-by-word table (this/removed/changing/I have chosen/observe) explaining exactly what each word forces, distinguishing 'the change is zero' from 'a thing being empty or worthless'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not sufficiency -- adequacy is. ... Sufficiency is about what a representation retains. Zero is about what a case can lose.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Zero from sufficiency/adequacy (built read-disjoint and measured independent per document 07) so a design reaching for Zero when it wants sufficiency will delete the wrong things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero fails in both directions between the element level and the set level. It is therefore not an irrelevance relation in the graphoid sense ... [x,x] ... redundancy ... [+c,-c] ... emergent eliminability
b_rows_sample.statement: States that Zero fails both graphoid-axiom directions (composition: 131 violations; decomposition: 63 violations), with the two canonical counterexample shapes named as the whole concept: [x,x] (redundancy, a composition failure) and [+c,-c] (emergent eliminability under a cancelling contract, a decomposition failure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A - Eliminated \equiv C in 1182/1182 -- exactly ... B is a different object. The transformation residual is not what the contract leaves unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Remainder trichotomy's exact positive identity: 'not eliminated' equals exactly 'contract-relevant unresolved material' without exception in 1182/1182 tested cases, while the transformation residual (B) is a genuinely different object, separating the residue of the operation from the residue of the concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One elimination in six is blocked by boundary information alone ... the rule-based and counterfactual notions of eliminability agree only 55.75% of the time ... 1559 elements the rule would remove are not Zero, against 301 that are Zero but the rule keeps.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the asymmetric-bias finding as a concept-level warning: a rule-over-field-types eliminability heuristic is wrong far more often in the dangerous over-elimination direction than the safe direction, so eliminability must never be implemented as such a rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L is not a projection and not an interior operator. It is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process. ... Which normal form you reach depends on the order you eliminate in.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that repeated-elimination L is reductive, terminating and iteration-monotone-decreasing but non-confluent (11/1162 non-commuting) and only operator-relative idempotent; concludes 'eliminate everything eliminable' names no unique object unless an order is fixed and declared.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is there a well-defined group/set formulation of Zero? OPEN -- H5+H6 show the element-wise formulation fails in both directions; they do not supply the replacement. This is the deepest open question about the concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the deepest unresolved question about the Zero concept: no replacement group/set formulation exists even though the element-wise one is refuted in both directions; also leaves L's monotonicity, k>3 higher-order eliminability, and semantic equivalence explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A representation R=T(D) realizes Q under decoder O iff O(R)=Q(D). ... O is fixed in advance, as part of the inquiry frame. ... If O may be chosen after seeing R, then "realization" is just adequacy restated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Realization with the decoder O fixed in advance as part of the inquiry frame, stating that fixing is the entire content of the definition -- a claim about the decoder you actually have, not the existence of one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate \land \neg C(R) \Rightarrow not realizable, though the information is present. ... This is why C belongs in the frame and not in the transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Adequacy (does R determine Q, an existential/population-level question) from Realization (does this fixed decoder recover Q, a per-case question), showing they diverge for two independent reasons: a weaker-than-needed decoder, or a failing use-time constraint C.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-REP-REDUCTION's design failed to operationalize the adequacy/realization separation. ... the only adequate level, R5, has F=1.0000. ... this experiment could not exhibit it, and no experiment yet has.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a specific design defect: the chain's transformations never dropped a record so C could never fail, and the decoder was strong enough at the one adequate level, so the experiment excluded its own target case by construction -- the separation is real by definition but was never exhibited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization \Rightarrow Adequacy. ... What would refute it: a case set on which O(T(D))=Q(D) holds throughout while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous ... Not tested.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the one open conjecture in the document with an explicit refutation condition (a decoder right by luck on observed cases without being determined by R), noting the converse (Adequacy=>Realization) is already refuted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Last adequate stage: R5. First inadequate: R4. Crossing transformation: T4 -- rounding to 3 significant digits. ... TEST reproduces TRAIN closely
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the located adequacy boundary (R5 adequate at Hhat=0, R4 inadequate at Hhat=0.4299) reproduced closely on an independent test split (0.4408 vs 0.4299), confirming it is not a one-sample artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We may NOT say: "Three significant digits is the universal preservation limit." We may say: for this carrier, this inquiry Q, this transformation chain, this contract and this value domain, rounding ... crossed the observed preservation boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the scope-bound discipline the whole result exists to teach: the boundary is a property of the inquiry frame (carrier, Q, chain, contract, value domain), not a universal numeric limit; by the DPI corollary the boundary is unique and cannot be re-crossed back into adequacy along the sequential chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Zero rate at the boundary crossing is not distinguishable from the rate at a non-crossing step, and is in fact lower. Eliminability carries no signal about where preservation fails.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the direct test of hypothesis H-RR2 (Zero marks the adequacy boundary): refuted -- the Zero rate at the actual boundary crossing (0.0377) is not higher than, and is in fact lower than, the rate at a non-crossing step (0.0426).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rank conventions are NOT invertible. desc \neq (n+1) - asc when values tie -- 21369 violations ... this is NOT an instance of DECISION-01 ... The headline built on it was withdrawn -- both my wording and the review's replacement wording.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records an explicit retraction: a prior claim that a rank-direction finding instantiated DECISION-01 (non-evidential invariance) required an invertible recoding between rank conventions, which the audit refuted (21,369 tie violations); both the original and the review's replacement wording are withdrawn, though the underlying adequacy/realization sensitivity gap survives as the one place that distinction was visible at all.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: **G-01** | **`𝒪`, the mandatory operation set, is never enumerated.**
a_rows_sample.statement: G-01 (CRITICAL): 𝒪, the mandatory operation set, is never enumerated; ≡ is defined by ∀T∈𝒯 so the quantifier ranges over an open collection — ≡ is not undecidable, it is unconstructed. K*, A∈K, K1=K2, and the Step 259/266 sufficiency and minimality results all inherit this gap. Resolution requires HUMAN DECISION D-1, after which the gaps below it become derivable.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
The theory is not incomplete because it is missing answers. It is incomplete because it is
> missing a premise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sharper statement of the theory's incompleteness: it is not missing answers, it is missing a premise — 𝒪, what KnowledgeOS is obliged to be able to do, was never written down, and five CRITICAL gaps are its shadow; a theory of sufficient state cannot be evaluated without the operations it must be sufficient for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## C. The closing sequence
a_rows_sample.statement: An 11-step dependency-ordered (not importance-ordered) closing sequence is specified: (1) enumerate 𝒪 [HUMAN D-1]; (2) ratify/revise exogenous authority and govern the schema vocabulary [HUMAN D-2]; (3) decide Determination's scope [HUMAN D-3]; (4) derive the congruence and K* for the fixed 𝒪; (5) replace Σ with the ≥5-axis product; (6) split A into A_struct+qualification layer, make ℛ first-class, restore H; (7) type Context, define evidence identity; (8) audit ordinal-arithmetic rules; (9) EKP engineering repairs; (10) run the day-1 selection precision/recall experiment; (11) freeze one corpus tree before the next verification pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 CONFIRMED by execution: content-only is NOT a sufficient abstraction.
a_rows_sample.statement: EXP-1: two knowledge states differing only in provenance are declared equal under content-only abstraction, but their explain() outputs differ, so content-only abstraction is confirmed NOT sufficient under even a minimal operation set.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
=> H3 is UNDECIDED, and H4 is CONFIRMED:
     K=(A,R) is sufficient IFF the mandatory operation set O excludes every
     history-sensitive predicate.
a_rows_sample.statement: EXP-3: two structurally identical states (K(H_calm), K(H_stormy)) are indistinguishable under K=(A,R) for a minimal/full operation set as coded, but become distinguishable once a plausible history-sensitive predicate (ever_contested) is added; therefore 'K=(A,R) is the minimal sufficient state' is not a theorem of the corpus but a consequence of an unstated choice of the operation set O. [Note: the second-order investigation (S1754/S1756) later argues ever_contested is a class-4 audit/history operation the corpus's own taxonomy excludes from this congruence test, correcting this experiment's inference though not its arithmetic.]

a_rows_sample.anchor:
> *"Zero is computable, total and terminating over finite R, **RELATIVE to per-requirement
> evaluators**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Computational closure is assessed CONDITIONALLY CLOSED: everything executed and computable (membership, equality, StructuralValid, contradiction detection, supersession, replay, lineage, Zero — 8/8 tests) is computable only relative to per-requirement evaluators (Γ semantics, HumanAuthorization oracles) that are themselves not established; the theory is computable down to its oracles, and the oracles are where the epistemics live.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 as stated in the first-order pass is wrong in its premise and wrong in its inference.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the first-order claim that O is never enumerated: Step 256 s256.2 enumerates nine operations and Step 259 s259.7 adds six more, for 15 named operations; and the '≡ is unconstructed' claim is not independent -- Step 259 s259.18 states the ∀T∈T-incompleteness problem verbatim, and Step 254 already writes Minimality(K|T).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K* = the coarsest abstraction congruent for T_class-1 and expressive for I_mandatory
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommended (not fact) formulation of the canonical Knowledge State: K* = the coarsest abstraction congruent for the class-1 transformation set T_class-1 and expressive for the mandatory invariant set I_mandatory, both declared per deployment -- consistent with s254's Minimality(K|T) and s259.15-16's Congruent_tested (never Congruent_global).

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-54 | Split has no semantic-preservation invariant (256.10 states the requirement and supplies none) | 1 ... G-55 ... G-56 ... G-57 ... G-58
a_rows_sample.statement: Five new gaps added by the second-order pass: G-54 (Split has no semantic-preservation invariant, s256.10), G-55 (merge-provenance invariant s265.11 not expressible in terminal A), G-56 (congruence necessary but not sufficient; invariant-expressibility is an uncomposed second criterion), G-57 (humanAct/humanActRef untyped prose, 79 strings/0 typed objects), G-58 (Determination lost in DDD->formalization band transition, unrecorded, third instance of this failure mode).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Five of the five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes are the same object: Sigma. ... STEP 272 ... does not exist.
a_rows_sample.statement: All five remaining CRITICAL theoretical holes (G-06 Sigma>=5 axes, G-25 Unknown homeless, G-27 Insufficient missing, G-11 evidence layer no inputs, G-12 no empirical relational structure) converge on the single object Sigma, matching the corpus's own Step 271 s271.35 marking Sigma RED and s271.36 commissioning the non-existent Step 272 to derive it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CLASS 1 -- state transformation  (11) ... CLASS 2 -- epistemic assessment  (2) ... CLASS 3 -- governance operation  (1) ... CLASS 4 -- audit/history operation  (3)
a_rows_sample.statement: Full classification of all 17 corpus-named operations per s259.7's five-class scheme: Class 1 state transformation (Add, Remove, Revise, Transform, Supersede, Merge, Split, Reject, Withdraw, Promote, Reintroduce), Class 2 epistemic assessment (Validate, Assess), Class 3 governance (Authorize), Class 4 audit/history (Replay, EverContested, RevisionCount); Class 5 observation has no named member.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 premise | 'O is never enumerated.' | False. ... KG-4 / EXP-3 inference | 'ever_contested refutes K=(A,R) sufficiency.' | Invalid. ... IE-4 | '≡ is unconstructed.' | Overstated. ... ON-1 | 'the dependency graph is cyclic.' | True as drawn, but ... G-31 | 'the aggregate boundary is never fixed.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Five further first-order findings corrected rather than withdrawn: G-01's premise (O is enumerated, 15 named ops), the KG-4/EXP-3 inference (invalid per class-4/class-1 distinction), IE-4 (≡ IS constructible relative to T, overstated as unconstructed), ON-1 (graph is acyclic once the Authority->Assertion edge is removed per implementation evidence), and G-31 (the Knowledge/Determination/Decision aggregate boundary IS fixed at s157/165/173, s173.5 calling their merge 'another dangerous merge').

a_rows_sample.anchor: |O_forced| = 14 ... forced-but-unnamed (new): ['Derive', 'Determine', 'Qualify'] ... |lower| = 14  |upper| = 18  |undetermined band| = 4
a_rows_sample.statement: Raw execution output validating oderive.py's reported 14-element forced lower bound, the finding that Derive/Determine/Qualify are forced-but-unnamed in the corpus's own registries, and the 14/18/4 lower/upper/undetermined-band split.

a_rows_sample.anchor: My independent/14-INDEPENDENT-VERDICT.md stated: 'Step 272 does not exist… the theory was interrupted.' That was true at 21:19 and is now false. The corpus contains # step 272 … whose body is STEP 273
a_rows_sample.statement: This session's own prior verdict ('Step 272 does not exist') is explicitly superseded: the corpus now contains a file headed '# step 272' whose body is actually Step 273 (Canonical Knowledge-State Sufficiency and Minimality), including a s273.31 'Important correction to Step 272' -- the research track had resumed and run ahead of every verification track.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An operation o is MANDATORY iff removing o makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law INEXPRESSIBLE ... This is a derivation, not a preference: the laws are corpus text, the forcing relation is entailment
a_rows_sample.statement: States and applies the derivation principle for operation mandatoriness: an operation is mandatory iff its removal makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law (e.g. 'Remove != Withdraw', 'Determination != Decision') inexpressible; encodes 26 such laws (with repetition-count weights as evidence weight, e.g. 'Expression != Meaning' at 71) and a table of which operation(s) each law forces, e.g. 'Determination != Decision' (weight 19) forces Determine, 'Observation != Evidence' (weight 20) forces Qualify.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Transform', 'Merge', 'Split' are named in 256.2 and forced by NO law. ... 'Qualify' and 'Determine' ARE forced ... but appear in NEITHER 256.2 NOR 259.7. The corpus's own enumeration MISSES two operations its own laws force.
a_rows_sample.statement: Result: Transform, Merge, Split and Reintroduce are named in the corpus's own registry (s256.2/s259.7) but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity is asserted, not entailed); conversely Qualify, Determine and Derive are forced by laws with weights 20/19/18 respectively but appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 -- so the laws under-determine O in one direction and the corpus's own enumeration over/under-determines it in the other, making set-membership not derivable from the laws alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FALSE AS STATED · TRUE IN SUBSTANCE · AND THE SUBSTANCE IS SHARPER THAN EITHER. ... So the missing premise is not the ENUMERATION. It is the NORMATIVE CLOSURE -- which of the candidates are mandatory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests and refines the claim 'O was never explicitly defined': FALSE as stated (s256.2 enumerates 9 ops in a boxed formula, s259.7 adds Validate/Assess/Promote/Reintroduce/Replay plus a five-class partition) but TRUE in substance (s256.2 itself calls its table 'a reconstruction target, not a claim that all nine are already formally defined', and s259.18 states the ∀T∈T-incompleteness problem as its own boxed negative result, so this was never an independent discovery by any verification track) -- the missing premise is normative closure (which candidates are mandatory), not enumeration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: non-collapse laws extracted (distinct) : 26 ... operations FORCED : 14 ... Two STRUCTURES are forced as a by-product, and neither is an operation: <D_t> ... <serialize>
a_rows_sample.statement: Derivation principle (o is mandatory iff removing it makes some corpus-stated non-collapse law inexpressible) applied to 26 distinct measured non-collapse laws: 14 operations forced (Authorize weight 45; Revise/Supersede 41; Promote 26; Qualify 20; Add 19; Determine 19; Derive 18; Replay 12; Assess/Validate 11; Remove/Withdraw/Reject weight 1 each), plus two non-operation structures forced as a by-product: <D_t> (recognised-dimension set, forced by UNKNOWN != ABSENT) and <serialize> (canonical form, forced by Expression != Meaning, the corpus's most-repeated law at 71 occurrences).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify, Determine, Derive are entailed by laws the corpus repeats 20, 19 and 18 times respectively -- and appear in neither §256.2 nor §259.7. ... Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce. The corpus never writes 'Merge != X', so nothing entails that Merge must exist.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two-sided mismatch between the derived forced set and the corpus's own named registry: Qualify, Determine, Derive are forced by frequently-repeated laws (20/19/18 occurrences) yet appear in NEITHER s256.2 nor s259.7 (a G5 promotion gap, not a G1 semantic gap); conversely Transform, Merge, Split, Reintroduce are named in the registry but forced by no non-collapse law (their necessity asserted, not entailed -- Transform's high usage, 8 of 9 kernel phases, is evidence of centrality, not mandatoriness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: |lower bound (forced)| = 14        |upper bound (named ∪ forced)| = 18 ... NOT derivable: which of the 4 band members are mandatory -- NORMATIVE -> D-1
a_rows_sample.statement: O is bounded but not determined: a 14-element lower bound and an 18-element upper bound are both derivable with no human input, along with the five-class partition and congruence rule (independently re-derivable since congruence is a property of an algebra's operations on its carrier, so an operation reading H is not an operation on K); only membership of the 4-operation undetermined band in the mandatory set is not derivable, because 'mandatory' is a normative predicate that no corpus of descriptions can entail -- this is D-1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The governing criterion is: F_i(H_1)=F_i(H_2) must imply F_i(\widehat T(H_1,c)) = F_i(\widehat T(H_2,c))
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate Knowledge-State abstraction F_i:H->K_i is sufficient for a mandatory transformation T over admissible context c iff F_i(H1)=F_i(H2) implies F_i(That(H1,c))=F_i(That(H2,c)); strengthened to require an actual state-level transformation T_i:K_i x C -> K_i such that F_i(That(H,c)) = T_i(F_i(H),c) for all admissible H,c (a commuting square between history-level and state-level transformations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: In particular: Definition of K != Adequacy of K, and: Congruence criterion valid != KnowledgeOS satisfies congruence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-correction of the immediately preceding step: a mathematical definition of K, a candidate representation of K, an abstraction F:H->K, and the claim that F is sufficient for the transformation family are four distinct claims that must not be conflated; Step 258 wrongly treated K as already a well-defined state abstraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not every operation has the form: T:K -> K. ... Assess:K x X -> Assessment ... Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Operations must first be classified into (1) knowledge-state transformations, (2) epistemic assessments, (3) governance operations, (4) audit/history operations, (5) observation operations; not every legitimate KnowledgeOS operation is an endomorphism T:K->K — e.g. Assess:K x X -> Assessment and Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision are non-state-closing operations, and only state-transforming operations enter the primary congruence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now introduce a revision rule dependent on lineage: Revise(x_1,x_2) is permitted only if: Origin(x_1) in ApprovedSources.
b_rows_sample.statement: Conditional counterexample sketch for candidate F_A (artifact-set state) under Revise: if revision eligibility depends on Origin(x1) (an approved-sources lineage rule) while F_A discards origin, two histories with equal F_A images can differ in whether a subsequent Revise is valid, which would falsify F_A's congruence — but this is CONDITIONAL, not PROVEN, unless the corpus actually establishes that revision eligibility depends on origin.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge is the strongest initial discriminator ... If the resulting provenance must distinguish Source_1 from Source_2, then F_A(\widehat{Merge}(H_A)) != F_A(\widehat{Merge}(H_B)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Conditional counterexample sketch for candidate F_A under Merge, described as the strongest initial discriminator among the tested operations: if two histories reach the same artifact x1 from different sources (Source_1 vs Source_2) with F_A(H_A)=F_A(H_B)={x1}, and a subsequent Merge(x1,x2) must record provenance distinguishing Source_1 from Source_2, then F_A fails congruence — again only if provenance is established as semantically observable by Merge, which the governing prompt requires testing (alongside evidence, replay, validation, implementation needs) before deciding whether Evidence/provenance belongs inside or outside K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: All transformations are K -> K | REFUTED as a universal assumption
b_rows_sample.statement: The results table explicitly marks the assumption that all KnowledgeOS transformations have signature K->K as REFUTED as a universal assumption (distinguished from the still-CANDIDATE status of F:H->K as a useful abstraction model, and from several UNRESOLVED items: whether history can be discarded, whether provenance must be inside or can remain outside K, whether the transformation family is closed, whether current K is globally sufficient, whether a minimal K exists).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot perform a valid global congruence proof until the mandatory transformation family is itself sufficiently closed. ... the quantifier forall T in T has no determinate meaning if T is incomplete.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central negative result of the step: a valid global congruence proof is impossible while the mandatory transformation family T is not itself closed, because the universal quantifier 'for all T in T' is not well-defined over an incomplete set; this reinforces the required sequencing Transformation Inventory -> Semantic Classification -> Congruence, rather than jumping to K -> Congruence in isolation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A finite test set can establish: Congruent_{tested}(F). It does not automatically establish: Congruent_{global}(F).
b_rows_sample.statement: Local/tested congruence (survival of a finite, executed test set) must be distinguished from global congruence (a formal proof over the fully specified domain and transformation family); an executed test yields only 'evidence of survival', never 'proof of universal congruence'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This also explains why Step 260 must come after Step 259. Minimality asks whether K* is the coarsest sufficient abstraction. But we cannot establish sufficiency until we know which operations must be preserved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequencing principle: no valid minimality proof (Step 260, testing whether K* = H/equiv is the coarsest sufficient state abstraction) can precede the operation registry and congruence-matrix analysis (Step 259), since minimality presupposes knowledge of which operations a sufficient state must preserve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A bounded context state is legitimate only if its externally observable behavior does not depend on information that the context has discarded. ... K1 equiv_K K2 must imply identical behavior under the context's published operations.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation of the congruence criterion: a bounded-context state representation is legitimate only when its externally observable behavior under the context's published operations does not depend on information the context's state has discarded — i.e. the congruence test is a rigorous check for an accidentally omitted domain invariant, not mathematical decoration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We must not assume: Statistical Sufficiency => KnowledgeOS Operational Sufficiency. That requires proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistical interpretation: two histories can produce the same estimated distribution P_theta under a distributional candidate state F_E, yet still be distinguishable by a future transformation dependent on information not identifiable from that distribution; statistical sufficiency must not be assumed to imply KnowledgeOS operational sufficiency without separate proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 259 establishes the formal mechanism by which candidate Knowledge-State abstractions can be falsified, but it does not yet establish that any candidate abstraction is globally sufficient. ... if the quotient does not exist in the required usable form, that is a valid research result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Conservative step verdict: the congruence-falsification mechanism is established but no candidate is proven globally sufficient; Step 260 is set up to test — not assume — existence, uniqueness, representability, computability, decidability, composability, equality, membership and identity of the candidate minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (H1 equiv H2 iff no mandatory operation can distinguish them), explicitly allowing a negative result (the quotient not existing in usable form) as a valid outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-sufficiency test F(H1) = F(H2) ⇒ F(T(H1,i)) = F(T(H2,i)) — executed, congruent for every input tested. See artifact F.
b_rows_sample.statement: The transformation-sufficiency (congruence) test F(H1)=F(H2) => F(T(H1,i))=F(T(H2,i)) was executed and found congruent for every tested input, with full detail deferred to a separate artifact F — direct empirical support for the K=(A,R) abstraction passing the Step-259 congruence criterion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The model is executable, so removal is testable. The phrase MINIMAL KERNEL is therefore earned — but only in the sense step 254 names: Minimality(K | 𝒯), relative to the transformation set. Not ontological necessity. A richer 𝒯 could force more.
b_rows_sample.statement: Minimality caveat: the removal-based necessity audit only earns Minimality(K|T) relative to the specific tested transformation set T (per step 254's framing), never ontological necessity of the components — a richer transformation set could force additional components to become necessary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F(Hx) = F(Hy) ? False — different states, so congruence is NOT tested by this pair ... A congruence test requires two DIFFERENT histories producing the SAME state. Two of my first three attempts were vacuous, and would have "passed" while proving nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-disclosed methodological failure: two of the first three attempted congruence-test constructions used history pairs that already produced different F-images, meaning congruence was never actually being tested (a vacuous pass); a valid congruence test requires two DIFFERENT histories that fold to the SAME state F(H1)=F(H2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hr = [assert A1, assert A4] ; Hs = [assert A4, assert A1] ... F(Hr) = F(Hs) = True ... i = relate(A1,A4,supersedes) -> congruent: True ... i = assert A2 -> congruent: True ... i = relate(A4,A1,refines) -> congruent: True ... b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Soundness (Sound(S)), Completeness (Complete(S,Q)), and Decidability (Decidable(S,Q)) as properties of the reasoning system S (a problem/procedure/formal-system property), not properties of Knowledge itself and not epistemic distinctions (Decidability != EpistemicStatus, distinct from Known(p) and Determined(p)); recommends filing them under 'Formal Representation and Reasoning' alongside an existing Complexity(S,Q) line of work rather than as universal epistemic distinctions in R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document identifies a weakness in its own preservation criterion: it does not account for context-sensitivity. This is correct. I would make the correction stronger. Instead of D_Q we should eventually have D_Q(Gamma) ... R_req may be a global baseline, while the actual required distinction set is: R_req(Q,Gamma). This is a major improvement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the source document's own context-sensitivity self-correction: replaces D_Q with D_Q(Gamma) where Gamma bundles context, scope, time, authority, task, and representation regime; correspondingly R_req becomes a global baseline while the actually-applicable set is R_req(Q,Gamma) -- described as a major theoretical improvement over a fixed universal set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I disagree with 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' ... A Tier-1 distinction d3 could be irrelevant to that question. Then R_1 may legitimately discard d3. So Tier(d) should influence governance priority, but should not automatically determine semantic preservation. The better rule is: Requiredness(Q,Gamma) > Tier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the rule 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' as too rigid: even a Tier-1 distinction may be legitimately discarded by a representation used only for a task whose D_Q does not require it. Proposes Tier should govern governance priority, not automatically determine semantic preservation, i.e. Requiredness(Q,Gamma) takes precedence over Tier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document says transformation invariance should preserve distinctions, but then recognizes that transformations may intentionally modify distinctions ... define a transformation's declared change set: Chg(T) subseteq R. Then: d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d. This is much better for KnowledgeOS because some operations are supposed to change state. Otherwise the preservation requirement makes state transition impossible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the transformation-invariance rule: instead of requiring T to preserve all of R_req, defines a declared change set Chg(T) subseteq R such that d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d; explicitly noting that an unconditional preservation requirement would make state transition impossible, since some operations are supposed to change state.

Instead: Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) asks what is not justified by the available representation within the declared inquiry boundary. Therefore Zero's required distinctions are: R_Zero(I,Gamma,L) not automatically all Tier-1 distinctions. This is a major correction.

The correct direction is something like: R_req(Q,Gamma) = minimal distinctions sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria. This makes R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a mathematical gap in the source document's minimality claim (a set claimed minimal 'relative to what?' -- as stated, an empty distinction set could trivially satisfy preservation/non-collapse/compositionality conditions); corrects the definition to R_req(Q,Gamma) = the minimal distinction set sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria, making R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Completeness of R_req' is itself a dangerous concept ... There may be no useful universal set D_all. There can always be another task requiring another distinction. So instead of asking 'Is R_req complete?' we should ask: Complete relative to which task/question/domain? ... Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma) could mean: no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req. That is a tractable governance question. 'Complete for all possible knowledge representation' is not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that asking whether R_req is 'complete' in an absolute sense is a dangerous, likely-unanswerable question (no useful universal distinction set D_all can be assumed to exist, since any new task can require a new distinction); replaces it with a tractable relativized governance question Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma): no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 47 distinctions should therefore NOT be frozen as universal ... Better: 47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope. ... We should preserve KnownSet(R) without claiming R=D.
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the source document's claim that its 47 distinctions form a comprehensive foundation, to '47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope', distinguishing the known distinction set KnownSet(R) from a claim that R equals the (unknowable) universal distinction set D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Historical proof objects ... HistoricalValidity != CurrentValidity. ... ProofStatus_t(pi) = Valid [may later become] Superseded or Invalidated. ... LocalRevision rather than GlobalRecomputation ... minimality is not an unconditional law. ... The reasoning engine must never treat a rule merely becaus
a_rows_sample.statement: 21.66-21.69: new evidence can invalidate premises/assumptions/rules/models/derivations/determinations within the cycle Evidence->Reasoning->Conclusion->Determination->Decision->Action->Observation->Revision, but proof objects are historical epistemic artifacts -- a previously valid proof can remain historically valid while its conclusion is no longer currently accepted (HistoricalValidity≠CurrentValidity); reasoning revision changes ProofStatus_t(pi)=Valid to Superseded or Invalidated at t+1 depending on contract, without deleting the old proof; minimal mutation prefers reconsidering only the dependency closure Affected(a) (LocalRevision over GlobalRecomputation), but this is not an unconditional law -- a global rule change may legitimately require broad recomputation, so minimality is itself contract- and dependency-dependent; rule and model governance must track identity/authority/version/provenance/effective-time/scope/approval-status/change-history (rules) and identity/version/training-lineage/validation-status/scope/limitations (models) -- a rule's mere existence in storage never makes it authorized.

b_rows_sample.statement: 21A.28 (new counterfactual): after release, discovery of a payment-ledger error retracts PaymentConfirmed(S) while the historical proof Proof_t1(pi_release)=Valid is not erased -- instead Status_current(pi_release)=Invalidated (or another contract-defined status), pi_release remains in History(K), and Determination_current(ReleasePermitted(S))=RequiresRevision, jointly demonstrating HistoricalValidity≠CurrentValidity and Revision≠Erasure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: true knowledge combines intelligence, instinct, intuition, wisdom, empathy, and an understanding that oneself and others participate in the Supreme Energy underlying the universe. ... Knowledge != information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the book's central claim that Vedic 'true knowledge' is not information from books or applied skills but a combination of intelligence, instinct, intuition, wisdom, empathy and understanding of universal participation -- stated as the single most important sentence for the reconstruction: Knowledge != information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Data -> Information -> Understanding -> Knowledge -> Wisdom -> Realization
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a six-level knowledge hierarchy from the source material (Data: something received; Information: organized representation e.g. a memorized sentence; Understanding: knowing what it means; Knowledge: understanding supported by inquiry and experience; Wisdom: knowing how to live according to it; Realization: directly knowing/being the truth), explicitly noting the book insists true knowledge is not merely information from books.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ask fundamental questions, withdraw from distractions, discipline themselves, concentrate, contemplate deeply, experience insight, test what they have discovered, share it with others. ... Knowledge changes the state of the knower.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the Upanishadic seeker does not merely acquire propositions but undergoes a transformation through an eight-step process (question, withdraw, discipline, concentrate, contemplate, experience insight, test, share), giving Knowledge = transformation produced by understanding reality, contrasted with the modern notion of knowledge as something stored in a database.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source -> Guru -> Student -> Memorization -> Multiple representations -> Cross-checking -> Recitation -> Next generation ... an ancient knowledge-integrity architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes the Vedic oral-transmission system as an ancient knowledge-integrity architecture: multiple recitation patterns (Patha) encode the same content through different sequences functioning as redundancy mechanisms for detecting corruption, explicitly analogized to a KnowledgeOS integrity concern; separates this from meaning, stating Problem A (integrity: was it preserved correctly), Problem B (meaning: do we understand it), and Problem C (realization: have we verified/transformed ourselves through it) as three distinct knowledge problems, with correct preservation alone insufficient for knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Faith without inquiry is insufficient. Inquiry without commitment is insufficient. Knowledge emerges from disciplined inquiry. ... shraddha ... willing to question, analyze and demand answers.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the Upanishadic student must not accept 'the teacher said it' as sufficient; using the Nachiketa narrative, defines shraddha as a form of faith willing to question, analyze and demand answers (not blind belief), yielding: faith without inquiry is insufficient, inquiry without commitment is insufficient, knowledge emerges from disciplined inquiry.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the Upanishads permit multiple interpretations, even contradictory ones, and "the debate is never over." ... A knowledge tradition can preserve a stable body of knowledge while allowing interpretation to remain open.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Upanishads permit multiple, even contradictory interpretations with debate never closed, extracting the principle that a knowledge tradition can keep a stable knowledge artifact while leaving its interpretation open, separating the knowledge artifact from its interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A document is a representation of knowledge. A database is a storage mechanism for representations. A validated model is structured knowledge. A capable engineer is embodied knowledge. ... When does knowledge actually exist?
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the KnowledgeOS view of knowledge lifecycle (captured->structured->governed->validated->preserved->transmitted->reused) with an additional dimension from the source: knowledge is not fully knowledge until it changes the capability/state of the knower, giving the graded distinction document-as-representation < database-as-storage < validated-model-as-structured-knowledge < capable-engineer-as-embodied-knowledge, and posing 'when does knowledge actually exist' with the answer 'when the knower has understood, verified, internalized, and can act from it', not when a document or database merely contains it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The book does not present a formal 'information theory' in the Shannon sense. ... Information is a representation of something that can be transmitted from one knower to another, but the representation is not identical with the knowledge itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly disclaims that the source presents formal Shannon-style information theory, instead extracting an implicit theory from its treatment of oral transmission: information is a transmissible representation, not identical with knowledge itself, illustrated by the Vedic sound-carrier being multi-dimensional (words+pronunciation+rhythm+tone+emphasis+sequence) rather than merely textual.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Make corruption detectable by introducing structured redundancy. ... multiple patterns of recitation ... CROSS-CHECK -> INTEGRITY.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analogizes the Vedic tradition's multiple recitation patterns (Patha) to error-detection/redundancy mechanisms in information systems, describing the pipeline Original -> multiple recitation Patterns A/B/C -> cross-check -> integrity as an information-preservation strategy distinct from, but structurally similar to, technical redundancy coding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Successful information transmission != successful knowledge transmission. ... INFORMATION TRANSMISSION: Sender -> Signal -> Receiver. KNOWLEDGE TRANSMISSION: Teacher -> Signal -> Student -> Interpretation -> Understanding -> Experience -> Realization.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central distinction that a message can be perfectly transmitted (heard and repeated) without producing knowledge, splitting Information Transmission (Sender->Signal->Receiver) from Knowledge Transmission (Teacher->Signal->Student->Interpretation->Understanding->Experience->Realization), called foundational for KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SIGNAL: Syntax (word/order/sound/rhythm/tone/sequence), Semantics (what the signal means), Pragmatics (what the receiver does with the meaning). ... MESSAGE + CONTEXT + KNOWER = INTERPRETATION.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes a transmitted signal into syntax, semantics and pragmatics layers, and states information is inherently contextual (Message + Context + Knower = Interpretation), illustrated by the Upanishads' use of stories, analogies, metaphors, dialogues and questions to convey meaning that could not be reconstructed from the words alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Around 700 BCE, rituals had become elaborate and were often performed simply because they were traditional, with few people understanding their significance. ... PROCEDURE PRESERVED != PURPOSE UNDERSTOOD. ... Artifact integrity != Semantic integrity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses the historical example of ritual practice persisting after its original meaning was lost (c. 700 BCE) as a concrete demonstration that a procedure can be perfectly preserved while its purpose is not understood, extracting the distinction artifact/representation integrity != semantic integrity, and proposing a third dimension, intent integrity (why it was said), alongside them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information quality depends not only on the message but also on the receiver. WORLD -> SENSES -> PERCEPTION -> MIND -> INTERPRETATION -> UNDERSTANDING. Each stage can introduce distortion.
b_rows_sample.statement: States information quality depends on the receiver as much as the message, modelling a World->Senses->Perception->Mind->Interpretation->Understanding chain where each stage can introduce distortion, citing the source's observation that senses and mind are not automatically reliable and personal bias influences interpretation -- explicitly noted as a departure from purely technical (receiver-agnostic) information theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information is a detectable difference that can alter the state of a receiver.
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes information beyond language, citing the source's account of understanding another's emotions/intentions without words, to a broader definition: 'information is a detectable difference that can alter the state of a receiver', spanning linguistic, visual, auditory, behavioral, emotional, contextual and experiential carriers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information is a structured representation or signal carrying distinctions, meaning, or experience from a source to a receiver through a transmission channel... Information becomes knowledge only when the receiver successfully integrates the information into understanding and can validate or experie
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a formal extracted definition of information (structured representation/signal carrying distinctions/meaning/experience via a channel, with integrity depending on encoding/preservation/transmission and usefulness depending on receiver decoding/contextualizing/interpreting) and its transition to knowledge (successful integration into understanding, with validation or experience of significance).

b_rows_sample.anchor: INFORMATION: representation, encoding, signal, storage, transmission, integrity. -> KNOWLEDGE: meaning, context, understanding, validation, experience, reasoning. -> WISDOM: judgment, action, transformation, capability, realization.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assembles a three-layer architecture (Information: representation/encoding/signal/storage/transmission/integrity; Knowledge: meaning/context/understanding/validation/experience/reasoning; Wisdom: judgment/action/transformation/capability/realization) and closes with four foundational principles: preserving information != preserving knowledge; preserving representation != preserving meaning; transmitting meaning != producing understanding; knowledge exists only when information has transformed the capability of the knower.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'vedic-implicit-information-theory-transmission-integrity' POSSIBLY relates to 'roopa-pai-vedas-upanishads-knowledge-hierarchy' (batch B0056). Note: Extracts an implicit (non-Shannon) theory of information from the same Roopa Pai Vedas/Upanishads source's treatment of oral transmission, distinct from that file's knowledge-hierarchy extraction. Central claim: information is a representation transmissible between knowers but not identical with knowledge. Models the Vedic sound-based information carrier as multi-dimensional (words+pronunciation+rhythm+tone+emphasis+sequence, with Sama Veda melody notation as an encoding example), subject to transmission degradation (loss/distortion/addition/reinterpretation), for which the tradition's redundant multi-pattern recitation functioned as an error-detection/integrity mechanism (Original->multiple recitation Patterns A/B/C->cross-check->integrity). Enumerates five information channels (oral, musical, written, demonstrative, dialogical) noting the Upanishadic teacher-student form is INTERACTIVE (question-driven), not one-way broadcast. States the central distinction 'successful information transmission != successful knowledge transmission', splitting Information Transmission (Sender->Signal->Receiver) from Knowledge Transmission (Teacher->Signal->Student->Interpretation->Understanding->Experience->Realization). Adds a syntax/semantics/pragmatics decomposition of a signal, and states information is inherently contextual (Message+Context+Knower=Interpretation). Uses the historical example of ritual practice persisting after its meaning was lost (~700 BCE) as a concrete case of 'procedure preserved != purpose understood' (artifact integrity != semantic integrity), motivating a three-part integrity requirement: representation integrity (was what was said preserved), semantic integrity (was what it meant preserved), and intent integrity (was why it was said preserved). States information quality depends on the receiver, not just the message (World->Senses->Perception->Mind->Interpretation->Understanding, each stage introducing possible distortion), and that information is broader than language (linguistic/visual/auditory/behavioral/emotional/contextual/experiential), reformulated generally as 'information is a detectable difference that can alter the state of a receiver.' Concludes with a formal extracted definition ('information is a structured representation...carrying distinctions, meaning, or experience from a source to a receiver through a transmission channel; information becomes knowledge only when the receiver successfully integrates it into understanding') and a three-layer architecture (Information: representation/encoding/signal/storage/transmission/integrity -> Knowledge: meaning/context/understanding/validation/experience/reasoning -> Wisdom: judgment/action/transformation/capability/realization), plus four preserved principles: preserving information != preserving knowledge; preserving representation != preserving meaning; transmitting meaning != producing understanding; knowledge exists only when information has transformed the knower's capability.

Different questions can legitimately produce the same determination ... Therefore the correct statement is: Q1!=Q2 does NOT imply Det(E,Q1,Gamma)!=Det(E,Q2,Gamma). What you actually demonstrated is: there exist Q1,Q2 such that Det(E,Q1,Gamma)!=Det(E,Q2,Gamma). That is much weaker -- and correct.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a logical over-generalization in the Non-Collapsing Axiom: the universal claim 'Q1!=Q2 implies different Determinations' is false in general, since different questions can legitimately produce the same determination (e.g. two distinct queries both yielding DeterminedPositive); the axiom must be weakened to the existential claim actually demonstrated -- there EXIST Q1,Q2 for which the determinations differ -- not a universal implication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The biggest DDD problem: Actionability is leaking into Determination ... If Actionability is already inside Determination, then the determination object is starting to encode downstream governance/decision semantics. For example: PERMITTED is not merely an epistemic determination. It is a governance/authorization consequence. Therefore I recommend: Determination = <Status,Basis,Scope,Uncertainty,Provenance> ... Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a DDD layering violation: Determination's Actionability field (PERMITTED/REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW/BLOCKED) is a governance/authorization consequence, not an epistemic determination, and its presence inside Determination collapses the intended chain Evaluation->Determination->Decision->Authorization->Action; recommends a purely epistemic Determination=<Status,Basis,Scope,Uncertainty,Provenance>, with Actionability moved downstream into Decision/Authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1: Generative Expansion (Yoni Engine G): G(K_t,Q,Gamma) = {o_1,...,o_m} where o_i in {ASSERT,LINK,REVISE} ... Phase 2: State Mutation Transition (delta): K_temp = delta(K_t, o_m o ... o o_1, Gamma) ... b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the refactored four-phase epistemic cycle: Generative Expansion G produces a batch of candidate O_core operations; State Mutation delta executes them monotonically; Boundary Examination Z runs EVal over every active node and applies ISOLATE wherever the structural conflict predicate Phi_conflict holds; the Determination Bridge Det then maps the post-isolation evaluation set to a boundary/gap profile B_{t+1}. The whole cycle is the function composition Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma).
